title: Bills, Budda Baker Trade Rumors Give Buffalo Small Opening for Deal With Cardinals
full_text:
We are just one day away from the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10 and the Buffalo Bills continue to be linked to interest in a safety.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the "Bills have scanned the safety pool of late," something that has been reported by more than one NFL insider over the past week.
However, Fowler also added in an interesting nugget on Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker, who he says might be open to leaving the Cardinals to join a contender.
The caveat, Fowler says, is the Cardinals' willingness to actually trade him.
"My sense is Budda Baker would welcome chance to play for contender if AZ entertains talks (big if)," Fowler reported.
The Cardinals are currently in the midst of a rebuild and their timeline just doesn't match up with Baker's.
After all, he'll be 31 in January and there's a good chance Baker will already be on the decline by the time the Cardinals are competitive again, if they even get to that point.
It makes all the sense in the world to trade Baker now, as his value may never be higher than it is currently. Not only is Baker still a top safety in the NFL, but he also has one more year left on his contract, which helps his stock further.
The Cardinals may not want to trade Baker because he is pretty much a franchise great at this point, but if the veteran tells Arizona he wants to be moved to have a chance to compete, we could definitely see the Cardinals obliging out of respect.
Baker is OK in coverage, but he is one of the very best box safeties in the NFL. The eight-time Pro Bowler and four-time All-Pro is not only a very good run defender, he is also an elite pass-rusher when asked to blitz.
The Bills are currently lacking a starting-caliber safety next to Cole Bishop. Buffalo recently cut C.J. Gardner-Johnson and that leaves the team depending on Damar Hamlin, who we know is best suited as a backup, and Jalon Kilgore, who the jury is still out on.
Baker would shore up Buffalo's need in one fell swoop while also adding more toughness and veteran leadership to a defense that needs all the help it can get.
We might have a measuring stick for what a Baker trade will look like.
On Monday morning, the Jacksonville Jaguars pulled off a trade for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates, with the Jags giving up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. To get the deal done, the Falcons picked up most of his $6.5 million of salary .
That last part is especially important to note for the Bills, as they only have $3.9 million in cap space and will need more to fit in what's left of Baker's $14.4 million base salary.
Or, the Bills could look to have the Cardinals eat some or all of that, in which case it will cost more in draft capital to acquire Baker.
If the Bills take that route, we suspect they'll end up paying what the Jaguars did, or at least something close to that. If the Bills take on all of Baker's salary, we're probably looking at a third or fourth, and then a late Day 3 pick, also.
As for the Bills' available trade capital and cap situation , we wrote about how a potential deal would be affected, and there's clear path forward for general manager Brandon Beane.
Not only does Beane have the picks to get any of those deals done, he certainly has the motivation with the Bills being among the true Super Bowl contenders in the NFL this season.
But just because it makes sense doesn't mean the Bills are going to do it. We'll know for sure by Tuesday.

title: Monday Night Football Injury Status for Bills' DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid, Keon Coleman
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills could be without the starting left side of their offensive line when they visit the Minnesota Vikings for Monday Night Football, but there is plenty of good news elsewhere on offense.
Set to go against the NFL's No. 2 defense , Bills' quarterback Josh Allen will have a relatively healthy arsenal at his disposal in Week 9.
Wide receiver DJ Moore, tight end Dalton Kincaid and wide receiver Keon Coleman all began the practice week wearing red non-contact jerseys coming out of the November 1 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
There were no missed practices by any of the three pass-catchers this past week, and all three have been cleared for the November 9 primetime matchup in Minnesota. They'll take on the top-ranked defense against the pass.
Buffalo, however, will be without one of its wide receivers. Josh Palmer pulled up lame while running a route in the first quarter against Baltimore. Although the severity of his hamstring injury is unknown, Palmer appears to be in jeopardy of missing multiple weeks.
Meanwhile, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson are officially questionable for the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff .
Moore appears to finally be in the clear when it comes to the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 2.
After missing back-to-back games heading into the Week 7 bye, Moore returned to the starting lineup in Week 8 against the Ravens. Officially listed as questionable for the game , Moore proceeded to make four receptions for 82 yards and one touchdown in the 36-10 win.
Moore appears to have avoided any potential knee issue from the November 1 win. Following his final catch of the game midway through the fourth quarter, Moore was slow to get up. He went into the blue evaluation tent where he was cleared .
This week marks the first time that Moore does not carry a questionable tag heading into a game since Week 2.
Kincaid experienced discomfort while running a third-quarter red zone route against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18.
He went to the locker room for evaluation, and was subsequently cleared to return. Three snaps after returning to action, Kincaid made a 14-yard fourth-quarter reception.
Still, the Bills were cautious with Kincaid coming out of the bye. He was limited all week leading up to the Ravens game, and he carried a questionable tag before playing 57 percent of snaps. The tight end made four catches for 86 yards and one touchdown.
Kincaid progressed to full strength in Week 9. He was a limited participant on Thursday before increasing to full participation on Friday and Saturday. He also ditched the red non-contact jersey.
Coleman was a new addition to the injury report in Week 9 after appearing to make it out of the November 1 win intact. He had been dealing with an ankle issue earlier in the season, this trip to the injury report comes as a result of a shoulder problem.
The Bills listed Coleman as a limited participant for all three practices this week. The wide receiver was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey during the media-viewing portions, but he'll be available for Monday Night Football.
Leading all skill position players in offensive snaps (63), Coleman, who entered with a three-game touchdown streak, was relatively quiet against the Ravens. He made only one four-yard catch, but there was one play where he ran open deep down the middle of the field only for Allen to overthrow him on what would have been a touchdown.

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Minnesota Vikings Week 9 Expert Pick Roundup
full_text:
This Monday night presents a huge opportunity for the Buffalo Bills as their No. 1 ranked offense will take on the Minnesota Vikings , who boast the No. 1 ranked defense in the NFL.
It's a battle of strength vs. strenght, and Josh Allen says he welcomes the opportunity for the Bills to prove themselves against the best. They will also have plenty of eyes on them during the showdown, with the two teams squaring off on Monday Night Football.
There's some intrigue with Kyler Murray being out this week , meaning the Bills will take on backup Carson Wentz. Buffalo can't go into this one thinking it will be easy, however, since Wentz is one of the more experienced backups in the NFL and is more than capable of moving the ball on offense.
That said, the Bills are the favorites in this one as many experts see them walking out of Minnesota with a victory. That can be seen in our following Week 9 expert pick roundup.
The experts are in strong agreement, with Buffalo standing out as the overwhelming favorite in this one. While the loss of Murray might have swayed some of those opinions, it's more likely a belief that the Bills' offense will find success against Minnesota's powerful defense thanks to Josh Allen.
Allen is a former NFL MVP for a reason, and this can be a statement game for him. Of course, it could also be a huge opportunity for defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. His unit played well in their Week 8 win over the Ravens, shutting down their backup quarterbacks. If they can do the same to Wentz and Justin Jefferson, that would be a major confidence builder for a defense that needs to start finding success.
That's exactly what I expect to happen in this one. It might be slow going at first, but eventually, Allen and the offense will hit its stride while the defense has success once again.

title: Bills' Trade Capital, Salary Cap Situation Heading Toward Tuesday's NFL Deadline
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are presumably looking to reinforce their defensive secondary on the trade market, but will general manager Brandon Beane strike a deal prior to Tuesday's deadline?
The Bills, who are surrendering nearly 26.0 points per game, rank 30th overall in pass defense (254.7).
In particular, the Bills seem most likely to trade for a proven safety if they're to make any type of move.
One can make the case for adding a cornerback being that Buffalo has only three true outside corners on its 53-man roster, but the recent practice squad additions of former NFL starters Tre'Davious White and Kader Kohou are adequate insurance policies.
With the Bills already cutting bait on the Chauncey Gardner-Johnson experience, veteran Damar Hamlin has been forced into a starting safety role while practice squad veteran Geno Stone brings more starting experience.
Although Buffalo can likely get by with Hamlin or Stone, Beane may look to make a true splash by bringing in an Amani Hooker or Jessie Bates type.
The Bills have the necessary draft capital to swing a trade for a Pro Bowler, but they would need to exercise some creative salary cap gymnastics in order to stay compliant.
Earlier this week, we wrote about potential roadblocks facing Buffalo prior to the 4 p.m. ET deadline on November 10.
Spotrac estimates the Bills are holding approximately $3.8 million in salary cap space. They are eating $2.3 million in dead money from cutting Gardner-Johnson.
While their cap space ranks 27th overall , the Bills can still swing a deal if the trade partner is willing to absorb a larger portion of the player's salary for the remainder of the season. Buffalo could entice a team to do this by offering a better draft pick in a trade.
For example, Tennessee Titans' safety Amani Hooker counts $11.9 million against the cap. With the season halfway over, his number is down to under $6 million. If Tennessee is willing to pay $3 million of his remaining cap hit, then the Bills could swing the deal.
The Bills have a presence in all seven rounds at the 2027 NFL Draft. They currently have eight total picks, but are expected to add a ninth selection in the form of a fourth-round compensatory pick to be determined in the offseason.
Buffalo has its own selections in Rounds 1 through 6. It also has the Colts' sixth-rounder and the Raiders' seventh-rounder.

title: Five Key Things to Know About Bills vs. Vikings in Week 9
full_text:
It has all the makings of one of those classic “the irresistible force meets an immovable object” matchup.
No team in the league is averaging more points per game than the Buffalo Bills. No club in the NFL is allowing fewer points per game than the Minnesota Vikings.
Both clubs own 6-1 win-loss records and each are at the top of their respective divisions.
Bills’ quarterback Josh Allen continues to be one of the most productive players at his position. On the other hand, Vikings’ head coach Kevin O’Connell has turned back to Carson Wentz for this interconference clash as Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury.
As for the Bills, their injury report features two starting offensive linemen.
While Joe Brady’s team is riding a three-game winning streak for the second time this season, the NFC North frontrunners are coming off their first setback of 2026 in the form of a 19-15 loss at Detroit. I t will be interesting to see how O’Connell’s team performs after its initial loss of the season.
Vikings vs Bills Week 10, 2022. pic.twitter.com/CKiukQhqFW
This interconference series dates back to 1971, and the Purple Gang owns a three-game edge (9-6) in the standings. The last time these teams met, they put on quite a show at Orchard Park as the Vikings came up with a wild 33-30 overtime victory back in 2022. The teams combined for 967 yards of total offense in four-plus quarters.
As for the Bills’ last appearance in Minneapolis, the team came away with a 27-6 victory in Week 3 of 2018. It was just Josh Allen’s second NFL start and wound up being he and the team’s first victory of the season.
🏈🔥 Josh Allen put on a SHOW against the Ravens today! 🤯🦬 🎯 289 PASSING YARDS 🏈 2 PASSING TOUCHDOWNS 🏃 30 RUSHING YARDS 💪 1 RUSHING TOUCHDOWN 📈 26.56 FANTASY POINTS 3 TOTAL TDS. 319 TOTAL YARDS. 36–10 BLOWOUT WIN! 🔥 JOSH ALLEN AND THE BILLS ARE ROLLING! 😤🦬 pic.twitter.com/kCuv35Pr84
Joe Brady’s team has totaled an impressive 233 points (33.3 average) in seven games. The Bills have scored 84 points in the second quarter and a combined 80 points in the fourth quarter and overtime. Led by Brian Flores’s imposing defensive unit, the Vikings have surrendered just 93 points in seven games.
Buffalo’s offensive unit has reached the end zone 27 times this season, led by quarterback Josh Allen (9) and running back James Cook (7), who have combined for more than half (16) of those touchdowns. On the other hand, Minnesota has given up just eight offensive TDs (4 rushing, 4 passing) in seven contests.
Coordinator Jim Leonhard’s defense has surrendered 22 offensive touchdowns in seven games, two-third of those (15) through the air. The Bills have given up two or more scores through the air in five of those seven contests. Last week, Buffalo defenders did not allow a TD pass in the 36-10 win over the Ravens.
Third-year edge rusher Dallas Turner got off to a fast start for the NFC North leaders this season. In his first four games, he racked up 5.5 sacks and a pair of forced fumbles. These days, Andrew Van Ginkel now leads the Vikings with six QB traps. He totaled a season-high 2.5 sacks in last Sunday’s loss at Detroit.

title: Are Bills, NFL MVP Favorite Josh Allen Playing Sunday? When Is Their Next Game?
full_text:

As a result, it'll be an stress-free Sunday for Bills' fans, who can spend their time afternoon rooting against the Kansas City Chiefs in a 1 p.m. ET kickoff and against the New England Patriots in the 4 p.m. window. title: Believing Josh Allen-led Bills Will Easily Dismantle Vikings on Monday Night Football
full_text:
The upcoming matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings should provide plenty of fireworks on Monday Night Football at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis.
According to most metrics , the matchup will feature the NFL’s top defensive unit in Minnesota, and the league’s top offensive attack—at least in terms of scoring—from the Bills.
And, despite some question marks at the quarterback position for Vikings’ head coach Kevin O’Connell’s home squad, the scoreboard should be fairly tight under the primetime lights . . . even if Buffalo did just hold Baltimore to only 10 points in Week 8.
In order to come out on top, the Bills and former 2024 MVP quarterback Josh Allen will still need to put forth a good offensive display on the road on Monday evening.
But, that’ll probably be easier said than done.
So far this fall, no matter what team the Vikings have faced, defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ unit has stymied every opponent, regardless of who the quarterback was.
Even in its first loss last Sunday at Ford Field, Minnesota’s defense allowed just 19 points to a Detroit Lions’ offense that is averaging 29 points per game behind veteran gunslinger Jared Goff, which places them third in the NFL behind only Cincinnati ( 29.4 PPG ) and Buffalo ( 33.3 PPG ) through seven games.
For that reason, even if the Bills do come out victorious, one might expect it to still be a low-scoring affair in the Upper Midwest to finish off Week 9 . . . right?
@DannyParkins predicts Josh Allen will TORCH the Vikings defense 👀 "I think he will have the best game that anyone has had against Minnesota this year, by a comfortable margin." pic.twitter.com/mL4cTg2K8L
Well, according to analyst Danny Parkins, that’s not the case. In his opinion, Allen and Co. will cruise to victory on Monday night despite the Vikings currently allowing a meager 271.6 total yards per game to opposing offenses, along with just nine total touchdowns and only 13.3 points per game.
“I think [Josh Allen] will have the best game that anyone has had against Minnesota this year by a comfortable margin. And, I expect [Buffalo] to win,” Danny Parkins said during an appearance on FS1 ’s First Things First on Friday .
“I think the Vikings’ defense is obviously very, very good. They’ll be playing at home, (so) that crowd noise will help, (but) Josh is spectacular against the blitz (with) his mobility, getting the ball out fast, their offensive line’s great, (and) all those things. It’s a great Xs and Os football matchup.
“I think the Vikings—last week—almost got exposed in that game against Detroit. . . . I think Josh Allen will have close to 300 yards, multiple touchdowns, and win this game in Minnesota.”
Given that Minnesota has allowed opposing quarterbacks—which includes players like Green Bay’s Jordan Love, Chicago’s Caleb Williams, and the aforementioned Goff—to only gain 182.7 total yards per game, four total touchdowns, and nine turnovers through seven outings, Allen going anywhere over the 250-yard mark would seemingly be a feat in and of itself.
Allen recently reflected on his last game in Minneapolis that occurred eight years ago during his rookie season, which famously included his hurdle of linebacker Anthony Barr during a 1:00 p.m. ET time slot on Sunday, September 23, 2018.
Buffalo was a 16.5-point underdog entering that contest all those years ago in Allen’s first career road start, but the team wound up defeating the Vikings 27-6 in huge upset fashion.
And, if all goes according to what Parkins sees happening, then Bills Mafia might be celebrating a similar outcome in the coming days.
Kickoff for this iteration of the enticing interconference matchup between the NFC North and AFC East squads is slated for 8:15 p.m. ET on Monday.

title: Slumping Panthers Still Atop an NFC South in Total Disarray
full_text:
A season ago, the NFC South was won by a team that lost more games than it won. That would be the Carolina Panthers, who captured its first division title since 2015 with an 8-9 win-loss record. Of course, that was also the case back in 2022, when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finished 2022 also managed an 8-9 mark and walked away with the top spot in the division.
Speaking of the Panthers, they are currently tied for the best record in the NFC South with the 3-5 New Orleans Saints. Dave Canales's team currently has the tie-breaking edge due to the fact that they have split a pair of divisional games. On the other hand, Kellen Moore’s club was blasted at home by the Atlanta Falcons, 45-24, on a Monday night in Week 4 in the club’s lone clash with an NFC South rival this season.
That changes this week when the Saints host the Panthers on Sunday afternoon for the first of their two meetings. A year ago, Moore’s team finished 6-11 and in the division basement (the 3 other clubs all posted 8-9 records), but they managed to sweep Carolina. And given the way things have gone for each of the four clubs at home this season, it’s anyone’s guess what will happen at the Superdome.
Not only is every team in this division at least two games under .500, the four clubs all own sub-.500 marks at home. Now keep in mind that the Saints and Falcons have “home” losses to the Steelers and Bengals in Paris and Madrid, respectively. Take those setbacks out and Carolina (1-3), New Orleans (1-3), Tampa Bay (1-4), and Atlanta (1-3) are a combined 4-13 in their own buildings this season.
As for Canales’s club, it is currently in the midst of a three-game skid, the latest loss a 26-21 home setback to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. The slide began back in Week 7 at Bank of America Stadium, when the Bucs opened up a 33-6 halftime advantage on the way to a 43-13 victory. That was followed by a Thursday night loss at Lambeau Field and yesterday’s loss to Sean Payton’s surging club.
The Panthers OL finally gave Bryce Young time to breathe and he rewarded them with a strong performance against the Broncos defense pic.twitter.com/GCGbIlw1cw
Ultimately, it may be the Saints who decide who wins this division due to the fact that they will face NFC South rivals in four of their final five games.
Here are the latest NFL Power Rankings via Vinny Iyer of The Sporting News , and it certainly speaks volumes when it comes to this quartet. He has the Buccaneers as the division’s top team, but at No. 21. They are followed by the Falcons at No. 22, the Saints at No. 23 and the slumping Panthers at No. 25.
Is it a foregone conclusion that the NFC South will have a champion with a losing record for the third time in five years? And is it possible we could see this division by a team with 10 losses?

title: Reports of Bryce Young's Demise Were Greatly Exaggerated
full_text:
Bryce Young, quarterback for the Carolina Panthers, did have a good game against the Denver Broncos, but the Panthers lost the game. This season, Bryce Young has received a lot of criticism, some of it justified, but some of it not. There have been several games where the Panthers' offense has struggled to get anything going, and many fans are questioning whether or not Bryce Young is the Panthers' long-term answer at quarterback.
While the offense struggled in some of the Panthers' games this season, there were also games where the offense was clicking and Young looked like a good quarterback in the NFL.
It's easy to blame the quarterback for a loss when the offense isn't scoring enough points. For much of the season, fans and media have been wondering if the Panthers should be looking for a new quarterback.
The game against the Broncos was not enough to clear up all the questions that people have about Young, but it sure did give people something else to talk about.
While one game cannot be proof of anything, it can be the starting point to show that Young is capable of being a good quarterback in the NFL.
Young did his part to keep Carolina in the game. The Panthers didn't come away with a win, but the offense gave them a chance, and Young deserves some credit for that.
Carolina's offense has had some struggles this season, with Young holding onto the football too long and missing out on some opportunities to get the ball out quicker. These are certainly things that need to be addressed, but they shouldn't be the only things that people remember from his season.
Some of the talk about Bryce Young has made it seem like the Panthers are ready to move on from the young quarterback. After watching him against the Broncos, that doesn't appear to be the case.
While Bryce Young can receive much of the criticism for the Carolina Panthers' losses, t here are many other problems with the team that the Panthers must address.
The Panthers are going to have to get better at several things, and that includes Bryce Young. While he has some things that he can work on, the Panthers' offense needs to get better around him as well.
Even though Carolina lost to Denver on Sunday, Bryce Young gave the Panthers a chance to win the game.
Carolina may have another loss on its record, but Young gave his critics a reason to reconsider how quickly they've written him off. He still has plenty to prove, and Sunday's performance showed why that opportunity shouldn't be taken away just yet.

title: 3 Major Takeaways From Panthers' Frustrating Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had opportunities to take down the Denver Broncos on Sunday, but the team fell short and lost to the Broncos, 26-21. After taking a 14-13 lead in the third quarter, the Panthers were unable to hold on and lost for the third straight game.
While the Panthers had several good moments, particularly on offense, errors in the game cost the team the victory. Once again, Carolina found itself in a position to win but couldn't finish the job.
Three things we learned from the Panthers' loss to Denver on Sunday.
Carolina had 13 penalties for 119 yards on Sunday. The Panthers gave up a lot of yards to the Broncos in the game, many of which came on penalties that allowed Denver to keep drives going.
There will always be some penalties in a game, but the Panthers had too many on Sunday. A number of the penalties were for pass interference, and some of those resulted in Denver gaining extra yardage on drives that otherwise would have ended.
The frustrating thing is that the Panthers were competitive for the majority of the game, and they didn't have to play a perfect game to win. But giving the Broncos free yards is not the way to win.
Dave Canales and his coaching staff have to get these penalties under control before they cost Carolina another game.
The Carolina Panthers quarterback, Bryce Young, had some really good plays on Sunday. He had three touchdown passes on the day, gave Carolina the lead in the third quarter and kept the Panthers in the game until the final minutes.
The Panthers have also had problems protecting Young throughout the season , making his performance against Denver an encouraging sign.
One of Carolina's scoring opportunities ended with a strange interception. Young threw to Tommy Tremble in the end zone, and the ball was deflected before ending up in the hands of Devon Key of the Denver Broncos.
Officials initially ruled the pass incomplete, but Denver challenged the call. After reviewing the play, officials determined that the ball had hit Tremble's foot rather than the ground before Key secured it, giving Denver the interception.
This took away another opportunity for the Carolina Panthers to extend their lead in the game. The ball wasn't caught by the receiver, and that was out of Young's hands.
Young had a solid game for the Panthers, throwing three touchdown passes. He gave the team opportunities to win, but the rest of the players on the field must take advantage of those opportunities.
The secondary was once again giving up too much space to opposing receivers, especially in the first half of the game. Bo Nix was able to find many of his receivers on short completions and drive the Broncos down the field.
As Panthers On SI discussed in its halftime breakdown, Carolina's defensive backs were giving Denver's receivers too much room to operate.
While the defense held Denver to a field goal prior to halftime, the secondary allowed too much space for the opposing team's receivers and gave up too many opportunities.
The Panthers also had a number of pass interference penalties on the defensive backs. Those penalties made it even harder for the defense to get off the field.
To be a competitive team in the NFL, the defensive backs of the Carolina Panthers need to challenge receivers and not give up easy completions to the opposing quarterback.
Even with the problems, the Panthers showed that they can compete with the Broncos. But too many mistakes are keeping Carolina from winning games.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Carolina Panthers Falter in NFL Power Rankings After Tough Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers looked for a moment like they were going to inexplicably right the ship. They had the Denver Broncos on the ropes, first-and-goal from the one with a seemingly inevitable eight-point lead coming in mere seconds.
A missed defensive pass interference on the first attempt is one thing , but letting the Panthers run a whole play before going back to grant a challenge is another. After it was overturned to an interception, the Panthers fell behind by 12 points, and their comeback attempt was thwarted by a sack-fumble.
For a moment, it felt like the Panthers might actually surge up the NFL Power Rankings this week, as they did after a shocking home win over the Detroit Lions. That is their second-most recent win, and it also feels like it was six months ago.
Now, the Panthers are 3-5 and in a freefall, no longer in first in the NFC South and tumbling down the power rankings.
The Panthers have been slipping and sliding in the Power Rankings for a few weeks now. After they beat the Philadelphia Eagles, they breached the top 10 on some lists. And at the time, it didn't feel ridiculous.
Since then, the entire season has turned on its head. A shocking and embarrassing home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers started things in the wrong direction. That led to a frustrating one-score loss to the Green Bay Packers, which led to (checks notes) a frustrating one-score loss to the Denver Broncos.
Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer had the Panthers ranked 22nd last week , and now they're 25th. We firmly believe this team is better than that and better than 3-5, but the record is what it is. Injuries have played a role, but there's no caveat in the rankings.
"The Panthers' big defensive issue, with or without now-fired former defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, has been staying on the field too much after third down. Opponents have converted around 54 percent against them. The Broncos were 6-for-10, even when held to 82 rushing yards by a horrible run defense," Iyer wrote.
Next up is the New Orleans Saints. They've been a thorn in Carolina's side, but this is a winnable game. The Saints are, however, riding high after a clutch overtime win over the Cleveland Browns, a team that beat the Panthers this year.
Regardless, that's their next chance to right the ship and get moving in the right direction on the power rankings.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: The NFL’s Explanation of Broncos’ Challenge vs. Panthers Holds No Water
full_text:
We've all seen the play and the ridiculous circus that took place after, which turned into a Carolina Panthers turnover in the end zone. To summarize, Tommy Tremble appeared to be interfered with, and the ball bounced up off his hand and into the hands of Denver Broncos' DB Devon Key.
The Panthers then ran a whole play and got stuffed at the goal-line before referees appeared to retroactively grant a Sean Payton challenge. The tipped ball was correctly ruled an interception on the replay, so it was a touchback for the Broncos.
The Broncos went down and took a lead they wouldn't relinquish after that play. On a pretty dismal day by the referees, that mistake loomed large. Surely, the explanation after the game will help us all make sense of the unprecedented turn of events?
Pool reporter @alexzietlow05 spoke with referee Alan Eck and VP of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth after the game: pic.twitter.com/M2oETnPMXf
Not so. Charlotte Observer reporter Alex Zietlow asked the referees about the replay gaffe, and their explanation doesn't make any sense.
Head referee Alan Eck said, "Replay can get involved to make sure that the head coach throws his challenge flag prior to the next snap. We were actually able to use angles to show that the flag was out before the snap, and so we permitted the challenge."
That doesn't hold water, though. In the past, if the referees did not see the challenge flag come out and the play commenced, it's dead in the water. It's an unfortunate and rather silly aspect of the challenge process, but it's been this way forever.
If you don't get the ref to see what you want to do before the ball is snapped, then you're just out of luck. Unless you're Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos, it seems.
And it's not as if the referees blew the play dead because of the challenge. The play was blown dead because it had ended. The play had entirely taken place, and the referees decided to retroactively grant the challenge.
We won't pretend to have seen every challenge in NFL history, but that feels like something no one has seen before or will ever see again. And the nonsense explanation from Eck doesn't help the matter.
That's not the only mistake the refs made that hurt the Panthers, and it's not the only reason the Panthers fell short on Sunday in Charlotte. But it was essentially a 13-point swing in a five-point loss, and the NFL's attempt to justify one of the biggest mistakes this season just doesn't hold up.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: It's Time for the Panthers to Have an Uncomfortable Conversation About Dave Canales
full_text:
How much longer can the Carolina Panthers keep losing games before Dave Canales' job security becomes a serious conversation?
The Carolina Panthers had another opportunity to win on Sunday, but in the end, it was a 26-21 loss to the Denver Broncos. The Panthers held a 14-13 lead in the third quarter but were unable to close out the game.
But at some point, the head coach of a team must be held accountable for more than wins and losses. Mistakes on the part of the team have contributed to their current losses, and the organization must decide if Canales is the right person to lead the team to success.
The 13 penalties for 119 yards on Sunday against Denver were a big problem. Many of those penalties gave the Broncos extra yards and continued drives for them on offense.
Before Bryce Young threw the interception in the end zone to give the Broncos another opportunity, the Panthers had a chance to build on their third-quarter lead against the Broncos.
But Canales can't stop every single penalty or every single interception. At some point, the lack of discipline and poor execution of a team must fall on the head coach.
The Panthers are a team that is capable of competing with some of the best teams in the league. However, the problem is that Carolina is not winning games, and that is becoming increasingly obvious.
Carolina's offense was supposed to improve under Canales, and there have been some good moments for Bryce Young as he continues to develop as a quarterback. But those good moments are few and far between.
Carolina is 3-5 after three straight losses. Changes have been made on the defensive coaching staff, but the problems persist on both sides of the ball.
The Carolina Panthers must determine how much longer David Tepper is willing to wait for Dave Canales to turn around the offense and help develop the organization's young quarterback, Bryce Young.
If the Panthers continue to lose games for the same reasons, then Dave Canales should be on notice.
This is not to say that another coaching change would solve anything for the Panthers. There has been enough of that in Carolina over the past few years.
But keeping a coach on because you don't want to go through another coaching change is not a good enough reason to keep him.
Canales still has time to turn this season around. It remains to be seen if he will be able to do so.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Grading Bryce Young in Panthers Heartbreaking Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The downslide continues . After a 3-2 start to the season, the Carolina Panthers have lost their third straight game. This week's loss comes to the Denver Broncos, one of the top teams in the AFC and the current leader in the AFC West.
In the 26-21 loss, Carolina had multiple opportunities to build a bigger lead or go down the field and win the game, but timely mishaps from the offense and defense cost them.
Entering Sunday, Bryce Young had been in a bit of a slump, turning the ball over and struggling to find a consistent rhythm under constant pressure.
Despite the loss, Young was the least of Carolina's problems, and put together a great performance that gave the Panthers a chance to win.
Carolina leaned on Bryce Young throughout this game. Young threw 39 passes, completing 28 of them for 276 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, and 1 interception. That 71% completion percentage is Young's season-high, and it is only the second time he's posted over 70% this season.
Young took what the defense gave him. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker had moments throughout the game, but Young found the tight ends early and often. Two of Young's three touchdown passes were to tight ends; Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller were major factors in the game.
Even under pressure, Young returned to the subtle pocket movements that he's so good at, giving him just enough time to find his targets. Not only was he efficient, but Young also regained his poise and conviction in this game, a great sign for the rest of the season.
The box score will say that Young had two turnovers against Denver. One of them was an interception, and the other was a fumble. Neither of them was a crippling mistake by Young.
The interception was just a wild play: a throw to Tommy Tremble in the end zone, where Tremble and Broncos linebacker Justin Strnad made contact. The ball bounced off Tremble's hand instead of the ground, right there for Broncos safety Devon Key to intercept it.
One of the wildest interceptions in the Panthers Broncos game 🤯 pic.twitter.com/EEMtkoMbif
It was a freak play, and Young was exceptional on the drive before the turnover.
The game-sealing fumble perfectly summed up why this season has gone downhill for Carolina. With under two minutes to go, Young completed the first pass of a potential game-winning drive to McMillan for 11 yards.
Then disaster struck, as on the next play, left tackle Rasheed Walker was on an island with elite edge rusher Nik Bonitto. As Walker has done all season, he allowed pressure, resulting in a strip-sack by Nik Bonitto, recovered by the Broncos.
Nik Bonitto wreaking havoc! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fakoemKzzQ
Walker has given up the most pressure by a starting left tackle in the NFL this year. Carolina should've at least had Chuba Hubbard chip Bonitto to give Young extra time.
The Panthers can't ask for a better performance from Young. Being efficient, making plays with his legs, and making plays off schedule are what good QBs do, and Young did all of that.
The defense failed Carolina with too many penalties, and when the Panthers needed it most, the offensive line crumbled, as it had all season.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: 7 Winners and 8 Losers from Panthers' Hard-Fought Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers lost a frustrating one at home on Sunday. A crucial turnover in the end zone, aided by some truly shocking referee process, flipped the script when the Panthers appeared to have a win in their grasp. So, which players were winners and losers?
Where were you for the Darren Waller game?
Darren Waller may have jumped a route and stolen a catch from Jalen Coker, but he was reliable all day long. The Panthers needed to get things going quicker, and Waller was a good target in the middle of the field for Bryce Young to throw to.
13 penalties for 119 yards for the Panthers today
The undisciplined play continued this week. The Panthers can't stop committing bad penalties at bad times. We've harped on this all season and believe it ultimately comes back to coaching, and once again, Canales did not have his team playing clean football.
Another day, another great Chuba Hubbard outing. He was once again great at fighting through contact and picking up yardage where there really wasn't much. The Panthers needed something to keep the defense on its toes, and Hubbard provided that.
"Ref, you suck" chants at BOA after some questionable non-calls.
Now, on that discipline note, the Panthers did not help themselves, but the refs didn't, either. A few ticky-tack calls against the Panthers, plus a really bad miss when Feleipe Franks had his helmet punched off after a play was over.
Tommy Tremble's 10-yard TD catch in the 2nd quarter marks his 3rd of the season, which ties a career high (also 3 in 2022 and 2023).
The Panthers have relied on Tommy Tremble's blocking all season, and he was once again excellent in clearing lanes for Chuba Hubbard. Occasionally, he gets a chance to make his receiving presence felt, and he did so again today with a beautiful touchdown catch. He's rounding into an all-around weapon.
It's a trend with the cornerbacks, but Chau Smith-Wade has been pressed into action. He quite literally saved a touchdown on a fantastic deflection before the half. And among the main three coverage players, he didn't have any catastrophic mistakes or get picked on. He also broke up another would-be touchdown in the fourth quarter.
We understand that Marco Wilson's job is impossible, but he's also been bad. He continues to commit bad penalties and get burnt. You can't do both. He shouldn't be in this position, but he is and has to play a lot. And he's playing poorly.
That's OUR ball #DENvsCAR 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/5lc3GL2Nhz
The same logic applies to Corey Thornton. He has been on the practice squad for a long time, and we saw why for a while on Sunday. The Panthers shouldn't be relying on him like this, but that's the situation. From the get-go, the Broncos took aim at him and relentlessly abused him. However, he did come down with a massive interception. He also committed a crushing DPI on third down in the fourth quarter. It was a rollercoaster.
Ryan Fitzgerald with a 42 yard missed FG and a kickoff out of bounds with 1:27 left in the half that's not good enough
The Panthers are hard-pressed for points with how rough things have been on offense the last few weeks. Ryan Fitzgerald simply cannot be missing simple field goals. He has quietly been very mediocre this year, and it bit the Panthers badly on Sunday. Kickoff mistakes really hurt the Panthers, too.
Panthers shutting down the run and getting off the field on 3rd and long I wonder what changed
Todd Wash has his work cut out for him this week. He absolutely rose to the occasion. Despite playing without Jaelan Phillips and with no viable cornerbacks, Wash had this defense playing as well as we've seen it (yes, Bo Nix helps make a defense look better). They were aggressive and stopped the run, two things we've been begging to see all year. It was certainly not perfect, but this is a win with an asterisk for Wash.
Monroe Freeling was out of sorts on a couple of crucial plays, including a near-immediate sack on third down right after the Panthers surrendered the lead. He appeared to not even know the snap count and got beat before he even got out of his break.
The offensive line held up better, but the difference in this week versus the last two was Bryce Young. His mobility was clearly back to normal, and his confidence returned. He got into a roll in the second half that few quarterbacks have reached this season.
Understandably, there was some criticism of Brad Idzik. He seemed unable to find answers for his offense. That wasn't the case today, and it came against the NFL leader in sacks. His usage of the tight ends and Chuba Hubbard was pitch-perfect.
Nik Bonitto with the strip-sack on Bryce Young. Beats Rasheed Walker. Bonitto also recovers it.
Rasheed Walker nearly escaped unscathed, but he couldn't avoid making a back-breaking mistake. He was beat badly on the sack that became a fumble, essentially ending the game with the Panthers driving down by five.

title: 1 Egregious Referee Call Crushed Panthers in Week 9 Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers committed plenty of penalties, so the referees didn't do a whole lot to hurt them in that regard. They did miss some calls, but that's par for the course. What the refs did do to hurt the Panthers was much worse.
The Panthers got a defensive pass interference to put the ball on the one-yard-line. Then, they threw it to Tommy Tremble, and he was interfered with again, but the referees didn't call it. They let it go, and the ball seemed to bounce off the ground.
Instead, the ball actually bounced off of Tremble's hand and up into the air, where Devon Key snatched it. He didn't realize he'd intercepted it, and seemingly, no one else did. They played on.
After the Panthers ran the ball and were stuffed at the goal-line, the referees went to review it, saying that Broncos head coach Sean Payton had challenged it. But if he had, why did a full play go on and then some before they granted the challenge?
And of course, the ridiculous play was correctly ruled an interception, taking points away from the Panthers and reversing the momentum they'd built. The offense was rolling and it looked like the Broncos were on the ropes, but the black magic they've employed all season kicked in just before the fourth quarter.
DPI turned into an interception..after a whole play was run after this... https://t.co/VmEAmmgnYR
Panthers beat reporter Sheena Quick summed it up best. A penalty was missed, a play was run, and then a review of the previous play hurt the Panthers. It's not something you see every day, to say the least.
This is the second time the referees have arguably crushed the Panthers and took a win out of their hands by making a bad call or missing a call like this. Against the Cleveland Browns, a really ticky-tacky roughing the passer negated a game-sealing interception. On the next play, the Panthers yielded the winning touchdown.
This time, the referees' ineptitude cost the Panthers points. And on the immediate next drive, the Broncos scored a go-ahead touchdown. It was a monstrous point swing, and it was almost entirely because of referee ineptitude. And it ultimately cost the Panthers a win.
The Panthers didn't help themselves by committing a bunch of bad penalties, but this one was particularly awful and it wasn't even their fault. The interception was horrible luck, but the missed defensive pass interference and the review process were shady at best.
a total whiff by the ref and next snap is a sack/fumble clock should have stopped https://t.co/FB0SOT5Q23
It's also worth noting that on the decisive play in the fourth quarter, the referees appeared to miss an offsides and the Panthers had to continue hurrying up and turned the ball over on the next play. Had it been called correctly, that likely wouldn't have happened.

title: Panthers' Secondary Is Playing With Fire Against the Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina secondary had a rough first half against Denver. While Denver was able to exploit the Panthers’ secondary on several occasions, Carolina was able to prevent the Broncos from completely dominating the game.
Bo Nix is taking advantage of the space that the Carolina defensive backs are giving Denver’s receivers when they play off them. This was on display during the Broncos’ final drive before halftime.
The Broncos drove the length of the field but came away with only a field goal after a great stand by the Panthers’ defense.
The major problem is the amount of space Carolina is giving the Denver receivers. Denver has capitalized on the softer defense, finding room underneath and keeping drives alive.
The Panthers also have themselves to blame, with several penalties giving Denver more opportunities.
The secondary has bent in the first half, but not broken. Holding Denver to three points on its final drive of the first half was a huge stop for Carolina.
Todd Wash needs to make some adjustments at halftime. He needs to get his defense to challenge Denver’s receivers more.
If the Panthers are going to continue to play so far off Denver’s receivers, then Nix is going to continue to take what the defense gives him.
As Panthers On SI previously discussed in its breakdown of Carolina's defensive challenges against Denver , the Panthers need to find ways to make life more difficult for Nix.
The Panthers can still limit the damage done by Denver’s passing game, but the defensive backs need to be more aggressive in the second half.
The defensive backs have to tighten things up in the second half.

title: Caleb Williams' Interceptions Say the 'Big Eraser' Still Has Work to Do
full_text:
The Bears will be off two weeks before facing New Orleans but their offense already can imagine what it is going to face in that game and probably throughout the rest of the season until they show they have it fixed.
Caleb Williams identified the problem, and said it led to two of the four interceptions thrown in Sunday's 27-24 win over Tampa Bay. One interception he took complete blame for with his own ridiculous decision and another was a fluke tipped pass off a pass breakup.  On the two Williams threw on the dead run to his right in the second quarter, he cited extreme pressure from a blitz. He did mention he was trying to throw it away on both.
“They sent the same blitz a couple of times, and they got through, and that's what happens," Williams said. "You know, when a defense sends a similar blitz or sends a blitz over and over, that just means that they're getting through. That means they're going to keep going until we stop it."
The blitz, Williams maintained, kept him from being "the big eraser," and wiping out problems.
"We have to find ways to get better," Williams said. "We have to find ways to push through that.
"We have to find ways when it does happen, we have to make the adjustments. And then when it does happen, I have to be the big eraser.”
—Rex Ryan weighs in on the concerns he has with Caleb Williams following his performance against the Buccaneers ✍️ pic.twitter.com/vkpINFo5rE
It sounded a great deal as if he was pointing to some of his pass blockers not getting the job done against the blitz. Perhaps the big eraser should be used to wipe away his comments because his own mistake on the play actually caused the interception — he failed to throw away the ball. The big eraser should have been wiping out the play with a simple pass to the sideline to live another day.
Williams was out of the pocket on both plays and if he wanted to throw the ball away instead of trying to make a miracle throw or hope his receiver would make a leaping or diving catch, he had plenty of opportunity to do so. He just needed to throw it to the sidelines and be done with the play. He did it on other occasions.
It's not easy to simply give up on a play, but armed with a lead, and with a defense that was so good on third down (2 of 12) and at preventing points after turnovers (11 points allowed on five turnovers), all he had to do was show a little faith in the other side of the ball. He could have thrown it away on both plays instead of being "the big eraser."
One thing I hope happens over the bye week is Garrett Bradbury gets replaced by Logan Jones. It’s just impossible to do anything when your center misses his assignment and it’s instant pressure with an unblocked defender. pic.twitter.com/lvKbWbf7q6
The Bears equaled their season-high total of 15 pressures allowed in the game, according to Pro Football Focus. The blitz did have something to do with plenty of problems they had. The big eraser could have erased the pressure on those plays by throwing it away.
The biggest problem was not pressure but Williams' decision making, and more than anything else, his lack of awareness.
Miracle plays are best left for when they're needed, like on fourth-and-8 or third-and-long while facing a deficit. Leading in a game and throwing his second interception on the dead run from the Tampa Bay 35 on a first-and-10 play was foolish. They still had two more downs to get closer for a field goal or pick up the first down. Time wasn't a factor. Throwing it away gives them a shot to go in and add to a 14-3 lead.
Caleb Williams getting exposed in primetime after all this hype is so satisfying. Been way too hyped up since last year. Never should’ve been the Madden cover athlete. Glad we can finally get back to being honest. He’s nothing better than a “pretty good” QB. Tonight he’s BAD.
The third interception of the game came on a first-and-10 play from the Bears 26, which was about the worst place and down imaginable. They were winning 17-3 then and while time was a factor, having the ball at your own 26 inside of the final 40 seconds doesn't exactly say you've got an opportunity for more. Since it was first down, throwing it away again should have been automatic even for a QB who thinks he's the "big eraser."
The worst thing Williams did, though, was afterward.
Although he did take the blame for his first interception with the Bears at the edge of the red zone, not owning the second and third ones entirely and citing the pressure was actually fingering some of his blockers for blame.
“My belief is greater today than it was yesterday.” @danorlovsky7 shares his thoughts on the Bears after their victory against the Bucs with a game-winning field goal 🏈 pic.twitter.com/BLqVKy3yiy
Breakdowns in blocking will always happen against blitzing teams. The Bears also had 15 pressures allowed against Minnesota. Two interceptions on first-down plays when the sideline is right there for the throwaway puts it all on Williams. Not accepting all of the blame for it is all on Williams as well.
The bye week should come with some introspection for the Bears QB. This should include a decision to be a little more aware of down, distance and score before needlessly risking something stupid. All of that information is routinely stored on the scoreboard for him if he needs a reminder.
As for the blame game, the "Big Eraser" needs to erase that. He doesn't need to cite pass-blocking breakdowns as issues. Quarterbacks can afford to do this even less than they can afford to make big mistakes like needless interceptions on first down with the lead, because blame games tend to break down teams from within.
With Caleb Williams struggling do the #bears look to make a change? Whether that is starting Keenum or making a move. I just feel like you can't waste a defense of this caliber because you're qb can't protect the ball

title: Jeffery Simmons Draws Dirty Hit Accusation After Bears' Win Over Buccaneers
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive lineman Luke Goedeke is clearly not a fan of Chicago Bears defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons.
We saw the two players going at it a bit during the Bears' Week 9 win over the Bucs on Sunday night , and after the game, Goedeke expressed his frustration with a few things Simmons did.
According to ESPN's Kalyn Kahler , Goedeke claims Simmons holds opposing offensive linemen so he can help free up the defensive end on any given play.
Goedeke also accused Simmons of taking a cheap shot at his head.
"I mean, you're holding me on one, you came right at my head," he said. "I mean, that's always fun. He's known for it in pass pro, just holding the tackle so that the DE can run free, so I got that twice.
"So that's always a good one. But yeah, just kind of going back and forth. I mean, respect the guy, but some of the stuff he can really take out of his game. It's just kind of old, to be honest."
When asked to expound on what he said, Goedeke provided more details of what he doesn't like about Simmons' game.
"There's no reason to come out on a TE and just drill a tackle on the side of the head," Goedeke added. "It's really not a place really in the game for that, to be honest with you."
Goedeke said he only "occasionally" sees players doing what he accuses Simmons of doing, "but most will at least play with their hands and not try and launch themselves at you," he said.
The Bucs offensive lineman certainly isn't the first player in the NFL to complain about Simmons. We've heard a good amount of players air their grievances with the star tackle over the years.
We've seen multiple players accuse Simmons of not only dirty play , but even of spitting on them . Simmons is quite the trash-talker, something even Caleb Williams has experienced before .
Despite all of the accusations against him, Simmons has never been suspended or fined for spitting, but he has faced fines for other infractions, like unnecessary roughness, for example.
Simmons made his Soldier Field debut on Sunday night and once again made a big impact.
Big Jeff filled up the stat sheet with four tackles, one tackle for loss, one sack, one pass defensed and one QB hit. He tallied three pressures and two defensive stops in total, per Pro Football Focus .
But Simmons' impact extends beyond the stat sheet. Teams are routinely double-teaming him, and that is freeing up the guys around him to make plays.
Through two games, Simmons has been everything the Bears could have hoped for.

title: Bucs Let Caleb Williams and the Bears Off the Hook in a Win Straight Out of 2006
full_text:
If there's an uglier way to win a football game than the Chicago Bears' undeserved Week 9 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , I don't want to see it. Frankly, airing such a game would likely violate the Geneva Conventions. On Sunday night, after a first quarter in which Caleb Williams looked like prime Peyton Manning, Murphy's Law took over and everything went downhill for the Bears, with Williams throwing a career-worst four picks .
Somehow, someway, the Bears still managed to pull off a badly needed win, and they did it in classic Bears fashion: a dominant defensive performance to dig the Bears out of the gigantic hole dug by the offense.
In fact, this Sunday night game harkened back to arguably the most well-remembered game from the Bears' 2006 Super Bowl season. According to ESPN's Courtney Cronin , last night's win was the first time since Week 6 of the 2006 season that the Bears won a game with a -3 turnover differential.
For those that need a refresher, that Week 6 game was that famous showdown with the Arizona Cardinals in which the Bears came back from a 20-0 deficit to win. Quarterback Rex Grossman threw four interceptions, but the defense scored two touchdowns on forced fumbles and Hall of Fame returner Devin Hester carried a punt into the endzone for the go-ahead score.
After this game, the Cardinals head coach Dennis Green unleashed his postgame iconic rant , shouting to the media, "The Bears are who we thought they were, and that’s why we took the damn field... they are who we thought they were, and we let them off the hook!"
Tampa Bay's head coach Todd Bowles gave no such statement after the game, but he could hardly be blamed if he did. Caleb Williams channeled his inner Rex Grossman and nearly sunk the Bears with four disastrous interceptions. In his defense, at least he started off red-hot with back-to-back touchdown drives, but it was still a disgraceful performance.
Much like that 2006 game, Chicago's defense stepped up big time. They sacked Baker Mayfield four times, forced several three-and-outs and also repeatedly held the Bucs to field goals in the red zone. Then, in the fourth quarter, Jaylon Johnson picked off Mayfield and took it all the way back for a touchdown, his second career pick-six.
As frustrating as this game was for Bears fans, there's a bright silver lining, and that is that trading for superstar Jeffery Simmons has made this defense a Super Bowl caliber unit. A defense that can overcome five turnovers from the offense is a defense that can go all the way, and that was the biggest question facing the Bears  entering the 2026 season.

title: Gauntlet Ends for Bears With Win Thanks to Jaylon Johnson and Defense
full_text:
Maybe the Bears simply ran out of gas. It was a theory Ben Johnson had after Sunday's catastrophe averted with a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Bears have just played three strong defenses in a short period of time, four games in 22 days to be accurate.
"They know that we didn't play as well as we're capable of playing," Johnson said. "But I believe the best is yet to come in terms of our football in the back half of this season.
"We'll continue to build that as we go forward. They need some rest right now. That's what they need. They need to get away from these coaches. We'll clean up some things over the next couple of days and get them free from us for a little bit.”
JAYLON JOHNSON HOUSE CALL ☎️ 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/FVkfIjPwvQ
The rest can't hurt their running game, which will also benefit by getting Kyle Monangai back. It will obviously help running back D'Andre Swift after he was held to 31 yards on 12 carries as the running game had a season-low 72 yards.
The five turnovers nearly proved their undoing but the Bears' defense was up to the task of carrying the offense after Caleb Williams had built a 17-3 coming out to start the game.
"That's just who we are. We always fight," cornerback Jaylon Johnson said.
Bills could certainly use Cam Lewis. Another Brandon Beane masterclass https://t.co/vcDmsyRns5
The five turnovers produced only 11 points for Tampa Bay, and it was only three points for the first four turnovers on Williams' picks before Luther Burden fumbled while absorbing a helmet-to-helmet hit and a concussion.
Johnson's 67-yard pick-6, finished behind a block from Montez Sweat, kept the Buccaneers at bay. They also had an interception from Cam Lewis to thwart a threat. Four sacks didn't hurt, including one from defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons
“I think it was a big play all around," Ben Johnson said of Jaylon's pick. "You really could feel the momentum swing back in our favor after that one. He did a great job.
Jeffery Simmons' first sack at Soldier Field. pic.twitter.com/lRaQP6AV2d
"I thought it was a great call by (defensive coordinator Dennis Allen), just mixing up some coverages on him, and he was in a great spot. And once again, I thought Sweat showing up and leading the way with the lead block there to spring us free. That was huge for us.”
It wasn't everything as disaster nearly struck when Burden was injured and lost the ball to set up the tying points inside the red zone. But the Bears responded.
The defense was far from perfect, allowing 4.5 yards a carry and 126 total rushing yards while giving up a 58-yard pass to set up a TD.  However, they did hold Tampa Bay to 2-of-12 on third downs and 2-of-5 for TDs in the red zone.
Austin Booker breaks through for the sack on Baker Mayfield! 💥 📺 Sunday Night Football: Buccaneers at Bears on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/6UZjueLaXC
“I think that was really the story of the game was those guys stepping up and it was all the way up until that last one that they finally broke through and scored the touchdown," Johnson said. "But for the four previous (turnovers), I thought our defense did an outstanding job rising the occasion.
"They don't bat an eye, they don't blink. That's certainly what DA (Allen) preaches on that side of the ball, but I think those guys take a lot of pride in that as well. And we needed that tonight.”
It's not the type of overall team performance the Bears can be happy about but they haven't had another game like this with turnovers since the loss to Green Bay with backup quarterbacks playing. Williams survived his clunker thanks to his defense.
Now they need to get some rest.
Devin Bush hit pic.twitter.com/wXZgsXveya

title: Ben Johnson Confirms Zavion Thomas Was in the Dog House During Bears' Win over Bucs
full_text:
In three of the last four games going into Week 9, Chicago Bears wide receiver Zavion Thomas had seen an uptick in offensive snaps.
Thomas went from seeing nine or fewer over snaps over the first four games to playing 10 or more in three of the last four games, and he was on pace to see that many yet again or more in Week 9 after playing five early in the contest.
Unfortunately, the rookie made a bad mistake that cost him more playing time. Thomas was called for an unnecessary roughness penalty in the second quarter after a minor post-play dust-up between the rookie and a Tampa Bay Buccaneers defender.
After that, we didn't see Thomas on offense again, which made us wonder if he was being punished or if that was simply part of the game plan. After the game, head coach Ben Johnson basically confirmed Thomas' benching on offense.
"Did you say anything to him coming off the sideline after that possession ends?" ESPN's Courtney Cronin asked of Thomas.
"Yeah, I don't know that he played on offense after that," Johnson said .
Good on Johnson for teaching his young player a lesson. That is how you avoid things like that happening on a consistent basis.
The penalty came in the second quarter and on a first-down play when the Bears were on the Bucs' eight-yard line.
That penalty set Chicago back 15 yards to the 21 after D'Andre Swift's two-yard gain on the play. Caleb Williams tossed a pick on the very next snap and one has to wonder if that would've happened if the Bears were closer to the end zone.
In his five offensive snaps, Thomas was targeted twice and reeled in one catch for 13 yards.
It wasn't a full benching because Thomas continued in his return role, where he gained 88 yards on three attempts, good enough for a strong kick return average of 29.3 yards per tote.
Thomas had a long return of 40 yards, and he nearly had a 91-yard touchdown return but it was called back because of a penalty by linebacker D'Marco Jackson.
Thomas has come close to breaking one on a few occasions this season and it feels like a matter of when, not if, he finds pay dirt.
Thomas could see a sizeable role in Week 11 if Luther Burden is ruled out.
Burden suffered a concussion on Sunday that forced his early exit from the game, and while chances are he'll be cleared by before the next game because the Bears have a bye in Week 10, that's not guaranteed.
If Burden sits, Thomas would be in line for more work, as would Jahdae Walker.

title: Jeffery Simmons Puts NFL on Notice After Bears' Win Over Bucs: 'Good Luck'
full_text:
We've gotten used to seeing the Chicago Bears' offense bailing out the defense, but it was very much the other way around on Sunday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
After a fast start, the Bears' offense sputtered in a big way and just couldn't get its act together over the final three quarters.
Luckily for the Bears, the defense came to play and kept them in control until a Luther Burden fumble deep in Bears territory allowed the Bucs to tie the game up late in the fourth.
At that point, it was time for the Bears' offense to wake up, and the unit did just that en route to getting in position for a game-winning Cairo Santos field goal that averted what would have been a disastrous collapse.
The Bears did not play a complete game on Sunday night, but we know Caleb Williams is capable of better than the "Jekyll and Hyde" performance we saw against the Bucs.
We also know the Bears' defense is playing at a high level, and Jeffery Simmons rightly pointed out that if the Bears can put a complete game together on a weekly basis, this team will be incredibly tough to beat.
"One thing I told Caleb is, we got his back," Simmons said after the game, per CHGO Bears . "And just like at the end of the game when we really needed to get down in field goal range, he did his part."
"He made the plays that needed to be made and that's going to be the rest of the season," Simmons added. "Sometimes we're going to need him to pull us out of things. Maybe we can't get off the field on third down and they end up scoring.
"It's our job to go out there and just draw the line and that's what we're going to continue to do. We have his back and once we put a complete game together, good luck," Simmons said.
Hard to argue with that sentiment with the Bears sporting both a top-10 offense and defense. Chicago ranks seventh in points scored and ninth in points against after Week 9.
Bear in mind, the Bears aren't even at 100% on defense, with guys like Dayo Odeyingbo, Malik Muhammad and Coby Bryant all on the shelf, so there's the potential Dennis Allen's unit could be even better than it is right now.
Muhammad has missed two games in a row with his toe injury, but there's a realistic chance he will be back after the bye. Odeyingbo has been on injured reserve since Week 5, so he'll be eligible to return after the bye as well.
Bryant is probably still a ways off, if he returns at all. With the initial four to six month estimate, the earliest Bryant will be back is mid-December.
All of that and we haven't even talked about the potential for the Bears to make another trade, which could come at edge rusher and/or cornerback.

title: Luther Burden Headlines Bears Injury Updates Following Week 9 Victory Over Buccaneers
full_text:
The Chicago Bears saw a few notable players go down with injuries during the Week 9 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , but none were more important than wide receiver Luther Burden.
Burden suffered a scary injury in the fourth quarter when he took a hard shot to his head from Bucs edge rusher Rueben Bain in what was a nasty helmet-to-helmet hit that wasn't flagged.
The Bears wideout immediately fell to the ground after fumbling the football and had to be helped off the field by trainers after.
After the game, head coach Ben Johnson revealed that Burden has suffered a concussion and will now enter the protocol.
Along with Burden, cornerback Tyrique Stevenson was another player Johnson mentioned in his injury round-up after the win.
"Two injuries to note. We have Tyrique with a thumb and Luther with a concussion," Johnson told reporters . "So, we'll see where they're at from there."
Stevenson, who has been battling through injuries all year, exited the game twice with his thumb injury. He was able to return after the first issue, but the second one put him out for good.
We also saw Kyler Gordon exit briefly with what appeared to be an arm injury, but the veteran defensive back was able to return to the game and finish it out, so he appears to be OK.
It's hard to say for sure with either player, but both at least have a shot with the Bears set to be have a bye in Week 10.
It's impossible to know about Stevenson's status because we do not know just how severe his thumb injury is. We should get more information over the course of the week.
As for Burden, his concussion looked bad, so if the Bears had to play this week, he would be in serious doubt. But with an extra week to get right, Burden could be on the field in Week 11.
That said, concussions can be a multi-week injury, so Burden isn't out of the woods just because Chicago has a bye in between its next game.
The Bears could get two key defenders back in Week 11.
Dayo Odeyingbo, who is on injured reserve with a quadriceps injury, is eligible to return in Week 11, although it remains uncertain if he'll actually be able to.
The other key defender is Malik Muhammad, who has missed two games in a row because of a toe issue. Muhammad was reportedly expected to play in Week 9, but he did not end up suiting up.
We'll see if the week off will be enough to get him ready to go in Week 11.

title: 4 Winners and 3 Losers From Bears Week 9 Victory Over Buccaneers
full_text:
The Chicago Bears got off to a hot start against Tampa Bay, but they were unable to maintain it. Caleb Williams couldn't miss a throw over the first 20 minutes, and couldn't seem to hit one from that point until the final drive of the game.
Williams threw a career-high four interceptions, and the Bears committed a season-high five turnovers. They also struggled to get much going on the ground against Tampa Bay's stout run defense.
NFL teams rarely come out on top when they commit five turnovers, but the Bears moved to 7-2 on the strength of an elite defensive performance. Cairo Santos' 38-yard game-winner helped Chicago come away with a 27-24 win.
Unsurprisingly, Williams stood out for all the wrong reasons. A few notable defenders stood out for much better reasons, though.
Devin Bush easily had his best game as a Chicago Bear against the Buccaneers. He was all over the field from the first snap and looked like a bullet shooting through gaps at the line of scrimmage. Simply put, he set the tone. That was also reflected in the box score. Bush led the team (as a linebacker should) with nine tackles and also added two pass deflections.
Even when Bush didn't make the play, he often got in the path of the ball-carrier and allowed a teammate to make a play. This was the version of Devin Bush the Bears thought they were getting when they signed him to a three-year, $30 million deal this offseason.
Zavion Thomas' unnecessary roughness penalty completely stunted the offense's momentum midway through the second quarter. The Bears would've had a second-and-goal from the six if he hadn't committed the penalty, and Williams threw an interception (only his second of the season, at that time) on the next play.
The interception obviously wasn't Thomas' fault (more on that later). Still, they wouldn't have been in that situation if he hadn't lost control of his emotions. To his credit, he had what should've been a 92-yard kick return touchdown in the third quarter. Unfortunately, it got taken away due to a pitiful (on the ref's part) holding penalty. Still, it was a performance to forget for the third-round selection.
Chicago's defensive line might not have been perfect, but they held their own against one of the league's best offensive lines. It was a battle of good on good, and the Bears proved to be better for much of the contest.
Chicago finished the contest with four sacks and nearly got to Baker Mayfield on a few other plays. The Bucs stuck to their rushing attack and managed to accumulate a respectable 126 rushing yards, but they came into the game averaging a league-high 168.6 yards on the ground. It wasn't easy to find room to run against the Bears' stout defensive front.
Sure, Caleb Williams made a handful of plays early against Tampa Bay, but he was also far too reckless with the football. His first three interceptions were unacceptable, and two of them came immediately after Chicago's defense made great plays to get the ball back. He couldn't capitalize on the momentum.
Williams has extreme confidence in his arm, and that's for good reason. He's one of the league's most talented signal-callers. Still, Williams has to learn that opposing defenses occasionally have the answer on a play, and a zero-yard play is much better than a turnover.
To his credit, he hit the throw on their final drive when they needed him to. It was far from his best showing, though. He'll hopefully learn from the performance.
Cam Lewis has made a strong case to remain on the field in recent weeks. He had a rock-solid performance last week against Seattle, when he displayed a level of physicality that wasn't expected from someone with his size (5'9", 183 lbs.), and he followed it up with an even better performance against Tampa Bay.
Lewis tied for second on the team with six tackles and also had an impressive interception. His versatility was also on display, as he played nickelback after Kyler Gordon briefly left the game. Even after Coby Bryant makes his debut, Lewis will still be a key player in sub packages.
This is the second week in a row where opponents have gotten their hands on a punt. While they got lucky with a 45-yard roller last week, they weren't nearly as lucky this week. Tampa Bay got the ball at midfield after a second-quarter block.
Unfortunately, that wasn't the only negative play in the third phase. We already mentioned the ticky tack penalty that took away the 92-yard kickoff return (which is tough to pin against the unit), and Kalif Raymond also muffed a punt that he was lucky to get back on top of. They have quite a bit to figure out on special teams over the Bye Week.
The much-maligned Jaylon Johnson finally bounced back after a rough start to the campaign. He showed up when they needed him most and stole the momentum back for Chicago with a timely 6-67-yard pick-six late in the third quarter, giving Chicago a 24-13 lead when the Bucs were near field goal range.
Johnson also held up much better in coverage against the Buccaneers. He didn't have any coverage gaffes and seemingly didn't allow any completions in coverage. The previous criticism may have been fair, but he deserves his flowers for a strong performance on Sunday night. The Bears lose this game without his pick six.
