title: NFC North Standings: Can Bears Move Into First Place With Vikings Loss on Monday Night?
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' Week 9 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was anything but pretty, but it did move Chicago one step closer to taking over first place in the NFC North.
The Bears looked like they were going to dominate the Bucs early on, but Caleb Williams started throwing picks and the Bears' offense as a whole completely hit a wall.
Thankfully for Chicago, the defense saved the day , with the unit led by Jeffery Simmons making enough plays and stops to give the offense an opportunity to win the game late, which it did.
All in all, it was a successful day for the NFC North, but all eyes will now be on the first place Minnesota Vikings, who will close out Week 9 against the Buffalo Bills.
Here's a look at where things stand in the NFC North and if the Bears can move into first place with a Vikings loss.
1. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) 2. Chicago Bears (7-2) 3. Detroit Lions (6-2) 4. Green Bay Packers (6-3)
The Packers, Bears and Lions all won.
Hilariously enough, the Lions got all they could handle from the Miami Dolphins, who gave Detroit a run for its money.
Meanwhile, Green Bay had a very different result after crushing the New England Patriots thanks to Jordan Love, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson shredding the Patriots' defense.
Yes, the Bears will move into first place in the NFC North if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday night.
The Vikings do own the head-to-head tie-breaker over Chicago currently after beating the Bears in Week 2 , but Minnesota would have one less victory and the same number of losses as Chicago with a defeat at the hands of the Bills in Week 9, so the Bears would sport a superior win percentage.
Chicago's stay at the top could be very short if the Bears do get there on Monday night, as the Lions or Vikings could jump the Bears in Week 10 when they're on a bye.
If the Vikings lose in Week 9 but win in Week 10, Minnesota would pull even with the Bears record-wise, but again, the victory over Chicago earlier in the season would officially put the Vikings in first.
The Lions can also match the Bears' record and push past them next week since Detroit's 2-0 divisional record is superior to Chicago's 0-2 mark.
As we mention these tie-breakers, it's important to note that none of them are settled yet with more NFC North matchups waiting in the wings the rest of the season.
Because the Packers have three losses, they are the only team in the division that cannot walk out of Week 10 in first place.
After taking on the Bills on Monday night, the Vikings will battle the Packers in Week 10 in Lambeau. The Lions will take on the Patriots in Germany.

title: Game Balls in Bears' Undeserved Week 9 Win vs Buccaneers
full_text:
A game that should have been a blowout victory for the Chicago Bears turned into a nail-biter, thanks in large part to a befuddling meltdown by quarterback Caleb Williams. NFL analyst Donte Whitner picked the Bucs to serve the Bears 'humble pie' , and in a way they did, but at least it came with a side of victory as the Bears enter a badly needed bye week with a 7-2 record and, for now, the division lead.
Despite jumping out to a 14-0 lead and looking like The Greatest Show on Turf, a comedy of errors unfolded for the remaining three quarters. Williams threw four (yes, four) interceptions. Three of the Bears' first four second-half drives went three-and-out. Kalif Raymond muffed a third-quarter punt and nearly turned it over. A third-quarter injury to Kyler Gordon forced him to briefly exit the game. Murphy's Law reigned supreme.
There'll be plenty of time over the next few days to dissect what went wrong in this one, and the film review sessions should be particularly brutal for Williams. Adding insult to injury, he won't have a chance to redeem himself for another two weeks. But for now, let's hand out some game balls.
In what was by far his best game as a Bear, Devin Bush played like a man possessed on Sunday night. Almost every time the Bears needed a big play on defense, Bush was there to deliver a teeth-rattling hit. Whether it was defending the run or the pass, Bush was everyone all at once and kept the Bucs' offense from getting much traction.
For his electric performance, Bush earned this first game ball, his first of the season.
Caleb Williams had just thrown his fourth interception of the night (to be fair, it was an unlucky tipped pass), setting Tampa Bay up with yet another short field. All hope seemed to be lost, and that's when Jaylon Johnson reeled in arguably the biggest interception of his career. Johnson read Baker Mayfield's eyes on a pass, caught it at full speed, and took it all the way back for a touchdown, the second pick-six of his career.
I said in my Week 9 stat predictions that the Bears would pick Mayfield off three times. They fell one interception short of that mark, but Johnson did his job, and for that he gets this game ball, which is also his first of the season.
In the interest of full transparency, I struggled to identify a third Bear worthy of a game ball in this one. In the end, I went with the other defender to snag a timely interception, and that's Cam Lewis. He got the ball rolling near the end of the first half, easily cutting in front of a pass attempt in the middle of the field and securing the catch.
Unfortunately, a play that should have kept the Bucs at three points to end the half was for nought as Williams immediately gave the ball back to Tampa Bay with his third interception of the night, allowing Tampa Bay to tack on three more points. Nevertheless, it was a big-time play by Lewis and earned him this game ball.

title: Zac Taylor Shoots Down Idea That Bengals Will Make Trade Before Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is quickly approaching, and rumors and deals are gaining momentum.
Many experts believe the Bengals have a strong roster but need to make a move or two to improve their chances of winning. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor thinks differently.
"No, I feel good about where we're at," Taylor said when asked whether any specific areas of the team need improvement from the outside.
The Bengals have been mentioned in rumors as being interested in Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, as well as actively looking for "middle-tier options across the board," according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
When pressed again about what the next 24 hours would look like for Taylor with the trade deadline looming, he again said, "That's just that's a bunch for everybody to talk about, but we're good."
"We're just focused on Pittsburgh right now. It's our biggest focus," Taylor continued.
Taylor keeps dismissing trade talk, emphasizing that roster building depends on execution and internal development, not midseason trades. Taylor believes the Bengals' success starts in their own locker room. They need to tune out the outside noise and focus on what they can control. Taylor highlights how guys on the practice squad and backup unit step in seamlessly when injuries hit, specifically on the offense.
"Smart players get an opportunity to play here...We hold them to the same standard as Ja'Marr and Tee... The next-man-up mentality has been really good for us, and those guys have embraced it and stepped up."
Taylor clearly believes in the current roster and sees no need to bring in outside help.
The Bengals are betting on themselves. Of course, Taylor's comments don't mean the Bengals won't add at the deadline. They've made in season trades in each of the past two seasons. They also swung a blockbuster deal with the Giants for Dexter Lawrence in April.
Taylor can't come out and say they're hoping to add to the team. That's out of his control. His job as head coach is to focus on the players in the building.
The Bengals have won four-straight games. They host the Steelers on Sunday with first place in the AFC North on the line.
"We're not running from divisional games. A team that's gotten us once," Taylor said. "I think we've done a good job of just focusing on the opponent in front of us and making that game the biggest game of the year, and that will be no different this week when Pittsburgh comes down."

title: Report: Bengals 'Explored' Trade Options Ahead of NFL's 2026 Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals have reportedly "explored the middle tier" of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline market, but nothing has come to fruition.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that nugget on Monday afternoon as we sit a little more than 24 hours from the deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
Cincinnati has a big hole at starting linebacker and depth tight end, but no move has happened yet.
"After speaking to league sources over the weekend and really last week, let's dive into it," Schultz said. "Let's start with the Kansas City Chiefs looking for a wide receiver. Also, the 49ers are looking for a wide receiver and a pass rusher. The Bills would love to improve their defense. I could see them targeting a safety. The Broncos are looking for a running back or tight end.
"The Jags defensive tackle. They already made the big move for Jesse Bates. Pittsburgh wants a receiver and a corner. The Bengals explored the middle tier across the board. Chicago would love to add to their secondary with a corner."
Cincinnati is back in town as a team following the trip to Spain, and Zac Taylor didn't sound like the front office is going to make a definitive move before the deadline.
"Nothing, that's a bunch for everybody to talk about, but we're good," the Bengals' head coach said about trades to the media on Monday.
The Bengals shouldn't be overpaying for anyone that's reportedly on the market right now. They have clear needs at linebacker, but other than that, there aren't a ton of glaring holes that one move could fix right now.
Still, a fellow AFC contender in Jacksonville traded away multiple picks today, including a second-round selection, to go after new blood at safety and defensive tackle for a Super Bowl push this season.
Cincinnati needs to make sure they don't let a good deal pass them by with the lightning bottled right now. They sport the league's third-most efficient offense on the season by EPA/play and most efficient in the past month, the second easiest remaining schedule on ESPN's FPI, and the MVP frontrunner in Joe Burrow.
Team scenarios like that don't roll around every year, and Cincinnati has to do everything it can (rationally) to maximize this season. Many thought they'd be in the Super Bowl multiple times back in Feb. 2022, and they are yet to go back.

title: Zac Taylor Sets Injury Table For Final 2026 Matchup Against Steelers
full_text:
Zac Taylor's Cincinnati team completed its Spain trip, and he and the roster returned home safely on Monday.
Cincinnati picked up one new injury to starting guard Dylan Fairchild in Madrid, Spain, and other than that, their good injury luck looks like it's continuing into the huge AFC North matchup against the Steelers this week.
Cincinnati is hoping to get Kyle Dugger (quad) back soon from his lingering muscle issue, while injured reserve stints for Andrei Iosivas and Jalen Davis are closer than ever to being over.
"Was really the last play of the game," Taylor said about Fairchild. "We'll just see how he feels as the week goes on."
It's a historic matchup ahead in this Bengals-Steelers rivalry. Sunday night marks the first time since 1975 that two AFC North teams with .750 records or better are meeting in primetime in October or later
Cincinnati dropped a standalone-game statement on Sunday morning for the American audience.
Joe Burrow had another four-plus touchdown performance and became MVP frontrunner along the way.
"Joe is playing at an unbelievably high level right now," Taylor said. "It's difficult not to put the ball in his hands on every play given how everybody is playing around him as well. We just got to keep this momentum going. This is a fickle league. We're in a good spot right now coming out of this trip. We just got to maintain this momentum, and that's going to be on us to handle the flight back and the rest of the week the right way and be ready to go Sunday night."
Cincinnati handled last week pretty perfectly, and needs to lock in again this week.
"We knew two teams were going to handle the same schedule, and we just wanted to come out and make sure we showed that we've handled it better than anybody," Taylor said while in Spain. "Again, proud of the way all three phases played. There might have been a lull here and there in each phase, but the other side picked us up, and we were able to finish the game the right way."
Cincinnati battles the Steelers at 8:15 p.m. ET on Sunday night for control of the AFC North moving forward.

title: Bengals Stars Dominate With Great PFF Grades Across 34-17 Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Bengals won their fourth consecutive game on Sunday, 34-17, over the Atlanta Falcons . It featured some great individual outings all over the roster, captured by the Pro Football Focus grades from Sunday.
We start on offense, where Ja'Marr Chase (92.6 overall) exploded for his best performance of the 2026 season. He led all Bengals players in grading after hauling in 10 catches for 155 yards and one score.
A shocker, I know, but Joe Burrow (84.6) was right behind him with another MVP-level performance . The rest of the top five offensive grades went to Tee Higgins (78.9), Amarius Mims (76.1), and Dohnte Meyers (68.9).
Mims notched his best run-blocking mark of the season (89.4 overall) as he cements his place as one of the five best right tackles in the sport.
The bottom of the offense went in this order (min. 20 snaps): Jack Endries (48.2), Mike Gesicki (49.1), Ted Karras (51.1), Drew Sample (52.3), and Orlando Brown Jr. (61.8).
Flipping to defense, DJ Ivey (89.4) led all defenders, but only played seven snaps, so Sexy Dexy gets the nod this week. He's been a revelation for the Bengals defense, and Dexter Lawrence was great again (86.9 grade on 43 snaps).
The rest of the top five went in this order (min. 20 snaps): Josh Newton (74.9), Bryan Cook (73), Boye Mafe (70.1), and Jordan Battle (69.4).
It's good to see Cook and Battle playing well entering the trade deadline. Safety has been a shaky spot at times this season.
At the bottom, Sunday was one of the worst games in years for DJ Turner (32.9) as he committed a couple of pass interference penalties. The rest of the bottom five went in this order (min. 20 snaps): Demetrius Knight Jr. (42.8), Barrett Carter (51.3), Jonathan Allen (56.1), and Myles Murphy (57.1).
Linebacker continues to be a shaky position. Carter is posting a moderate 63.7 grade this season, but Cincinnati could easily upgrade Knight's spot. He posted a 40.4 grade as a rookie and is only up to 48 overall this season.
Cincinnati may be one defensive starter trade away from being the go-to contender in the AFC.

title: 3 Big Moves the Bengals Need to Make Before Upcoming NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals need to make some moves ahead of the NFL trade deadline this season if they want to be one of the top Super Bowl contenders down the stretch. They have the foundation of a loaded team with the talent to win it all, but they're missing a few pieces.
What do the Bengals need to do ahead of the trade deadline in order to put themselves in the perfect position to win the Super Bowl?
The Bengals would be best off if they could trade for Jonathan Taylor, but the asking price is going to be too much for them to pay.
As a result, they might need to pivot to a more affordable option like Breece Hall. Hall has a lot of talent and could be an impact player for the Bengals, though he isn't as valuable as a superstar like Taylor. Still, Hall would be the best running back on the Bengals.
He hasn't been as good as he normally is this season, but the talent is still there. Adding him without breaking the bank would be exactly what Cincinnati needs on offense.
The Bengals also need to target some help in their secondary, as cornerback has become an issue.
They have a few solid options, but that's it. Adding a veteran cornerback with the flexibility to play on the boundary and in the slot would be ideal. Somebody like Donte Jackson could likely be had for an affordable price while bringing enough value to the Bengals to be worth it.
The big splash that the Bengals could look to make is in the secondary at safety.
Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker is the perfect playmaker to add to the Bengals secondary. He has the ability to make splash plays, as he put on full display against the Bengals earlier this season when he intercepted three passes from Joe Burrow. Burrow is one of the better quarterbacks in the league, so it's even more impressive that Hooker tallied all of these big plays against him in their recent battle.
It might be relatively expensive to bring Hooker in, but he's the kind of playmaker they need to add in the secondary.

title: A Veteran Secondary Piece Who Could Elevate the Bengals Prior to the Trade Deadline
full_text:
It wasn't the prettiest performance, but the Cincinnati Bengals picked up their fifth win of the season last Sunday in a 43-36 shootout victory over the Tennessee Titans in overtime.
Every game is important, but with the way the AFC North has performed this season, the Bengals have to take care of business when they have an opponent on the schedule like the Titans.
With postseason dreams becoming a potential reality, it's time for the Bengals' front office to look a little closer at the trade deadline. One team has a very strong secondary piece that would fit perfectly in Cincinnati.
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer recently spoke with NBC Sports Boston about potential moves the New England Patriots could make before the November 10th trade deadline. One name Breer discussed was veteran cornerback Carlton Davis III.
“Carlton Davis would be another one to watch," Breer said . " If you look at the roster big picture, they’ve gotten older in a lot of key spots. And they aren’t exactly flush with draft capital over the next couple of years."
Breer believes the Patriots want to make their roster younger, and moving Davis would do exactly that. However, would a move be possible?
The Patriots are one season removed from a Super Bowl appearance, and their window doesn't seem to be closed at the moment. At 5-4, the Patriots are in place to get back to the postseason this season.
Davis joined the Patriots last season after one year with the Detroit Lions. Before that, Davis spent six seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he was a member of a Super Bowl winning team.
Davis is a veteran corner with postseason experience. His resume is one the Bengals' front office should be jumping all over if he becomes available.
The Bengals defense had a rough day at the office against Tennessee. Titans quarterback Cam Ward tossed for 304 yards and two touchdown passes.
To put those numbers in perspective, Ward had not thrown for over 250 yards all season. The rookie quarterback tied his best completion percentage at 65% and also threw two touchdown passes in one game for the first time in his career.
The Bengals' defense was part of a lot of firsts that no defense wants to be connected to. If Davis becomes available, this should be a no-brainer for the Bengals.

title: Winners and Losers from Bengals Dominant 34-17 Win Over Falcons
full_text:
There was no jet lag in sight for the Bengals and their offense as Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase lit the entire Falcons defense ablaze en route to a 34-17 rout in Madrid . The team now travels back to Cincinnati to prepare for a big game against the Steelers on Sunday Night Football.
Here are five winners and three losers from Sundays win in Madrid:
Everyone knew Ja'Marr Chase would have a huge game this season, though he still exceeded expectations for what it would look like.
Chase had the best first half of his career in Madrid, exploding for eight catches, 142 yards, and a touchdown in the first half. His touchdown also tied him with Randy Moss as the only two receivers to record at least seven touchdowns in their first six seasons.
He finished the game as the Bengals leading receiver with 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown.
This week is one that Turner will look back on as a disappointment as he had two costly pass interference penalties against Drake London that led to two Falcons touchdowns.
He also missed a key tackle against Bijan Robinson on 3rd and 13 that would have prevented the All-Pro running back from converting.
Burrow put on as electric a show as it gets for the crowd in Madrid. He had 18 completions for 234 yards in the first half, with three total touchdowns. He finished the day with 24 completions for 271 yards and four scores.
Burrow has cemented his place in the MVP race for this season and is playing as well as he ever has in his career.
The constant mental errors on defense have to end at some point.
An offsides penalty in the first half turned what should have resulted in a Falcons punt into a field goal for Atlanta. Add in Turners two DPI penalties that resulted in touchdowns and all of the Falcons points on the day came from needless errors.
It does not help that Jordan Battle also inexplicably dropped a pick-six that would have slammed the door shut in Madrid. Golden has to drill into this unit and officially put a stop to these mental errors.
Higgins dominated with several tough grabs in key moments, two of which happened in the end zone as he notched two touchdowns on the day along with five catches for 32 yards. He continues to have the best season of his career in this dynamic offense.
Gesicki witnessed his touchdown streak come to an end as he only managed two catches for 11 yards on Sunday.
He simply was not a large part of the Bengals gameplan this week. However, he still holds the Bengals record for most consecutive games with a touchdown at five, so he still has his name etched in franchise history regardless.
Chase Brown and Samaje Perine finally found light in the run game as both combined for 100 yards on 20 carries with Brown averaging 6.3 yards per carry.
Brown also added three catches for 18 yards to his total and both backs played their respective roles as well as they have all season. While it may still benefit the team to add another running back at the trade deadline, the may feel less inclined to do so after this performance.
Money Mac saw the field for the first time in a couple weeks and nailed both field goal attempts from 57 yards and 43 yards out respectively. McPherson has now extended his franchise record of consecutive field goals to 24.

title: Bengals Soaring in Unfamiliar Territory, and We're Not Talking About Spain
full_text:
Five weeks ago, Joe Burrow sat in front of the media following a 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars that dropped the Cincinnati Bengals to 2-2, and he made a proclamation.
“This isn’t Armageddon,” he said.
Because for the teams standing in way of Burrow and the Bengals’ swelling offensive juggernaut, those 60 minutes surely have felt cataclysmic.
“For the most part, we were lights-out,” Burrow said following Sunday’s 34-17 victory against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid.
Burrow accounted for four touchdowns, marking the fourth consecutive game in which he’s had at least that many. All four of those games have resulted in wins, moving the Bengals to 6-2, their best start since 2015 when they opened 8-0.
After scoring touchdowns on their final three possessions in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans, Burrow and the Bengals found the end zone on their first three Sunday at the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium.
“We didn't score on every single possession, so you know, always room to improve,” Burrow said.
That’s where the bar is right now for this Cincinnati offense, believing it can score on every possession.
As it were, the Bengals scored on their first four and five of their first six to race away from the Falcons and negate the explosiveness of Bijan Robinson and their run game.
Burrow’s first of four touchdowns came on a 47-yard deep shot to Ja’Marr Chase up the sideline, one that looked identical to the one he botched the week before with a wobbly throw that resulted in an interception and was followed by Chase, who had dusted the coverage, slamming his helmet on the sideline in anger.
Sunday, the duo  pulled off the play with perfection.
“Obviously when something like that happens … I worked hard on that this week so I don't miss another one like that,” Burrow said.
“They were pretty much in man (coverage) at first,” Chase said. “(The safety) played too low, and that's what we knew they were going to do. When Joe saw A.J. Terrell on me, he got pretty excited.”
And after Chase scored, the large contingent of Bengals fans who made the trip got excited watching Chase and Higgins show off a bull fighting celebration in the end zone.
The second drive ended with Burrow scoring on a 1-yard run to give the Bengals the lead.
Then Higgins caught a 4-yard TD from Burrow for a 21-10 advantage. And though Higgins capped the scoring drive, Chase fueled it with five catches for 69 yards on the 10-play, 88-yard march.
It started with a short pass that Chase turned into a 31-yard gain. There was a third-and-1 fling to escape pressure that resulted in a Chase diving catch, one the Falcons thought couldn’t been legit until they lost their replay challenge.
There also was a third-and-9 conversion in which Chase made one of the best sideline top-taps of his career, as the receiver showed off all of his skills in a span of 6 minutes and 43 seconds.
“I had so much fun watching him” Higgins said. “Once he got that first touchdown, I said, ‘Uh-oh, here it come.’ It just was a snowball effect after that. He was making play after play, and I'm so proud of him, for real.”
Higgins is off to the best eight-game start to a season in his career with 48 catches for 758 yards and six touchdowns.
That volume has come as Chase’s expense somewhat, but he flipped the script – literally – Sunday in Spain.
After Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards last week, Chase had 10 for 155 against Altana, including eight for 142 before halftime, marking the best first half of his career.
“We just feel like we got a lot of ways to attack you,” Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. “I'm not trying to gloat or anything like that. We have a lot of high-level player players. I feel like we have a lot of answers if teams want to try to take away somebody, whether it's Tee or Ja'Marr, whatever they want to do. We just feel like we got good answers.
“Joe doesn't force the ball. He takes the ball where it needs to go based on the looks,” he continued.” Even if sometimes they're leaning to a guy or doubling a guy, he's still going to give him the opportunity, and some of those opportunities come up big for us.”
Burrow has thrown at least three touchdown passes in four consecutive games. He has 23 and just six interceptions for the season.
He’s also scored three rushing touchdowns, leaving him just two shy of his career high in that category.
Don’t be surprised if he’s neck and neck with Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen for the best odds to win MVP by the time all of the Week 9 games are complete.
And, oh by the way, the Bengals got running back Chase Brown going Sunday with his two longest runs of the season for 19 and 16 yards. He finished with 57 yards on just nine carries (6.3).
Cincinnati is 6-2 and tied with the Steelers for first in the AFC North Division, although Pittsburgh has the tiebreaker edge via its 30-27 win in Week 3.
The Bengals offense is playing some of its best football of the Burrow era, and yet it feels as though there are more levels to reach. And more opponents to annihilate.
“To be 6-2 right now is a big deal,” Taylor said. “(We’re) going home. We have a major divisional game coming our way against Pittsburgh. They've already gotten us once this year, so we got to handle this flight back the right way. We got to get our bodies recovered. We got to have a great week and be ready for our home fans on Sunday night.”

title: 'Hopefully People Took Notice' - Joe Burrow Continues MVP-Level Run in Spain
full_text:
Joe Burrow is playing MVP-level football, and it's leading to a lot of winning for the Bengals.
He spoke to the media after Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons and detailed how this offense has been able to tally 30-plus points in four straight weeks and be by far the most prolific attack in the league over that span.
Burrow dialed up another elite day , going 24-of-29 passing for 271 yards, three touchdowns, and one more score on the ground.
He played great from start to finish and is now the odds-on favorite to win MVP this season according to FanDuel Sportsbook (+210 as of this writing).
"I wanted to come out and put on a show for everybody, and show what the excitement of the NFL can be," Burrow said. "And the NFL is really all about the stars and players making big time plays. And so you saw Ja'Marr Chase, you saw me, you saw Tee Higgins, you saw a lot of great players out there doing great things, and hopefully people took notice."
Oh, people are noticing. Burrow got his showcase on an international stage, and he'd love to do it again in 2027.
"We'll have to see where all the new places are next year. They're talking Mexico City. People are talking about Tokyo. So I don't know. We'll see," Burrow said about the series continuing in a new location.
Don't tell him they can count their chickens already this season. The goal is to score a touchdown every time they touch the ball. A lofty bar to clear in the NFL.
"Still, a lot of room to improve," Burrow noted. "Well, we didn't score on every single possession, so always room to improve, and it's never going to be perfect. So, a lot of room to grow and learn and improve from those reps."
"We have a chance to do everything that we set out to. We've worked really hard for a long time to put ourselves in this spot. We're 6-2. We have a big game next week against the Steelers for first place in the division. You know we're gonna have to go and get that one."
Burrow ranks first in the NFL in total touchdowns and is one game away from tying Peyton Manning's 2004 five-game run for the most consecutive outings with at least four total TDs scored.
He can do it in the most important game yet next Sunday night against the Steelers at home.

title: The Browns Must Make This One Major Move Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10th at 4:00 p.m.
So far this season, one thing has been very clear for the Cleveland Browns : the offensive line needs help.
If the Browns seriously want to make a playoff push or compete for their first AFC North title, they must try and make a move to renovate the guys up front.
Cleveland quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been sacked for an NFL worst 38 times.
Play after play, the blocking schemes break down, runs are unsuccessful, and both Sanders and Watson struggle to get the ball out in time.
However, the bigger problem is rooting out one lineman specifically.
Looking at PFF Numbers across the line for the starters, their overall grades are:
Other than Howard being pretty low for a starter, the rankings are right around average across the line.
Clearly, Cleveland needs help, but who should they trade for?
The best-case scenario for Cleveland is to go after a good lineman from a team severely underperforming. With this formula, Landon Dickerson stands out from the Philadelphia Eagles.
While it may take a lot to get him, Philly is now 2-7 in the season. If they are willing to get rid of the 28-year-old star for draft picks, Cleveland definitely has some to offer.
But how would it shake out with the offensive line?
This move would let a few changes occur. First, Austin Barber can move back to Tackle, which he primarily played in college. Next, Tytus Howard would be used as either a trade asset or a "6th man" lineman. Then, Dickerson and Johnson can decide who plays left and right guard, and go from there.
. @Jake_Trotter makes the case that the Browns should sell high and trade Shedeur Sanders before the deadline on Tuesday. Thoughts? https://t.co/4uPezsdtAq pic.twitter.com/uh1kDZnteG
At the moment, the Browns hold 11 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft, which include two selections in the first round.
While it would be ideal to hold on to both firsts, given a situation where Cleveland can dramatically improve, it would not be unlikely for them to use one of them.
As for players, while some have called for Shedeur Sanders or Jared Verse to be dealt, other names like Jerry Jeudy may come first.
Regardless of what they give up, the Browns seriously need some help on this offensive line

title: Browns Get Huge News on QB Deshaun Watson's Injury Status Ahead of Week 10
full_text:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson will be ready to return to play next week against the Houston Texans, according to ESPN Insider Jeremy Fowler.
However, that doesn't mean he is starting just yet.
The Browns fell short in Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints by a score of 23-22. Shedeur Sanders made his first start of the season in place of Deshaun Watson, who suffered a concussion in the loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The Browns' offense struggled mightily in the overtime thriller. The Browns' run game failed to get it going against a struggling Saints team. In addition, Shedeur Sanders was running for his life as the offensive line got beat several times, contributing to the offensive woes. Sanders finished the game with 297 passing yards and 2 touchdowns.
Browns head coach Todd Monken took the podium after the game and had this to say about Sanders' performance:
“I liked his confidence, like the way he operated; he looked very comfortable in terms of getting our guys in-and-out of the huddle, getting to the line of scrimmage was going to be half the battle this week, obviously, going there. And I thought he threw the ball, you know, extremely well...I do think there are positives to the amount of reps he got during the fall. I think obviously there was a two-month gap there, but I think there was enough there in terms of our system, how we do things.
"He’s been on every trip; he’s been on the headset during games. He hears every call that we make. So, if a player is diligent like he’s been, then you expect there to be some carryover.”
#Browns HC Todd Monken  on what he saw from Shedeur Sanders this week as he prepared to start against the Saints: “I liked his confidence, like the way he operated; he looked very comfortable in terms of getting our guys in-and-out of the huddle, getting to the line of… pic.twitter.com/ty3AvzmyoT
Despite Sanders' solid performance and compliments from Monken, the Browns could potentially still turn to Watson as the starting quarterback. The veteran would take on the Houston Texans, the team he played his first four seasons with.
When asked about the decision, Sanders told the media:
"...I control what I control, but what I think, in the grand scheme of things, don't really matter. I think being a great teammate, being a great whatever role I have on the team, I could do. Because you got to look at the bigger picture. We're out here connecting with each other, growing, learning in different areas.
"So if I'm playing, then, yes, I'm growing in this area. If I'm not playing, then I'm growing in this area. So, in every area you're growing, so you can't really ever look at the situation as negative."
#Browns QB Shedeur Sanders was asked if he thinks he earned the right to start again: "I think that's a setup question honestly...I control what I control, but what I think, in the grand scheme of things, don't really matter. I think being a great teammate, being a great… pic.twitter.com/FO1n3RH0Lh
The former 5th-round pick appears to be embracing whatever his role ends up being and will look to receive more opportunities moving forward.
The Browns will likely make an official decision in the coming days.

title: The Browns Have a Quarterback Decision That Could Shape the Franchise for Years
full_text:
After the Cleveland Browns ' week nine loss to the New Orleans Saints, the organization has a tough decision to make.
With an injured Deshaun Watson , Cleveland called on their backup quarterback, Shedeur Sanders , to try and win on the road. In the game, Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns, with no interceptions.
With Deshaun Watson in the last year of his contract, the Browns have three choices to make at the quarterback position. Let's go through each and look at what may happen.
Browns go for 2 and don’t convert. pic.twitter.com/l1j0BpTUzs
Despite the loss, there is definitely a case for some fans to argue Sanders should start over Watson.
However, if you take away some big plays primarily made by the offensive playmakers, there's an argument that Sanders did not nearly play to the level of Watson this season.
From what we saw on the field, Shedeur Sanders has taken a step forward compared to last year in regard to taking care of the football while still making big plays.
Yet one thing remains clear, he still needs more time to develop.
The optimism for the 2025 fifth-round pick is definitely high, but he will definitely need more time to shape into a true NFL starting quarterback.
Right now, Watson is on pace to receive yet another check from the Browns orgainzation.
However, even though he has done well this season, I would be wary of cutting the 31-year-old a big sum of money for a long period of time.
As we all know, Watson can go down at any moment. This week, he may go down midway through the season after playing an entire game.
The point here is that Cleveland must have a solid backup option for Watson. Whether they stick with Sanders or go for my final option, there has to be another guy in the QB room.
If there is someone the Browns have their eye on in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft, they should absolutely consider using one of their two first-round picks on him.
Looking at the quarterback situation for Cleveland, this move would set the Browns up nicely to do a couple of things. First, extend Watson.
This allows the organization to have a veteran quarterback to mentor the new rookie who has proved he can win games.
Next would be trading Shedeur Sanders.
After an impressive game against New Orleans, this may be all we see of Shedeur in 2026. On top of the fact that he was a Pro Bowl selection in his rookie season, Sanders has built a solid NFL resume that could land the Browns some valuable draft capital in a potential trade.
Then finally, train the rookie.
The Browns could have a legitimate chance to finally develop a first-round quarterback. If all goes according to plan, Cleveland may just find their franchise guy in the process while continuing to build assets and win games.
Shedeur Sanders was asked if he thinks he’s earned the opportunity to start again at QB for the Browns. His response. pic.twitter.com/apwzp83Jzr
At this point in the season, Deshaun Watson has been the only guy to prove he can win games for the Browns.
Unless a dramatic circus of events occurs, it seems as if the Browns will keep Watson for the foreseeable future.
It is all just a matter of how the Browns evaluate their quarterback room come the end of the season, and if they want to try and take a risk to find their franchise QB.

title: 2 Out-of-the-Box Trade Targets Who Could Help Fix the Browns’ Biggest Roster Weakness
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are not far off the top spot in the AFC North standings.
Following a rocky start to the 2026 campaign, the Browns turned the corner and are seemingly playing competitive football week in and week out.
But in order to round the final bend and make a push to finish the year strong, the front office will have to stay active at the trade deadline.
Recently, a report broke from Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer that the Browns would be considering adding more depth to the defensive line and a second option to the tight end room to pair with rising star Harold Fannin Jr.
Here are two out-of-the-box trades the Browns could end up making after taking Breer's reports into account:
Dallas Goedert isn't a blocking-first tight end.
But he has been a relatively solid one across his nine-year career in the NFL, even though that part of his game has declined with age.
The 31-year-old would bring the Browns a dual-threat tight end with plenty of experience and leadership in his back pocket. Not only can he still block decently well at his age, but he can also still get downfield and make plays for the offense.
This season, he has hauled in 26 catches for 258 yards and two touchdowns, with an average of 9.9 yards per reception. Just last season, he finished with a career-best 11 touchdowns.
From Week 10 through the end of the season, Goedert would place just a measly cap hit of $695,000 on the Browns, something that could be easily swallowed.
He is also on an expiring deal, so if the Browns ultimately don't end up liking his fit within the system, they could let him walk in free agency.
Trading for a player like Goedert would show that the Browns are investing in an offense that seems to be just a few pieces away from being really solid, all while giving Fannin Jr. a chance to learn and get more opportunities from a strong No. 2 beside him.
Looking to bolster the defensive line in a post-Myles Garrett era, the Browns are going to have to do a bit of work because of how poorly his replacement, Jared Verse , has played this season.
The freshly 26-year-old is currently on pace to have the worst season of his career, posting just 18 combined tackles, four tackles for a loss, zero sacks and six quarterback hits.
In order to free up more opportunities for him and help him break out of a slump, the Browns could look to stack up the talent around him. Trading for a player like the Washington Commanders' star defensive tackle Daron Payne would be a good option.
Payne is in his ninth season of NFL action, having posted a whopping 446 tackles, 67 tackles for a loss, 38 sacks and 86 quarterback hits across his career.
This season, he has 14 tackles, two for a loss, five quarterback hits and one sack. While he still has room to improve and return to the form he has shown in previous years, a fresh, new scenario could be exactly what he needs.
The Commanders are well below .500 and likely out of the hunt for a playoff spot, meaning for the right price, they would be willing to part with an aging lineman.
If the Browns toss a few picks the way of Washington, helping them pave a new path towards a rebuilding period this offseason, the deal could be done without even blinking.

title: 3 Takeaways as Browns Fall in OT to Saints, 23-22
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns were a successful two-point conversion away from victory Sunday afternoon against the New Orleans Saints. Alas, the team is now 5-4 and there is plenty to talk about following the loss.
This was a game that saw Shedeur Sanders start while Deshaun Watson watched from the sidelines. Sanders is certainly the top story from the game, but his play was not the reason the team lost.
Here are three takeaways that stand out as the Browns figure out where things went wrong in the 23-22 loss.
Sanders had a slow start in this game, but a look at the box score tells the complete story. He finished with 297 passing yards and two touchdowns, adding 28 yards as a rusher.
His best moment of the game was his 64-yard touchdown pass to KC Concepcion. The ball was a bit underthrown, but not enough to prevent the rookie receiver from making a play.
SHEDEUR TO KC CONCEPCION 64-YARD TD FOR THE LEAD! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Zs6x4Ko8SO
He even led an impressive scoring drive in overtime with a 39-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr., though the tight end did most of the work with a dominant run to the end zone. Add in some clutch runs, and Sanders showed he has the potential to be a starter in the league.
The negatives come with his five sacks and several missed reads, but he never turned the ball over and gave the Browns the lead late in the fourth quarter with his throw to Concepcion.
The defense simply couldn't hold on.
Sanders played well, just seemingly not well enough to suddenly seize the job from Watson. What he did do, however, was prove to everyone that he is indeed ready to step in and run this offense if Watson falters at all in the coming week.
Jared Verse did a lot of talking this past week and even called out his own teammates at one point. He had a chance against a 2-5 Saints team to change the narrative and show his dominance as a pass rusher.
Verse ultimately finished the game with two tackles and no other stats.
Sacks are not the only stat to focus on for defensive linemen. Yet it is still a concern that he has zero sacks through nine games. The worst part of all? Myles Garrett returned to action for the Los Angeles Rams and had three sacks on Sunday.
Audric Estime ran for 72 yards on only 15 carries to lead the Saints on the ground. For those who think his name is familiar, it's because he spent some time with the Browns earlier this year and even scored a touchdown in the win over the Baltimore Ravens.
The Saints as a team combined to run for 160 yards on 32 carries, which comes out to five yards per carry.
This comes one week after the Browns allowed the Pittsburgh Steelers to run for 200 yards. A week before that it was Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans going for 129 yards on the ground.
The defense is seemingly getting worse at stopping the run ever since holding Derrick Henry to 58 yards back in Week 6. Opposing coaches are scheming well, and the Browns' defense seems to have no answer. That is a major storyline to watch as the Browns prepare to host the Houston Texans next week.
Steve is a lifelong Cleveland sports fan who proudly wears his Guardians, Browns, and Cavs gear in his current home of Santa Barbara. He has covered Cleveland sports online for the past decade and is still waiting for the Browns to draft a QB who signs a second contract in town.

title: What Todd Monken Said When Asked Who Browns Starting QB Is Moving Forward
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns lost on Sunday, Nov. 8.
But it certainly wasn't for a lack of effort from starting quarterback Shedeur Sanders.
In a Week 9 road battle from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, the Browns fell to the Saints 23-22 in overtime. Going for two on the final play of the game, the Browns attempted to steal a win on the road, but a scramble from Sanders that led to a toss towards the end zone came up empty.
He did all he could; even if he had connected with a receiver, the Browns would have had to try again due to a holding call. All day long, such issues plagued Cleveland's offense.
11th penalty on #Browns . Shedeur Sanders pass to Denzel Boston for 2 incomplete. Final-OT #Saints 23 (3-5), #Browns 22 (5-4)
Even then, though, Sanders was able to muster up 297 yards and two touchdowns on 31 attempts, completing 19 of them.
When asked postgame what the plan was for the quarterback position moving forward, Browns head coach Todd Monken said that the team was not yet ready to answer such a question. He referenced the fact that the game had just ended.
"How long has it been? 30 minutes since the game ended? I'm not getting into quarterback," he said. "If we want to talk about Shedeur, we can talk about Shedeur."
He went on to praise the former Colorado Buffalo, stating that he was proud of the way he played , especially with the Browns being in enemy territory and being forced into an overtime game.
"I'm really proud of him...how hard he's worked since he's been here..." Monken was quoted saying in an X post from WEWS Reporter Camryn Justice, "to come in there and continue to battle...in terms of his work ethic, his diligence....he gave us a chance at the end...really proud of him."
#Browns HC Todd Monken on Shedeur Sanders: "I'm really proud of him...how hard he's worked since hes been here...to come in there and continue to battle...in terms of his work ethic, his diligence....he gave us a chance at the end...really proud of him."
No matter what lies ahead, though, for the 24-year-old second-year professional, he is going to maintain positivity and embrace the role that he is given.
"I control what I can control. I think being a great teammate, being a great whatever role I have on the team, I can do...I can't really complain about anything. I've got a great family. I've got a great team. I'm on the Browns, (we're) winning...the majority of the time.
"Today, we didn't get it done, though...but, there's nothing to complain about."
"I control what I can control. I think being a great teammate, being a great whatever role I have on the team, I can do...I can't really complain about anything. I've got a great family. I've got a great team. I'm on the Browns, (we're) winning...the majority of the time. Today,… pic.twitter.com/3NRiz8ZsBE
Such maturity shown by Sanders is a nice sigh of relief, especially considering comments earlier in the week put him in hot water. Entering Sunday's game, the Saints had taken some of his words as potential disrespect , which was shown during the game as Sanders' signature wrist-up celebration was mocked.
He even spoke about that situation postgame.
"I was never, ever throwing a shot. I apologize for that being taken out of context, but that's just how media is sometimes...but then, also, that's on me for not making it very clear and I understand that. I would never talk down on anybody, on any person.
"I understand how hard it is just to be in the league."
Sanders has put himself in the perfect position to be the Browns' franchise quarterback moving forward.
He took major leaps in different areas of his game compared to last season, spoke maturely following a close-knit loss and even emphasized that no matter what lies ahead, he will be ready to give his all.
The only question now is whether the Browns believe he is the right option moving forward.
When the Browns return to practice this next week, all eyes will be on the quarterback situation now that Sanders has complicated it again for Watson and the coaching staff.

title: Shedeur Sanders or Deshaun Watson? Evaluating What Comes Next For Browns QB Position
full_text:
Well, the Cleveland Browns expected to have this conversation at some point.
But for it to come up now, following Week 9 of the regular season, puts the coaching staff in quite a difficult situation.
Instead of the Browns changing quarterbacks due to struggles or on-field issues, the team has been thrown for a loop for a different reason.
Earlier in the week, starting quarterback Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol before ending up on the inactive list for the Browns' Sunday outing in New Orleans. Shedeur Sanders, the team's backup second-year signal caller, was then thrust into the starting role.
He looked sharp, passing for 297 yards and two touchdowns, all while adding 28 yards on the ground . There were obvious signs that he was still young and inexperienced, but he commanded the offense pretty well from the second half on. Unfortunately, even with some incredible plays down the stretch, the Browns weren't able to pull the win out in overtime, falling by one, 23-22.
And now, the Browns have a question: is it time for Sanders to take charge, or is this still Watson's offense?
A younger, more impressionable quarterback, Sanders is in just his second year of action at the NFL level.
And while there are areas he still needs to see improvements in, most notably his decision-making and processing after a play breaks down, he still has a lot of positives to his game. With more time, it is obvious there is something there with the 24-year-old.
Sanders seemingly has a higher ceiling, just off age alone, and turning to him for the rest of the season would show that the Browns are interested in continuing the youth movement across the board.
Such a decision would also allow the young players like Harold Fannin Jr., KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, all long-term staples of the offense, to continue growing chemistry with the expected future at the quarterback position.
The Browns are still in a position to play in the playoffs this season, though, above .500 by two games, which could result in the coaching staff returning back to the experience of Watson, even with Sanders showing promise.
In all likelihood, the Browns' coaching staff will probably give the reins back over to Watson. After all, he did enough to lead the team to a 5-3 record through the first eight weeks, and if it weren't for a freak concussion protocol incident, he would have been on the field Sunday.
On the 2026 season, the 31-year-old Watson has thrown for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions , all while completing 65.5% of his passes. In his two most recent starts, he has also tossed for back-to-back 300-yard performances
So far, he is putting up his best numbers since the 2020 season, the last year he was in Houston with the Texans.
With him finding such success, and still sitting on the Browns' biggest contract in franchise history, it only makes sense that the Browns continue to ride him out as the year dips into the back half.
And unfortunately, even if Sanders had thrown for 500 yards and five touchdowns, it seems that the goal was to always put Watson back under center when healthy.
Head coach Todd Monken, the rest of his staff and the front office will likely at least discuss the possibility of switching things up for a Week 10 duel with the Texans, but it is hard to imagine a world where Watson heads right back to the pine for the rest of his tenure with the Browns.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Inside Shedeur Sanders’ First Start of the 2026 Season: What Went Right and Wrong
full_text:
A new face started at quarterback for the Cleveland Browns in New Orleans against the Saints, but the play of the offense remained the same. Shedeur Sanders replaced Deshaun Watson as the play caller in his first start of the season.
Watson cleared concussion protocol, but Todd Monken believed in Sanders to get the road win.
The offense looked much the same under Sanders, with the pressure, lack of efficiency on the ground, and a burst late in the fourth quarter.
Todd Monken kept the reins in with Sanders . He only averaged 4.8 yards per completion in the first half. Sanders is at his best when he can push the ball downfield, but Monken made sure to mitigate any bad reads or high-risk throws, which resulted in a lot of check-downs. Sanders has zero turnovers in the conservative offense.
Sanders got to let loose in the third quarter when he threw a ball down the right sideline for Denzel Boston, allowing him to use his size to make a catch for 60 yards. The play of the day was in the fourth quarter when KC Concepcion was wide open for a 64-yard touchdown, momentarily putting them in the lead.
When Sanders had the opportunity to rip the football, the Browns had their two biggest plays of the season.
The new voice in the huddle led to a few miscues on offense . On a third-down drive, Quinshon Judkins ran the wrong play, and Sanders had to dive forward to get what he could.
The Browns had the ball at the one-yard line before the first half. On fourth down, the right guard pulled on a run to the left side, and Sanders opened up the wrong way. This caused a collision, delaying the handoff, and the run was stopped.
The offensive line continued to struggle. Sanders was sacked five times and had 10 rushes for 28 yards. Pressure got to him quickly, and he had to use his legs just to get back to the line of scrimmage. Sanders is not a runner like Watson , and he should not be running the ball as much as he did.
Spencer Fano gave up a sack to Chase Young on second-and-goal when the Browns were on the doorstep of scoring their first touchdown. On the next play, he got hit before the route developed and had to rush the throw, resulting in an incomplete pass.
Sanders was not completely faultless, as he held onto the ball too long at times. In the fourth quarter, he took a bad sack for an eight-yard loss when they were trying to eat up the clock.
With a minute left in the fourth quarter, Sanders had no choice but to get the ball downfield to his receivers. He made a great throw to Concepcion that was dropped on the first play of the drive, but on the very next play, he threw off his back foot while getting hit and connected with Jerry Jeudy to set up a game-tying field goal attempt.
INSANE: #Browns Pro Bowl QB Shedeur Sanders just made one of the most RIDICULOUS throws you will ever see. Sanders escaped pressure, rolled left, waited for his receiver to get open and delivered a perfect throw while getting ABSOLUTELY CRUSHED. WOW… pic.twitter.com/xdOylJZSJF
Harold Fannin Jr. and Sanders had a connection last season. Fannin did not have a catch in regulation, and the offense could have used his playmaking ability in the first three quarters. Then he came up with the catch of the day.
In overtime, the offense was uptempo, and Sanders got in a groove by staying in the pocket and using his check-downs. There was a blitz, and Sanders held tough and hit Fannin with a check-down, which allowed him to stiff-arm and stumble his way to a touchdown.
There were plenty of wrongs in New Orleans, and not enough rights to come away with a win. The offense looked like it did under Watson, with slow starts and then having to rely on fourth-quarter magic.
Sanders should get another start before the bye week, as the offense did not look any different under Sanders, and the Browns need to accurately evaluate him for the future.

title: Shedeur Sanders' Odd Comments Have Made Their Way Around Saints' Building
full_text:
Whether he meant to or not, Shedeur Sanders gave the New Orleans Saints something to motivate them a bit extra this weekend.
On Sunday, Nov. 8, the Cleveland Browns and Saints will clash from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans for a Week 9 matchup . Heading into the weekend, the Browns officially named second-year signal caller Sanders the starting quarterback, as Deshaun Watson works his way back from a concussion protocol issue.
While Sanders wasn't officially declared the starter until Friday, he was treated as such throughout the week.
When asked if he had been studying the Saints' defense and preparing for the game this weekend, the 24-year-old gave quite an odd answer.
"Yeah I seen a lot, when I smile just know that means something," he said with a chuckle. "I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying, I'm maturing, I could have gave that a decent answer but now I'm just gonna smile when it's some questions, you know."
"Yeah I seen a lot, when I smile just know that means something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying, I'm maturing, I could have gave that a decent answer but now I'm just gonna smile when it's some questions," - Shedeur Sanders on if he's studied the Saints defense. pic.twitter.com/IwiL3TE6u1
At first, it seemed that he was just blowing off the media, which he did a few different times back on Wednesday, but now, it seems the Saints took his comments as potential disrespect.
ESPN senior NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday morning, just hours before the game, that the clip of Sanders discussing the defense made the rounds in the Saints' building. Fowler continued that Saints head coach Kellen Moore had even referenced it during a meeting.
This clip of Shedeur Sanders discussing  the Saints defense made the rounds in New Orleans’ building. Head coach Kellen Moore referenced it in a meeting, per sources, while players openly discussed it to reporters. However Sanders meant it, New Orleans seemed to have some fun…
The confirmation just makes edge rusher Carl Granderson's comments on Friday make even more sense. Granderson, who has 5.5 sacks, five tackles for a loss and seven quarterback hits this season , said that the Saints feel the Browns have been "chirping a little bit."
"They've been chirping a little bit," he said. "We see what the quarterback said. [...] It's going to be a good game for sure."
While Sanders' awkward exchange with the media may not have been directed at the Saints in the way they ended up taking it, teams will always try to gain an edge wherever they can. And with how vocal the Browns have been the last few weeks, most notably edge rusher Jared Verse, it is hard to defend them.
The Browns, sitting 5-3 on the season and still in the hunt for the No. 1 spot in the AFC North standings, will look to put last week's loss behind them and turn to Sanders to lead the team to a victory on the road.
It's going to certainly be a trial-and-error experience, especially out of the gates, but Browns head coach Todd Monken is excited to see what Sanders can do.
“Oh yeah, I’m fired up," he said. "I’m fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn’t be?... This is what he’s wanted, right? He wants to be a starting quarterback in the NFL. Let’s go.
"Let’s let it rip. Let’s see what we got. We’re not holding anything back."

title: 3 Browns Who Need To Step Up Against the Saints
full_text:
In week nine of the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns are set to travel to New Orleans to take on the Saints.
While the matchup may seem easy for the Browns looking at each team's record, Cleveland is starting Shedeur Sanders for the first time this season.
With this game being a must-win for the Brown and Orange, here are three players who need to step up and help propel the team to victory.
As much as Browns fans want to see Shedeur Sanders throw for 300+ yards and 3 touchdowns, that's not what Cleveland needs.
So far this season, the Browns have struggled to run the ball. Looking at the stats , the Saints rank 29th in rushing yards allowed per game, with nearly 140.
For Judkins, he is averaging only about 3.4 yards per carry this season. Through eight games and 101 rushing attempts, the former Ohio State Buckeye has only 342 yards and three touchdowns.
This is a great opportunity for Cleveland to not only establish their run game going forward, but also control the game with their backup quarterback in.
Last year in their rookie seasons, Sanders connected more with Harold Fannin Jr. than any other receiving option on the team.
For numbers, in the six games Shedeur started, Fannin posted over 300 receiving yards and four touchdowns.
Now, there are two new rookie targets: KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. But let's not forget that Fannin is coming off a career-high 10 receptions for 154 yards last week against the Steelers.
When Shedeur has the ball in his hands, he needs to find his favorite target, who has been on fire over the past few weeks.
After an awful performance against the Steelers and a lackluster start to his Browns career, it's now or never for Jared Verse to step up.
While there are obviously high expectations for a player who was traded for Myles Garrett, Verse has yet to record a sack as a Brown and finished last week's rivalry matchup without a tackle.
Against a New Orleans team that has a young core down to their quarterback position, this is where Verse needs to stop leading with words and start leading with his play on the field.
A new hype video from Shedeur Sanders ahead of his first start of the season against the Saints 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/vuxrfiGjQ7
This game marks the halfway point of the season. If the Browns are serious about making the playoffs and even going for their first-ever AFC North title, this is one they must win.
It all depends on Todd Monken, Shedeur Sanders, and the supporting cast.

title: Ex-NFL GM Isn't Buying Cowboys' Rumored Stance on Trading George Pickens
full_text:
While there has been increasing speculation about the Dallas Cowboys possibly trading wide receiver George Pickens, the rumors suggest the Cowboys aren't interested in doing that.
Most recently, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Nick Harris put out a report stating the Cowboys have no plans to trade Pickens , and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport has said nothing is going on there.
However, former Tennessee Titans general manager Ran Carthon isn't buying that and he believes the Cowboys are "definitely exploring" trading their No. 2 receiver before the deadline.
"I think (the Cowboys) are definitely exploring it," Carthon said on CBS Sports. "Because, again, I think the writing is on the wall that they're not going to bring him back in terms of signing him to a long-term deal."
"So, if you're the Dallas Cowboys, why not explore being able to move on from (Pickens)," Carthon added. "Ryan Flournoy gives you that option now. He's a guy that's looking reliable, he's a guy that's going to show up, do his work, and he is one of the few guys on that offense as a whole who plays hard every single down."
The writing is on the wall that Pickens is not going to be back in 2027.
Co-owner Stephen Jones has already said in the past that it's tough to keep two high-paid wide receivers on the roster, which Dallas would be doing if it extends or even tags Pickens in 2027.
"The situation we have with George Pickens going alongside CeeDee.. I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said. "So, yeah. That's going to be a real difficult situation as we move forward. We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year."
It's clear the Cowboys might need an overhaul on defense again next offseason, or at the very least some improvements, and they will have to extend Joey Porter Jr. Having all of that money tied up in two receivers will leave the Cowboys with less wiggle room to accomplish everything they need to.
Furthermore, if the Cowboys do tag Pickens, we don't envision the veteran wideout simply accepting that again and entering another year without future certainty, so a hold out is more likely this time.
The tag-and-trade scenario is an option, but the Cowboys will have to keep that money on the books until he's moved and if they can't get a trade done quickly, that will hinder them in free agency.
So, when it comes down to it, the best courses of action are to either trade Pickens now or let him walk in free agency next offseason to get a compensatory pick, and only the former avenue guarantees what the Cowboys will get.
Some might view trading Pickens as waving the white flag on the season, but what exactly have the Cowboys accomplished with their star-studded duo at wide receiver? Nothing.
Unless Pickens can play cornerback or rush the passer, keeping him isn't going to make a dent in Dallas' playoff hopes in 2026.

title: Dallas Cowboys Breakout Star Expected To Miss Time After Career Game
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' running game saw a resurgence during Sunday's crucial Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium, but it may have come at a cost.
While starting running back Javonte Williams rushed for 101 yards and a touchdown, backup running back Tyler Goodson also came through with the best game of his career. Goodson rushed for a career-high 77 yards on 12 carries, but suffered a knee injury that is expected to sideline him for a few weeks.
During his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys COO Stephen Jones provided an update on Goodson, who was briefly sidelined on Sunday afternoon.
Jones revealed the team has its "fingers crossed" on the Goodson injury front. He added, "He’s got a real injury that unfortunately he’s probably gonna miss some time with .” To add to the Cowboys' injury concerns, star wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. are also battling lingering issues that the team will be forced to monitor throughout the week.
With the Goodson, Pickens, and Porter injuries, among others, the Cowboys could once again be short-handed when they take the field against the San Francisco 49ers next week. That comes at an unfortunate time with the team looking to build momentum entering a key stretch of the season.
Unlike the Indianapolis Colts, who appear to be preparing for a firesale ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the 49ers are a loaded team that will test the Cowboys on both sides of the ball.
Goodson's injury especially stings, because he provided some explosiveness to the running game as the offense was attempting to get back on track. Dallas has become more reliant on the run, but will now need to look elsewhere for additional depth until Goodson is healthy enough to return to the field.
Through the first nine weeks of the season, the Cowboys rank No. 21 overall in rushing, with 103.6 yards per game and 11 touchdowns. We'll have to see who the team calls on to contribute behind Williams for the foreseeable future as the week rolls on.

title: Cowboys' NFL Trade Deadline Blockbuster Hopes Take Massive Hit Thanks To Jerry Jones
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys found their way back into the win column in Week 9, closing out the Indianapolis Colts after suffering a strong scare at Lucas Oil Stadium. Now, it's time to turn everyone's attention to the NFL trade deadline .
There has been plenty of speculation about whether the Cowboys will make a move, thanks to the unpredictability of owner and general manager Jerry Jones .
Jones has hinted several times over the past few weeks and months about a potential deal, but any hope of making a splash took a major hit ahead of Sunday afternoon's game. Jones shared his thoughts on the trade deadline ahead of kickoff for Week 9, and it's not quite what Cowboys fans would want to hear.
As far as Jones is concerned, there won't be a lack of effort to make a deal, but it appears unlikely.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones with @KristiCowboy on the trade deadline: "You almost have to say if anything would be considered or working... if it's substantive for sure... you don't have any idea until you have the meeting of the minds and it's done. At this point I don't see it." pic.twitter.com/6TsVeBY1hy

title: Dak Prescott Shares Unpopular Opinion on Cowboys' Trade Deadline Needs
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have long been viewed as a potential buyer ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, and for good reason.
Owner Jerry Jones has said on several occasions that he is open to doing more to improve the defense , and he has said that even after the trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. We also know that, because of how poorly the defense has played, the unit could certainly use more help.
Credit to Jones, he has been aggressive in recent years in his quest to try and fix the defense, although so far that hasn't paid off, as the Cowboys sport one of the worst defenses in the NFL through nine games of the 2026 season.
While Jones remains open to making another move, quarterback Dak Prescott said after the Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts that he doesn't think the Cowboys need more help and they have everything they need on the roster as is to get to the playoffs.
“Yeah, I do (think the Cowboys have enough). Obviously, credit Jerry [Jones], credit the front office and those guys. If you can always add, go do it. Even if you think you have enough, if you can make sure you have enough and get better, go do it. I encourage that," Prescott said.
"But yeah, they've done a hell of a job with the team they put together. It's on us now. Period.”
Cowboys fans would probably beg to differ given everything that has transpired this season.
While we wholeheartedly disagree with Prescott's belief Dallas has enough on the roster right now to get to the playoffs, we aren't the least bit surprised he feels this way.
You're rarely, if ever, going to hear a quarterback say his team needs more help, as that would be a public admission he doesn't think his team is good enough, which is a bad look for a team leader, at least with his own teammates.
But the fact of the matter is, the Cowboys have shown zero indication they have enough to make the postseason, and specifically when it comes to the defensive side of the ball.
Entering Week 10, the Cowboys rank 30th in total yards allowed, 18th in passing yards, 31st in rushing yards and 25th in points.
Well, the Cowboys could use more help on the coaching staff, but since we know Dallas isn't going to make any changes there, that's a moot point.
One of the biggest issues has been edge rusher , where the Cowboys have gotten just 7.5 sacks out of the group.
The inability to finish off pressures has exposed Dallas' suspect secondary and has allowed opposing passing attacks to pick apart Christian Parker's lackluster zone defense.
Because of injuries, two other positions the Cowboys could explore are safety and linebacker.
Jalen Thompson remains on injured reserve and, P.J. Locke just suffered his second concussion in as many games. DeMarvion Overshown is injured yet again and simply can't be relied upon.
All that said, we think if the Cowboys do have an appetite for a trade, it will come at edge rusher, but only if it's for a true game-changing addition because that's exactly what this defense needs.

title: Cowboys' George Pickens Linked To AFC Juggernaut Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
We are approximately 24 hours away from the NFL trade deadline, and all eyes will be on whether the Dallas Cowboys and Jerry Jones decide to pull off a blockbuster move for the second straight year.
Dallas is riding high after a crucial win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday afternoon, and must now decide whether they want to push their chips into the center of the table and go all-in on the season in a wide-open NFC East.
Of course, the team could also go the opposite route, which has led to a lot of speculation about whether the team could decide to trade away star wide receiver George Pickens .
The latest speculation comes from Michael Robinson of the NFL Network , who believes the team should be sellers and ship Pickens to the Kansas City Chiefs.
George Pickens to the Chiefs? 🤔 Michael Robinson believes the Cowboys should be sellers ahead of the trade deadline 👀 pic.twitter.com/9MSZQQgH5Z
Pickens has been slowed by injuries this season and was held out of Sunday's Week 9 showdown, which led to some speculation that the team was preserving Pickens to keep him healthy for a trade. Of course, the team has been adamant that they plan to keep Pickens for the long run, but you can never take anything off the table when Jerry Jones is involved.
As for Robinson's suggestion, Pickens would give the Chiefs a No. 1 receiver option that they desperately have been lacking.
"I'm going to go seller first, Dallas Cowboys, the buyer, the Kansas City Chiefs, and I'm talking George Pickens," Robinson said. "It's going to take a lot of stuff for something like that to happen. George Pickens is one of the ones, right? Like, he's one of those guys at the wide receiver position. When I look at Kansas City, man, I mean, wide receivers have led them in receiving only three out of eight games this season. A lot of times it's Travis Kelce, the matchup nightmare on their offense.
"Could you imagine if Patrick Mahomes had an uber-talented receiver, uber-talented ex-receiver that he can go three-by-one and watch the coverage completely rotate to him? You think Kenneth Walker, who's already having a hell of a year, you think he wouldn't like this guy to be involved in that offense as well? And again, you put a deep threat like that on his office, I think the Kansas City Chiefs, that would be the Chiefs, though. I like that. I think that's a great call."
Giving a weapon as dangerous as Pickens to Mahomes would be a major problem for the league, but it doesn't seem like it's too likely to happen. And, for the sake of the Cowboys, let's hope Pickens keeps the star on his helmet past Tuesday evening.

title: Cowboys Given New Deadline Target After Jets Defender Requests Trade
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have a new candidate to target for a trade ahead of the deadline on Tuesday.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald has requested a trade.
The reason behind McDonald's frustration has to do with his lack of playing time. McDonald has seen his snaps go down from 66% the past two seasons to 46% in 2026.
"Jets pass-rusher Will McDonald IV has informed the team that he wants to be traded, sources say," Rapoport stated. "McDonald has played sparingly this season and is extremely frustrated with his usage."
The reduction in snaps for McDonald comes as a result of the Jets adding three edge rushers during the offseason, including David Bailey, Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare.
McDonald still has one more year left on his contract , so the Jets are not really in any rush to trade him, although it's conceivable they could get more for the former first-round pick now since McDonald won't be a rental, and teams tend to be a bit more desperate at the deadline.
The Cowboys badly need more help at edge rusher because the guys they brought in just simply haven't been good enough.
Dallas has gotten 7.5 sacks out of their edge rushers this season, and new additions like Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence and Von Miller have combined for four of those.
In all, the Cowboys have 17 sacks, tied for the 11th-fewest in the NFL.
What has made the Cowboys' lack of pass-rush juice off the edge even more glaring is the lackluster coverage Dallas has played, so the Cowboys desperately need more production to help fix that issue.
McDonald has the ability to provide it after posting 18.5 sacks combined over the past two seasons. He has just three in nine games this season, but that would still be tops among Dallas' EDGE group.
We suspect McDonald might cost a fourth-round pick, which the Cowboys have in 2027, although Dallas' draft stockpile is already depleted thanks to trades in recent years. If the Cowboys traded their 2027 fourth-rounder, they would be left with just three selections next year.
One thing the Cowboys will have to weigh is just how much they think a player like McDonald can help their struggling defense.
We've maintained that Dallas needs an elite edge rusher to even have a chance to save the unit, and even then that might not be enough.
McDonald certainly isn't elite, so the Cowboys might not think it's worth it to drain another draft pick to acquire him.
