title: Grades: Detroit Lions Offense Is Sluggish, Defense Carries Team
full_text:
The Detroit Lions notched their fourth-consecutive win Sunday, defeating the Miami Dolphins to move to 6-2 on the season.
Detroit looked sluggish for most of the afternoon, as the team didn't have the same intensity that they had the previous two weeks in pivotal divisional showdowns. However, they were able to make just enough plays to keep a competitive Dolphins team at bay.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Sunday's game.
Jared Goff had one of his worst performances of what has been a solid season. Against a Dolphins defense that had struggled coming into the game, Goff looked sluggish and was under constant duress throughout the game.
He had a pass tipped and intercepted on the team's second drive, and was sacked three times in the first half. Sunday marked the first time this season he had been held without a passing touchdown, and his ESPN quarterback rating of 17.7 is by far his worst mark of the season.
Jahmyr Gibbs got off to a fast start, and nearly scored on a crafty Wildcat play when he dashed around the left end but unfortunately stepped out. He was able to reach the end zone in the second half, but was held in check for most of the game.
Jeff Hafley, Miami's first-year head coach, was the architect of Green Bay's game plan last year as their defensive coordinator when they kept Gibbs largely under wraps. He once again had a solid plan, as Gibbs finished with 74 yards on 20 carries.
Sione Vaki, who was questionable to play with an ankle injury, recorded 14 yards on three carries.
Amon-Ra St. Brown once again led the way with eight catches for 86 yards despite dealing with a rib injury throughout the week. Jameson Williams was kept under wraps, as he had just one catch which happened to be a 31-yard grab.
Isaac TeSlaa helped convert a fourth-down on the team's first drive with a nine-yard catch, but that was his only catch of the game. He was also penalized for holding on an end-around run by Jameson Williams that went for a first-down.
DeAndre Carter also got in the mix, recording his first catch of the season for five yards in the third quarter.
Sam LaPorta was consistent, with 32 yards on four catches. It was a good bounce-back performance after a pair of quiet games against divisional opponents.
Elsewhere, the Lions didn't get any other receiving production from their other tight ends. Tyler Conklin got one target, while Brock Wright didn't get in the mix in the passing game on Sunday.
Detroit made a move on Sunday, as Miles Frazier joined the starting lineup as Christian Mahogany was benched for what Dan Campbell called disciplinary reasons. Frazier didn't play well in his first extended opportunity of the season, as he struggled mightily both in the run and passing game.
It was an overall rough day for Detroit across the board up front. Rookie Blake Miller struggled in his matchups with Chop Robinson, who entered the league as one of the top-performing defensive ends in terms of pressure rate.
Goff was sacked three times in the first half, but the unit did rebound and didn't allow a sack in the second-half. The biggest question moving forward will be whether or not the change from Mahogany to Frazier is permanent.
The Lions didn't get a ton of flashy production in the first half, as they didn't record a sack or a tackle for loss in the first two quarters. However, the defense fired it up in the latter half of the game with rookie Derrick Moore leading the charge.
With starter DJ Wonnum sidelined, Moore got a larger opportunity in Sunday's game and made the most of it. He recorded two sacks, while Alim McNeill notched another as well to help keep the mobile Malik Willis in check.
Detroit's defense allowed just 77 rushing yards on 21 attempts from the Dolphins, with the longest being an end-around from Kevin Coleman that went for 16 yards.
The linebacking corps was without its leader for the first time, as Jack Campbell was placed on injured reserve. As a result, Derrick Barnes stepped into the leadership role that was vacated, and Malcolm Rodriguez paced the defense with eight total tackles.
Barnes had a tackle for loss, while Trevor Nowaske and Joe Bachie each recorded a tackle of their own.
The Lions were also down a key starter in their secondary, as D.J. Reed was out with a hip injury. This meant more opportunities for Ennis Rakestraw and Rock Ya-Sin along with Roger McCreary. It was a tough start for McCreary, who was on the wrong end of both of Miami's two longest passing plays in the first half.
Rakestraw had a tough missed tackle when trying to get a third-down stop. Brian Branch led the secondary with seven total tackles, including four solos, while Roger McCreary had six.
Chuck Clark has proven to be a nice veteran addition, as he recorded his second interception of the season on Miami's first possession of the second half.
On one hand, the Lions got a perfect 4-for-4 performance from Jake Bates and an exciting fake punt completion from Jack Fox to Tay Martin. The fake punt was Fox's fifth completion of his career, with all five going for first downs.
However, they also gave up a 43-yard gain on a Dolphins fake punt from Bradley Pinion to running back Kaytron Allen. Additionally, Bates took a penalty for kicking a ball well short of the landing zone. Add in a penalty on Christian Izien on a punt return, and it was a mixed bag of a performance for Detroit's special teams units.
The Lions came out very slowly in Sunday's game, to the point where head coach Dan Campbell voiced his frustrations at halftime with the team's performance. The offense couldn't get going consistently, and while the defense didn't allow a touchdown they gave up some big plays.
After a pair of emotional wins against NFC North opponents, the Lions sputtered against the lowly Dolphins. It isn't a win that will inspire a ton of confidence moving forward based on how they looked, but it's their fourth in a row and the team has a lot of momentum.
Next week, the Lions are traveling to Germany for their international showdown with the New England Patriots. It's the start of a big stretch , with a game against Tampa Bay and then a Thanksgiving showdown with the Bears waiting in the wings.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Detroit Lions Beat Dolphins
full_text:
Here is a transcript of everything Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after his team defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, to improve to 6-2 on the season.
“All right, let me start here. A lot of what we said was, man, let's win number six for 46. And we did that today. We got that done. I'll start there. I told them as a coach, there's things that we need to clean up. We can be much better. We created some of our own issues at times. Ultimately, we played pretty dang good defense. And then offensively, when we needed it, man, we hit some explosives. That one drive – within three plays, we scored and then we finished the game out on the hole. So, that was a good thing. As a human being, as their teammate, I'm unbelievably proud of them. For everything that this week has been, this has not been easy. It's not been easy on anybody. And for them to come in here and lock back in and fight, get in a dogfight with the team, which by the way, Coach Hafley is doing a hell of a job. That team plays hard. The tape said so. We knew it would be that way. And hang in there and do what you have to do in the second half to finish this game. I'm unbelievably proud. So we'll take that. It's win number six.”
“Well, we've cleaned a lot up and guys are trusting what they're being taught . They're executing it, and then with that execution comes confidence. So their confidence has grown and they're trusting one another. That's always going to help you play better. Once we tighten a few things up on the back end, our front's been playing at a pretty high level. So we've been able to shut down the run and we can get to the cue. It took us a minute. We couldn't quite get there in the first half, second half, though, we started making some hay. So that's a big thing. I'm proud of those guys. We use all of them, Rock and Dorsey and Rakestraw and obviously McCreary and obviously our safeties, man. That was a huge pick by Chuck, that was big time. Chuck's a rock for us back there. And obviously BB (Brian Branch) and Abney. I mean, we use every one of those DBs, they’re in there, so proud of those guys.”
“I just think it was the whole week I mentioned this, it was prepare and play like Jack, and just understand, it kind of felt like we owed it to him, in a sense. It's all we could do because I mentioned this before, he'll take the prayers, but he didn't want the pity. He didn't want you wasting the time thinking about him. He certainly doesn't want us to go and not play our best ball and lose a game. So that's what we could do and we wanted to honor him. There's nothing easy about it. This is hard because you do want to talk about it and acknowledge it, because if you just brush it under the rug that's not fair. I mean, the guy means too much to us, and so the guys did that. Look, we got a very strong locker room. We got great leaders, man. Our captains and the leaders on this team, the core of this team, the coaches did a hell of a job. We bonded together and ultimately we found a way to win a game. And that's important here, especially coming off of that. It was emotional.”
“Well, that was just, that was team rules , Mahogany. It was really that simple. Miles deserved his opportunity, and he got it. And it doesn't mean it stays that way, but that was that was the way it was going to be today.”
“He wants to come back. Are you surprised by anything from Jack? I mean, that's Jack. Jack is all about the goal in front of me and I'm going to attack that goal and I'm going to destroy that goal and then I'll move on to the next thing. So ultimately, as you know, he's just the way he's wired. He will do any and everything it will take to overcome any perception of adversity. That's the way he is.”
“Yeah, and that was big. And look what it did. That’s the thing. We finally got some. And honestly, we had some guys open early and we couldn't hold up in protection long enough. We got edged on a couple of things where we can be better. And I thought we tightened some stuff up the second half. Some of it is you watch tape. I mean, we got a lot of crossover and certainly this week. Chop and those guys, Uche, they bring it off the perimeter and Sieler's slippery inside. He's big, so they're running some of these games and it took us a minute. They got speed now. They got speed on the perimeter and it's a little different. They play hard and it just took us a minute to get in it and figure a few things out, but once we did, we tightened it up.”
“That's what, that's what we're about . It’s why we got these guys because we think they can they can help us and they bring something. I mentioned this before, D-Moore, with every rep he's going to get better. That's how he is. The more reps he gets, the better he gets. He got a pretty good dose today and he's improving. That's important. So he stepped up for us. Hutch is Hutch. He does what he does and he uses up a lot of resources for their offense. So you got to win. Mac won today. D-Moore won today. I thought Sky (Skyler Gill-Howard) got after today. There was some stuff out there effort wise that I was so impressed with. Running the quarterback down, Sky did it, Tyleik did it. I love the way those guys hustle up front. We can get an edge, we can stop the run, and we hustle, man. We run out of the stack, that's big time. Kacy’s doing a hell of a job with those guys.”
“Well, I think time, right? Time heals everything. The longer this goes, every day he heals a little bit more, right? We’re a little bit more removed getting ready for the next thing in front of us, and so the thought of those two things is going to help you. We're never going to forget what that is and we got a locker in there set up for him. That locker's traveling, and we'll do our part. But at the same time, knowing that he is improving, he's getting better every day, that helps us get along with what we're doing.”
“I mean, you see it. You see it firsthand. It's a difference maker. We've got an edge and we got a guy in the middle who can get after it. We got more than that, by the way. We’ve got a little bit of everything. But those two guys, they do require resources. You have to take notice of where those two guys are at. And Mac is taking advantage of some of these where at some point in time, if you can give one of those guys a one-on-one somehow, some way, they got to win and they're winning. Mac is winning right now. I'm just proud. I'm proud of all those guys because they get after the run game and then they earn the right to get after the quarterback. That's how they treat it and that's what they're doing right now. So Mac is huge. He's playing some of the best football. He's playing the best football I've ever seen him play. He's locked in. He's wired right. He's one of our veteran guys. It's hard to believe we had all these pups and they're full grown. They're full grown and they're our dudes and they're playing at a high level right now.”
“We just felt like it was the right time. As always, we practice a lot of stuff and it just felt like it was the right time. Really there on that one, I probably should have gone safe. When they hit us on that it was a good call by them. We’d just scored, they got all three time outs, two scores, eight minutes whatever that was. I’ll take that. It was a good job by them. That certainly wasn’t on our guys, that was on me. But listen, sometimes that’s the way it goes. You try and get (DeAndre) Carter to return and they got us.”
“You know what? I didn't even get into that. And honestly, anything football, I didn't bring up anything football. All right, so anything that came, that was from him. I didn't bring anything about that up, me personally. You know what I mean? Jack's a stud, man. That's why it's just unbelievable. Family.”

title: 6 Winners, 5 Losers From Lions Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions squared off against the Miami Dolphins. The Lions were looking to continue their winning ways against a scrappy Miami team. While the Dolphins only had one win on the season, they had played in four straight one possession games.
The Lions were also looking to win the game for Jack Campbell, with the linebacker on injured reserve following a terrifying injury last weekend.
After a slow start, the Lions inched their way ahead with field goals until a fourth down Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown gave Motown a two-score lead. Here is who won the day in Miami.
With DJ Wonnum out of the game following a concussion last week, Moore saw an extended run. The Michigan product responded in a big way, forcing a Malik Willis throwaway in the second half after failing to wrap up the Dolphins’ quarterback, before getting a sack on third down in the red zone in the fourth quarter.
Moore and the entire defensive front was disruptive, and the Lions’ rookie second-round pick showed glimpses of what the staff saw when selecting him this spring. For the EDGE, it was his first career sack.
Moore got his revenge for being shook off his first two career sacks later in the game, bringing down Willis for another sack after the quarterback broke free from Aidan Hutchinson and Alim McNeill.
While it was not a game where Gibbs put up over 100 total yards, the running back provided what turned into the game-sealing touchdown at the end of the third quarter, pushing the Lions out to a two score lead.
Gibbs was stout with 61 yards on 16 carries on a day where the Miami defense overperformed expectations.
Another week, and another week of Alim McNeill making an impact on the game. The defensive tackle dismantled the Dolphins’ offensive line, tallying a sack of Malik Willis and providing pressure to make the Liberty product uncomfortable.
Overall, it was a strong day for the defensive tackle, and it is clear to see that the NC State alum’s extension was a wise investment by Brad Holmes. McNeill got his hands on Willis in the Dolphins’ last chance to keep the game close, but the quarterback broke free only to be sacked by Derrick Moore.
While the Lions offense stalled out, Jake Bates was relied upon to kick field goals and keep the Lions ahead on the scoreboard. Bates provided, going a perfect four-of-four on his field goals alongside an extra point on the sole offensive touchdown.
None of the kicks were the most challenging for the Arkansas kicker, as his longest only came from 43 yards out, but his consistency helped keep the game out of reach of the Dolphins. It was not a perfect game for Bates, as he did have a kickoff out of bounds, but his 13-point effort easily outweighs that.
Clark provided one of the turning points of the game, as the veteran defensive back intercepted Malik Willis to set up another field goal to keep Detroit in charge. That interception and ensuing field goal provided a spark for the Lions, as they rattled off three straight scoring drives to end the underdog Dolphins’ hopes.
On the day, Clark contributed 5 tackles, a pass defended, and his interception.
Gill-Howard’s stat line does not stand out, but if anyone were to ask Malik Willis about the big No. 50 on field, Willis would recognize him. Gill-Howard showed his speed during the game, chasing down Malik Willis and cutting off pursuit angles multiple times.
In the first half, Gill-Howard forced a throwaway, shoving Willis out of bounds after the quarterback barely released it. On Derrick Moore’s first career sack, Gill-Howard was set to sack Willis if Moore did not finish the job.
Additionally, Gill-Howard forced a holding call when in pursuit during the second half, forcing the Dolphins to later settle for a field goal.
McCreary did not have a strong start to the game , as the corner was targeted routinely in the first half. The corner allowed two of the longest Willis passes of the day, a pair of 13- and 14- yard receptions on two drives that resulted in field goal attempts.
In a day where the defense was stout, McCreary had an off day and did not meet the standards against a lowly Miami offense.
TeSlaa is a player that gets limited opportunities in the passing game, with productive pass catchers Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Sam LaPorta all available. However, what TeSlaa is known for is his blocking ability that allows Drew Petzing to call more runs in 11 personnel.
On Sunday, TeSlaa did not meet his own standards, having a quiet receiving day with 1 catch for nine yards while also being whistled for a holding call while blocking.
On Sunday, Miles Frazier got the surprising start over Christian Mahogany for disciplinary reasons. It is safe to say that Frazier did little to win the job against the Dolphins defense, as the lineman was pushed back multiple times, including a bad tackle for loss.
Additionally, Frazier was whistled for a false start. A questionable decision to move away from Mahogany only worked worse after Sunday’s contest.
Mahogany was relegated to special teams duty on Sunday, which was later revealed to be for a violation of team rules. The linemen was performing at a high level during his third season, but it is apparent he is toeing the line of Dan Campbell’s patience.
Although Frazier does not have an assured start waiting for him in the Munich game, nor did the LSU product’s play win the job, it is apparent that Mahogany has work to do to get out of the team “dog house.”
Williams did not have a bad day, but it was a quiet day. After five touchdowns in three games, Williams was held in check with only one catch and one carry on Sunday.
Williams did have a big 31-yard catch to start the Lions’ lone touchdown drive, but also had saw a pass bounce off his hands in the first half. The Lions’ former first round pick did not have the day that was expected after a massive three-week outing.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Detroit Lions Reveal Surprise Reason OL Benched
full_text:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell made an interesting change to his starting lineup Sunday afternoon in Miami.
He decided to start second-year pro Miles Frazier at left guard over regular LG Christian Mahogany, relegating Mahogany to special teams duty.
In the postgame, Campbell reiterated that Mahogany was scratched due to a violation of “team rules.”
Furthermore, according to the Lions flagship radio network, Mahogany also previously failed a conditioning test during training camp.
Consequently, Campbell's patience with the offensive lineman has likely evaporated.
Mahogany, a third-year pro, had started six of the Lions’ first seven games at left guard. He missed Detroit's Week 2 primetime tilt with the Buffalo Bills with a hip injury.
Entering the Lions’ battle with the Dolphins Sunday, Mahogany was rated the 10th-best guard in the entire NFL by Pro Football Focus. He had earned a 79.6 overall grade from PFF, including a 78.3 pass-blocking mark (seventh-best) and a 74.7 run-blocking grade (14th-highest).
Meanwhile, Frazier clearly was not ready for “primetime.”
He did little to seize the opportunity from the jump, being called for a holding penalty on the Lions’ third offensive series of the game. And it came one play after Jack Fox pulled off a fake punt and found Tay Martin toward the sideline for an 11-yard gain and subsequent first down.
The Frazier penalty ultimately was a drive killer, and led to a Fox punt just four plays later.
Frazier never found his rhythm, either, and looked like a “fish out of water” as both a pass-protector and run-blocker the majority of the Week 9 contest . In fact, he allowed multiple pressures in the first half alone to Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler.
“Miles deserved his opportunity, and so he got it,” Campbell said after the game. “It doesn't mean it stays that way, but that was the way it was going to be today.”
It will be interesting to see who gets the nod at left guard a week from now in Germany. The Lions are set to square off with the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots in the Week 10 international clash.

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 19-9 Victory Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had so much more to handle than a game plan against the Miami Dolphins this week.
A devastating injury to linebacker Jack Campbell created some adversity, but head coach Dan Campbell noted during a pregame interview that the focus for the team was on improving and responding to the challenge.
"I think it is just about, look we've improved really every week. Different ways, but we have improved and that's been it," Campbell said i "You win three games in a row, we've got two in the division, we've got to continue to improve. I think, really, I think a lot of this is we've got to emotionally get back into this. Let's call it what it is, what happened to Jack, that's hard. We've got to rally back up and get back to business, because that's what Jack would want."
After 60 minutes of hard-fought action against an AFC East foe, Detroit advanced their record to 6-2.
Here are the main takeaways from the Lions' 19-9 victory against the Dolphins.
Detroit was able to move the football effectively in the first quarter. A surprise decision saw Miles Frazier start the game at left guard in place of Christian Mahogany.
After winning the opening coin toss, Detroit elected to start the game on offense.
Both Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs were both ready from the start, as Detroit moved the football effectively.
As Detroit neared the goal line, the Dolphins defense tightened up . Detroit's opening drive ended when linebacker Josh Uche sacked Jared Goff, forcing the Lions to kick a 28-yard field-goal.
On Detroit's next drive, the Dolphins were able to pick off the veteran signal-caller for only his second interception of the season.
Miami capitalized and tied the game at 3-3.
What a throw, @MrJackFox pic.twitter.com/n3m4I5phod
After the Dolphins stopped the Lions again on their third offensive drive, Campbell dialed up a trick play to try and gain a litle momentum.
Punter Jack Fox, who was named Special Teams Player of the Week in Week 8, fired a laser to Tay Martin to extend a drive.
Unfortunately, the interior of Detroit's offensive line struggled on the first three offensive possessions and throughout the first half.
It was reported Frazier playing a decision made by coaches, but the former LSU lineman looked outmatched in his 2026 season debut.
Miami was able to record three early sacks, as Detroit started to show a negative impact of not having Cade Mays and Christian Mahogany in the lineup early in the game.
The Lions' offense sputtered throughout the first half, amassing just six points. However, the defense was able to navigate some of the tough spots they were put in and ultimately allowed the Lions to go into the locker room with the lead.
After forcing a three-and-out on Miami's first possession, the defense was forced into a difficult situation when Goff was intercepted. However, they were able to limit the damage to just a field goal.
Late in the first half, the Dolphins drove down the field thanks in part to a 16-yard end-around from Kevin Coleman and a 14-yard pass from Malik Willis to Malik Washington. However, a holding penalty moved them back, and Zane Gonzalez's field goal attempt to tie the game on the final play of the first half hit the right upright and bounced no good.
The Dolphins out-gained the Lions 123-120 in the first half, as the Lions' defense did not record a tackle for loss.
The Dolphins started the second half with the football and seeking to avenge an error that prevented the team from tying the game at the end of the second quarter.
Unfortunately, Willis was too aggressive and turned the football over.
On a pass intended for wideout Washington, Willis was picked off by veteran Chuck Clark. He was able to return the ball from the Lions own 40 all the way to the Dolphins 26-yard line.
Clark tied his single-season career high with two picks, as he also accomplished that feat back in 2021. His 35 interceptions return yards this season are the most he's had in a season in his career.
Miami's defense tightened up with Detroit again in the red zone, as a Bates 33-yard field-goal extended their lead to 9-3.
Detroit Lions defense steps up pic.twitter.com/nMMf89NQWu
As the defensive battle continued in the third-quarter, Detroit was finally able to extend their lead to 16-6 with a touchdown scoring drive, after the Dolphins trimmed the lead to 9-6.
Goff led the Lions on a six-play, 65-yard drive that featured a deep pass to Jameson Williams for a gain of 31 yards to kick off the drive.
On the following play, Goff connected with St. Brown for a gain of 17-yards.
On 4th-and-1, Campbell again elected to go for it. Gibbs took the handoff and scampered eight-yards to give the Lions a 10-point lead.
Gibbs is the first player in franchise history to produce 11 or more touchdowns in four-straight NFL seasons.

title: Jack Campbell Is Determined To Return: Make Sure House Is Taken Care Of
full_text:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell told head coach Dan Campbell earlier this week he was determined to get back to playing football.
The former first-round draft pick remains hospitalized in Detroit, after he was carted off the field in the second half against the Minnesota Vikings.
In a CBS pregame sideline report, Melanie Collins shared, "Lions linebacker Jack Campbell remains hospitalized in Detroit, where we're told that he continues to improve following the neck injury he suffered last Sunday against the Vikings. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard and the linebackers arrived at Hard Rock Stadium today wearing No. 46 jerseys in honor of him. That is the mentality going forward. Prepare and play like No. 46.
"Dan Campbell told us he had the opportunity to see Jack in the hospital this week. He said he is doing well. He's improving. He doesn't want anyone's tears or sympathy and he is determined to get back on this football field, telling Dan Campbell, 'Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back.' That is what the players and coaches are hanging on to this week."
Initially, the team was in shock and only concerned themselves with the overall well-being of their fallen teammate.
As the week progressed and updates started to be reported, the team returned to focusing on the task at hand.
The talented linebacker did not want his teammates to focus on him or his injury, but instead to get back to focusing on winning every week.
Campbell's No. 46 jersey was hung up in the Lions' locker room in Miami this week.
“I think every day we've gotten better," said Campbell earlier this week. "We're getting a better handle on this. Jack continues to improve, which is all great news. And there again, this is about, man, how would he prepare? How would he play? Those are the standards for us going into this game. We owe it to him.”
Teammates Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske and Malcolm Rodriguez are now tasked with filling in during Campbell's absence.
The team also signed linebacker Joe Bachie to the active roster and added K.J. Britt also.

title: How Long Will Josh Jacobs Be Out After Surgery And How Will Packers Pivot?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs’ broken finger will require surgery that will keep him out of the lineup for the next couple games, a source told Packers On SI.
Jacobs was injured while stiff-arming Patriots safety Craig Woodson on his fourth carry of the game. His right ring finger got caught in the defender’s facemask.
Josh Jacobs got his right hand caught in the defenders face mask. I’m curious if it’s his hand or his fingers. It almost looks like one of his fingers snaps. pic.twitter.com/hngCa0PdG6
“It looked nasty,” Jacobs told reporters after Green Bay’s 45-27 victory. “It look a lot better now than what it did, but we’ll see. We’ll see how it goes.”
Jacobs and the team opted for surgery rather than trying to have him play with a splint or some other protective appliance, which would hinder him in warding off defenders and for ball security.
Jacobs tried to play through the injury.
“That’s what we was trying to do during the game,” he said. “We was just trying to figure out a way if I can still go, and the biggest thing is just being able to grip the ball. Catching is obviously going to be tough, but just being able to grip the ball, but we’re going to see. I know it’s broke, but I don’t know the extent.”
The Packers will host the Vikings in a big rivalry rematch on Sunday. Then comes an unusual schedule, with what’s essentially back-to-back mini-byes rather than a traditional bye week. There will be an extended break before the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Rams and then another extended break before the Dec. 6 game at the Saints.
It’s possible Jacobs could be back for the game against New Orleans, according to a source. If not, the Packers will host the Bills on Dec. 13.
The Packers’ running game sputtered during Jacobs’ six games on the exempt list, and it wasn’t much better during his two games back in the lineup. He carried four times for 5 yards before the injury.
Against New England, Jacobs, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong were the running backs with MarShawn Lloyd (knee) inactive and Chris Brooks (ankle) not activated from injured reserve.
With Jacobs set to miss at least the next couple games, the Packers will have to shuffle the deck at running back.
After spending four games in the doghouse due to a fumble at Tampa Bay in Week 4, Johnson had a big-time game against the Patriots. His 68 rushing yards eclipsed the team’s meager season average of about 61 yards entering the game. He presumably will have a key role the next couple weeks.
“He played really good. He played really good,” Jacobs said. “I was trying to tell him just on the sideline, just keep doing what he’s always done his whole life. Trust his eyes, trust his reads and just keep making plays and don’t try to overpress, and just get it when it’s there and he did a really good job at that today. So, I’m happy for him because I know that was big for him.”
Brooks returned to practice last week but was not activated from injured reserve. That presumably will happen this week. He figures to immediately reclaim the third-down role.
Lloyd was added to the injury report on Thursday, and while he practiced on Friday, he was inactive for the game. He’s averaging only 2.6 yards per carry.
Strong was promoted from the practice squad for the Week 5 game against Chicago. In his five games on the roster, he played 25 snaps vs. the Bears, 41 vs. the Cowboys, a combined 17 vs. the Lions and Panthers, and 30 vs. the Patriots. He’s averaging only 2.4 yards per carry.
There will be a logjam at running back from a roster perspective with Jacobs, Brooks, Lloyd, Johnson and Strong. If Jacobs is only going to be out a few games, injured reserve will not be an option to create a spot on the roster.
Johnson was a third-round pick by the Steelers last year but quickly fell out of favor. The Packers acquired him at the end of training camp for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
After the fumble at Tampa Bay, Johnson played a combined 13 snaps against Chicago and Dallas and was inactive against Detroit and Carolina. Now, just in the nick of time, he should be back in the coaches’ good graces. He had a 2-yard touchdown in the first half and runs of 34 and 10 yards in the second half.
“It felt great. I feel like I’m getting back to me, getting back comfortable with the system and running the ball,” Johnson said.
The Packers hadn’t rushed for more than 86 yards in a game this season. Over the previous four games, which included two games with Jacobs, they averaged 2.6 yards per carry. Against the Patriots, they rushed for 129 yards and averaged 4.0 yards per carry.
“I just think that everybody coming together as a team and knowing what we’ve got to do each and every day on and off the field – especially in practice – and everybody just coming together and just executing and all being one unit,” he said. “When everyone does that, it’s unstoppable.”
We’ll see about unstoppable, but at least the Packers had an effective run game against the Patriots.
“I thought it was big time,” coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. “I thought all those guys going in … especially losing Josh, I mean, that’s a tough loss right there. For Pierre and Kaleb to step up and go in there, and Kaleb ripped off a couple explosive plays, he scored his first touchdown. That was huge.”

title: Three Words Perfectly Summarize Packers’ WRs Christian Watson, Matthew Golden
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Josh Jacobs said it perfectly when asked about Green Bay Packers receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden after Sunday’s blowout win over the Patriots.
During the Packers’ destruction of the Patriots on Sunday:
Watson caught 7-of-8 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown. It was the seventh-most receiving yards by a player this season.
Entering Monday’s game, there have been 197 instances of a receiver being targeted at least eight times in a game this season. Watson’s 21.4 yards per target against New England was the highest figure of the year. Watson now holds four of the top five spots this season.
Golden caught all 10 targets for 164 yards and one touchdown. It was the ninth-most receiving yards by a player this season.
Among receivers who have been targeted at least 10 times in a game this season, Golden is the only player with a 100 percent catch rate. He finished with the most receiving yards by a player who caught all 10-plus targets in a game since the Steelers’ Antonio Brown in 2017. Over the past 40 years, Golden is just the third receiver with a 100 percent catch rate, 10-plus targets and 16 yards per target.
Combined, they caught 17-of-18 targets for 335 yards and two touchdowns.
“It’s crazy. The plays, I mean, it’s elite. That’s the only way you can really describe it,” Jacobs said.
According to the league, they became the fifth pair of teammates in NFL history with at least seven receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown apiece in the same game. The last were the Dolphins’ Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle in 2022.
It was one of the most dominant dynamic-duo performances in Packers history.
Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first Packers teammates with 150+ receiving yards and 1+ receiving TD since Don Hutson and Andy Uram in 1942. #GoPackGo | @packers
And they did it with coach Matt LaFleur not calling a passing play during the fourth quarter.
The 335 combined receiving yards between Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the most by a Packer duo since Nov. 1, 1942, when Don Hutson (207 yds) and Andy Uram (174 yds) totaled 381 yards in a 55-24 rout of the Chicago Cardinals.
“We talk about it all the time. We feed off each other,” Golden said. “Whenever he gets going, I get going. It goes back and forth. I think when we’re on the same side of the ball, it makes it even better. You got to pick one. I know me and him, we talked about it all offseason – we were going to come in, do this thing and take off with it. It’s just about continuing to keep going and keep winning games.”
Watson and Golden are the only duo to have a combined 300 receiving yards in a game this season. Moreover, there have been only 19 games this season in which a quarterback threw for at least 335 yards in a game, let alone all those yards going to two players.
“Not to sound cocky or anything, but I think we did what we expected us to do,” Watson said. “And I say it every week, we’ve got one of the best receiving corps in the league just because of the playmakers that we got. Obviously, me and MG doing our thing, Tuck and the tight end room, I mean we’ve got it all.
“Our goal every single game is to make plays when our number is called, and we did just that.”
Watson and Golden have combined for 1,662 receiving yards in nine games. That’s more than 200 yards ahead of the next pairing, Dallas’ CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Watson and Golden are on pace for 3,139 receiving yards. Only four receiver duos in NFL history have reached 3,000 yards, with Detroit’s Herman Moore and Brett Perriman holding the record of 3,174 yards. That is within reach, though Moore and Perriman did it over the course of a 16-game season.
Regardless, what they are doing together is staggering. Every defense knows the Packers are going to throw the football with Jordan Love. Every defense knows Love’s two preferred targets.
On Sunday against New England – one of the best defenses in the NFL with one of the best cornerback tandems in the league – they were unstoppable. They combined for 90.1 percent of Love’s passing yards.
For the season, they are up to 63.5 percent of the team’s passing yards and more than half of the team’s total yards.
What Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are doing right now has not been done over a full season in the past two decades 🧀 pic.twitter.com/D0tD6D9F3X
“It just speaks about the confidence the coaches got in us, especially with Jordan,” Golden said. “It wasn’t just built now. It happened over time. We had to put the work in to get where we are now. If we continue to do that, it’s going to keep happening.”
The Packers haven’t had a 1,000-yard receiver since Davante Adams. Well, Watson and Golden might get to 1,500 yards this season.
Watson is third in the NFL with 879 yards. He’s on pace for 1,660 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns. In NFL history, there have been only 10 seasons of at least 1,600 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns.
Golden is fourth in the NFL with 783 receiving yards. He’s on pace for 1,479 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.
“We’ve got to keep building,” Love said. “There’s still more out there for us. I talk about this all the time, but just the connection we’ve been having and making plays downfield, and I think tonight was just kind of the epitome of everything we’ve been putting work in for. But I think there’s still more out there . But these guys, those two, they’re just making play after play. So, it really makes it easy for me. Just keep going to them.”

title: Packers Overreactions: NFL Should Be Terrified of What Jordan Love Said
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers blew out the New England Patriots on Sunday. It was a statement victory against the defending AFC champions.
With Jordan Love, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and some big plays on defense, the Packers are good enough to beat any team on any given Sunday.
Maybe even the second Sunday of February.
Here are this week’s Packers Overreactions
Jordan Love threw 18 passes to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. They turned those into 17 completions for 335 yards and two touchdowns. To say that trio single-handedly led the Packers to victory would be exaggeration, obviously, but they powered an emphatic win over one of the top teams in the NFL.
Asked about Watson and Golden after the game, Love had this to say:
“I think that’s something that we’ve been building on. You know, me and Christian have been together for a while now, and MG going in Year 2. I think more opportunities for those guys, and to really just settle in and get as many reps as possible throughout OTAs, training camp, and we made the most of it.
“So, we’ve got to keep building. There’s still more out there for us. I talk about this all the time, but just the connection we’ve been having and making plays downfield, and I think tonight was just kind of the epitome of everything we’ve been putting work in for. But I think there’s still more out there. But these guys, those two, they’re just making play after play. So, it really makes it easy for me. Just keep going to them.”
The three big words there?
More? More than 325 yards and two touchdowns? More than six deep completions for 235 yards? More than Watson ranking third in the NFL in receiving yards and Golden ranking fourth? More than their pace to finish with more than 3,100 yards?
More than dominating one of the premier cornerbacks in the NFL in Christian Gonzalez? More than routing a defense led by Mike Vrabel? More than being unstoppable when everyone in the stadium knew where Love wanted to throw the ball?
What a scary statement for the rest of the league entering the second half of the season.
Love was magnificent. When the Patriots blitzed, he had answers. When the Patriots had pressure, he made a play. When he had time, he made the Patriots pay.
“Flowing. That’s what it feels like. Feels like you’re just in that flow state and just finding ways to get guys the ball,” Love said. “But, definitely, just feels like you’re flowing. It’s a great feeling, and you just want to keep chasing every play and keep making big plays.
“I think I made some good throws, but I think guys are making some pretty cool catches, as well. So, yeah, we just got to keep you know building on that. Christian and MG, I mean, I looked at their stat line after the game and it was just crazy. It’s crazy to see that, and I think they’re balling right now. So, we just got to keep finding ways to get them the rock.”
The Packers entered Sunday’s game averaging barely 60 rushing yards per game. That put them on pace to have the worst rushing attack in NFL history.
Against a stout Patriots defense, the Packers ran for 129 yards. With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger and MarShawn Lloyd inactive, coach Matt LaFleur had to let Kaleb Johnson out of the doghouse. He responded with 68 yards on 14 carries. He had 60 yards after contact, by our count.
“I feel like this is a little thing of what I can do when I get comfortable with the system and get familiar with the system,” he said. “Going over plays with [running backs] coach [Ben] Sirmans every day and just building on that and learning what to do on and off the field and just being me, just getting comfortable and confident.”
The Packers should have their backfield for the rest of the season.
In 2024 and 2025, the Packers leaned on Jacobs as the No. 1 runner with Emanuel Wilson providing solid play as the No. 2 and Chris Brooks entering in pass-protecting situations. That should be the plan going into the second half of the season, with Jacobs as the No. 1 back, Johnson as the sidekick and Brooks entering in pass-protecting situations once he’s activated from injured reserve.
And Lloyd? Maybe it’s time to admit defeat on the former third-round pick.
Before the game, Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon called the matchup against New England’s offense a “big-time challenge.” The start of the challenge was quarterback Drake Maye and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.
“They’re a Super Bowl-caliber team, and they’re playing that way on offense,” Gannon said on Tuesday. “I think Josh McDaniels does an excellent job. They’re very creative, their scheme is robust, he gets them in the right plays. They got good backs, the O-line’s good, they got skill guys. This is a good crew now.”
The Packers led the Patriots 42-14 late in the third quarter. They forced four turnovers and made life miserable for Maye, last year’s MVP runner-up.
You know all of that. But consider the challenges.
Micah Parsons just returned to practice. The Packers are 11th in points allowed and total defense with their best player having missed all nine games.
The Packers played most of the game with their No. 3 and No. 5 linebackers. Edgerrin Cooper, who had been the team’s best defensive player without Parsons, is out for the season with a torn Achilles and defensive captain Zaire Franklin missed a third game with an injured shin. On Sunday, backup-turned-starter Ty’Ron Hopper played two snaps before exiting with a chest injury.
So, the Packers had to line up with steady veteran Isaiah McDuffie and special-teams ace Nick Niemann. Sure, Niemann gave up a touchdown catch but the Packers shut down one of the top offenses in the league without their All-Pro edge rusher and with a skeleton crew at linebacker.
You’d think an offensive guru like McDaniels and a top quarterback like Maye would be able to take advantage. They couldn’t, though, because Gannon sent blitz after blitz after blitz that McDaniels and Maye couldn’t handle.
“I thought it was pretty solid,” said Xavier McKinney, who had two interceptions. “Obviously, I thought we did a good job of getting the ball. We had a lot of turnovers. I think they gave us some plays that we didn’t really want to give up. They scored 27, so we got some things to get corrected. But I think overall we played a solid game. I do think there’s still a lot of room for improvement.”
That’s a variation of what Love said about there being “more out there,” but it’s the same theme. The defense wrecked the Patriots but there’s room to improve.
“I think JG’s brought a different level of energy to our defense and even to our team, to be honest with you,” McKinney said. “Obviously with the players that we have, everybody’s hungry, everybody is trying to figure out ways where they can be better as individuals, and then collectively that helps the group.”
Added together, if there’s another gear for the offense with the emergence of the running game and there’s room to improve on defense – hello, Micah Parsons – Sunday’s blowout could be the jumping-off point for this team.

title: Snaps, Studs, Duds and Defining Stats From Packers’ Destruction of Patriots
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Are the Green Bay Packers good enough to get to the Super Bowl?
The Packers answered that question in emphatic fashion on Sunday, crushing the defending AFC champion New England Patriots 45-27 on Sunday. Jordan Love made a statement . His receivers caught everything in sight. There was an honest-to-goodness running game. The defense produced four takeaways and the special teams bounced back.
Here is our weekly look at the snap counts, along with some studs and duds.
The Packers played 66 snaps on offense.
Quarterbacks: Jordan Love got to watch the final 9-plus minutes from the sideline. He played 58 snaps, with Tyrod Taylor running out the clock.
Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns even while not attempting a pass in the fourth quarter. He was great under pressure, he destroyed the blitz and he made one big-time throw after another. It was a virtuoso performance.
Running Backs: The Packers’ projected running back depth chart was Josh Jacobs, Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd. For most of Sunday’s game, it was Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong. With Jacobs suffering a broken finger, Brooks on injured reserve and Lloyd inactive with a knee injury, Strong played 30 snaps, Johnson played 26 and Jacobs was limited to 10.
Johnson had been in the doghouse since fumbling at Tampa Bay. Because of circumstances, he’s probably out of it. Johnson carried the ball 14 times for 68 yards and one touchdown. We credited him with 60 yards after contact and two broken tackles. The Packers, barely averaging 60 rushing yards per game through Week 8, rumbled for 129.
Receivers: Christian Watson and Matthew Golden ran circles around one of the best cornerback tandems in the NFL. Watson played 51 snaps and Golden played 49. They combined to catch 17-of-18 targets for 335 yards with one touchdown apiece.
Savion Williams has become a key piece to the puzzle with 32 snaps. For all his work as a gadget guy, he is far more productive when he plays receiver and does receiver things. His 10-yard touchdown catch was superb work. Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant played 15 snaps apiece. On special teams, Melton played 21 and returned a kickoff to midfield and added two tackles, and Sturdivant played 20.
Tight Ends: Tucker Kraft played 54 snaps. He contributed almost nothing statistically because Love was zeroed in on his receivers. Kraft converted two quarterback sneaks but both were nullified by false starts and then was stuffed when he tried to jump over the pile on the third.
Mark Redman played 24 snaps and had the big block on Kaleb Johnson’s touchdown run. Inactive last week, Jonnu Smith played 16. Drake Dabney was elevated from the practice squad and played six snaps on special teams.
Offensive Line: Right tackle Anthony Belton and center John Williams went the distance, and left tackle Jordan Morgan and right guard Laken Tomlinson played 58.
Left guard Aaron Banks missed some time in the first half and got to watch the end of the game on the sideline. So, he played 46 snaps. Kevin Zeitler finally got some action on offense and played 20 snaps as part of the shuffle following Banks’ injury and then in garbage time.
Morgan was tremendous; he’s really playing well as the blindside protector.
The Packers played 63 snaps on defense.
Defensive Tackles: The Packers’ defensive front will be as fresh as spring daisies for next week’s game against the Vikings. Rookie Chris McClellan played 33 snaps and Karl Brooks played 32, so barely more than half. Devonte Wyatt played 29 snaps, followed by Anthony Campbell with 25 and Jordon Riley with 20.
Brooks is having a really good season, even if the stats haven’t shown it, so it was good for him to have two sacks among his four pressures.
Edges: Just like at defensive tackle, the scoreboard allowed defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon to level out the playing time even more than usual. Brenton Cox led the unit with 34 snaps. He was followed by Dani Dennis-Sutton with 32, Lukas Van Ness with 32 and Barryn Sorrell with 30. Sorrell also logged 25 snaps on special teams.
Cox and Dennis-Sutton shared a sack; Cox for the second consecutive week led the team in pressures with five, according to Next Gen Stats. The others had two apiece.
Linebackers: The Packers came out of training camp with a depth chart of Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin as the starters and Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper as the linebackers. Yeah, those were the days. With Cooper on injured reserve and Franklin inactive again with an injured shin, Hopper started but dropped out after two snaps with a chest injury. Even McDuffie was shaken up at the end of the game.
So, the snaps wound up being McDuffie for 60, Nick Niemann for 59, Kristian Welch for three and Hopper for two.
McDuffie led the team with nine tackles, including one sack. Niemann had six tackles. He gave up a touchdown but broke up one pass and had some production as a blitzer.
Cornerbacks: Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse’s days were over after 51 snaps. Nixon got beat for a double-move touchdown, the first score he’s allowed this season. Cisse’s pass breakup turned into an interception. According to PFF, he was targeted four times and allowed one catch for 2 yards.
Carrington Valentine played 13 snaps, veteran Benjamin St-Juste – who had played only one snap all season – played 12 and Kamal Hadden played five in the slot. He dropped a pick-six late in the half. St-Juste is a good player; a cornerback-hungry team would be wise to ask the Packers about his availability.
Safeties: Do the Packers’ have the best tandem of safeties in the NFL? Probably. The better question is which of the safeties is better? Evan Williams played 61 snaps. He had one interception and added four pressures, according to PFF. Xavier McKinney played 51 snaps. He had two interceptions, tying him for first in the league with five.
Javon Bullard played 40 snaps in the slot and Kitan Oladapo played 14.
QB Jordan Love: Bombs away.
Jordan Love completed 6 of 8 deep passes (20+ air yards) for 235 yards and a touchdown in Week 9. Love completed six deep passes for the second time this season. No other quarterback in the NFL has done so in any game. #GBvsNE | #GoPackGo pic.twitter.com/lMgscdboLl
WRs Christian Watson and Matthew Golden: They were the dominant forces. On passes thrown 20-plus yards downfield, they combined to catch 6-of-7 for 235 yards. Against premier cornerback Christian Gonzalez, the carnage was 11-of-12 for 192 yards and the two touchdowns, according to Pro Football Focus. With the Monday night game to be played, Watson is third in the league in receiving yards and Golden is fourth.
S Xavier McKinney: McKinney is tied for the NFL lead with five interceptions. Quarterbacks are foolish to throw it in his direction, especially when it’s not thrown at max velocity. He’s just too good to lob one up in his ZIP code.
S Evan Williams: Williams is tied for sixth in the league with three interceptions. He’s got 71 tackles, as well, making him the only player in the league with 60-plus tackles and more than one interception.
DT Karl Brooks: The Packers’ defensive tackles have been playing selfless team defense throughout the season, so the statistical production hasn’t matched their impact. At some point, though, players have to make plays. Brooks had two sacks.
CB Brandon Cisse: The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Month continued his sensational season. He was targeted four times, allowed 2 yards and produced one interception on the deflection that was picked off by Williams.
LG Aaron Banks: Jordan Love got sacked in the first half because Banks botched a stunt. PFF charged him with that sack and three pressures. The Packers need better from their $77 million lineman.
DT Devonte Wyatt: Wyatt signed a three-year, $54.9 million contract extension to keep him in Green Bay through the 2029 season. He shows up twice in the NFL’s statistical gamebook: He started and he played 29 snaps. He had no tackles, no sacks,…

title: Packers Report Card: One Obvious A-Plus In Blowout Win Over Patriots
full_text:
The grades are in, and it’s hard to imagine anything other than giving an A-plus for the way the Green Bay Packers started Sunday’s blowout win over the New England Patriots.
Drake Maye threw an interception on his first pass attempt of the day. The Packers led 17-0 before going into halftime with a 24-14 lead. It was more of the same in the second half, with Green Bay rolling to a 45-27 win. Jordan Love threw for 372 yards, with 335 yards going to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.
Here is our Packers report card from Green Bay’s statement victory.
Matthew Golden and Jordan Love must have heard the noise all week about Christian Gonzalez, because they targeted him early and often. Golden was responsible for 126 receiving yards in the first quarter. That included a 49-yard pass early in the game along with Love’s 100th career touchdown pass.
Love was not done. The Packers’ deep-ball approach tore apart New England’s defense in the first half. If Love had time to throw the ball, he found his top two guys, Christian Watson and Golden.
Love threw for 219 yards in the first half. The only real downside was him getting sacked three times, and some odd sequencing to end the first half. Otherwise, he looked in complete command of the offense.
The protection? That’s another story. What Love has done this season behind this offensive line should be studied by science. Love was pressured on half of his first 20 dropbacks. It doesn’t seem to matter. He’s rarely fazed.
Love threw for 372 yards in less than three-and-a-half quarters. Watson caught 7-of-8 passes for 171 yards and one touchdown and Golden caught all 10 targets for 164 yards and one touchdown. They became the first teammates with 150-plus receiving yards and one touchdown in the same game since the Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb and Brandin Cooks in 2023. They were the first Packers receiver duo to ever hit those marks in a game.
Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first Packers teammates with 150+ receiving yards and 1+ receiving TD since Don Hutson and Andy Uram in 1942. #GoPackGo | @packers
Savion Williams contributed, as well. All three of the top receivers had a touchdown, but the story is Love.
Love was dynamite from the beginning of the game until they built a 42-14 lead.
No offensive line, no run game? No problem. The Packers have Love, and that might be all they need.
A sequence in the second quarter probably sums up Green Bay’s run game the best. They were facing a third-and-1 from the Patriots’ side of the 50 nursing a 17-7 lead. Kaleb Johnson was tackled short of the line to gain after Jordan Morgan was beaten off the snap by Christian Barmore.
On fourth down, Matt LaFleur kept his offense on the field and called a sneak with Tucker Kraft taking the snap from center. Jordan Love was lined up in the backfield and tagged for a false start after losing his balance. That resulted in a Packers punt.
Lack of attention to detail, poor blocking and the inability to create any yards after being contacted. That’s the Packers’ run game in a nutshell.
With Josh Jacobs suffering a hand injury early in the game and not returning, their leading rusher was Johnson. Back on the field after getting just one rushing attempt the last three games, he helped the Packers get over 100 rushing yards with a few explosive runs.
The 100 yards felt like a miracle. The Packers averaged 60 rushing yards during the first eight games. Adding any semblance of a ground game could make this Packers’ offense even more dangerous as the weather turns colder.
How good is Green Bay’s secondary? That group was excellent in the first half against Drake Maye, starting from his first pass attempt.
Maye rolled to his right before dialing up a deep ball to Mack Hollins. Hollins throttled down for some reason, and Xavier McKinney looked more like the intended receiver than anyone in a Patriots uniform.
The best play of the game probably came from Brandon Cisse and Evan Williams. Maye threw the ball deep up the left sideline with Cisse in coverage. Cisse stayed in phase and knocked the ball in the air, where Williams performed some fancy footwork to land in bounds to knock the Patriots’ offense off the field.
The third interception of the half came from McKinney again after Maye and Co. looked like they were poised to pull within one possession. Maye was looking for another explosive play on a crossing route, but McKinney jumped it for his second pick of the day and the team’s third.
They nearly had a fourth interception in the first half when a pass from Maye hit Kamal Hadden’s fingertips. If Hadden caught the ball, it would have been a pick-six. He had to settle for a PBU and forcing a Patriots punt.
They finished with three interceptions and a forced fumble.
If there is one thing to quibble with, Green Bay’s four-man rush did not apply much pressure on Maye. When they did get pressure with their front four, it was largely a byproduct of coverage that made Maye hold the ball. They’re going to get Micah Parsons back, but he’s not going to be full tilt until later in the season.
One exception to the rule was Karl Brooks, who had two sacks on the day, but he has had his ebbs and flows on the season, as well. The pass rush must become more consistent before Parsons returns to the lineup.
The Packers’ run defense was given an assist from its offense. The score was 17-0 before New England knew what hit it. With the score growing to 42-14 in the third quarter, Patriots ran for 94 yards on 19 attempts.
Even when the Patriots were in a neutral game script, they were unable to get much traction on the ground. Green Bay’s run defense has been excellent for most of the season.
The first half was solid outside of Coleman Owen not fielding a punt that cost his team good field position in the first half. Bo Melton had an explosive kickoff return to midfield that Green Bay’s offense wasted, and Trey Smack made all of his kicks without much drama. With the drama that had taken place in previous weeks with Smack, a quiet half was a more than welcome sight.
Smack was excellent in the second half, as well, including a 51-yard field goal. The Packers hope this was Smack bouncing back from his struggles.
The strangest sequence of the first half came when the Packers started at midfield after Bo Melton’s 48-yard kickoff return. At the 2-minute warning, they faced a third-and-2.
Coach Matt LaFleur ultimately ran two plays to try to move the chains and get into scoring range. One of them was a swing pass to Savion Williams in which it looked like Williams was trying to throw the ball down the field. It felt like an odd time for a trick play considering the Packers’ offense was moving the ball almost at will.
On fourth-and-3, Love threw incomplete to Williams when LaFleur could have punted to try and pin the Patriots deep before the end of the half. Instead, the failed conversion gave the Patriots a chance to pull within one possession in a half the Packers essentially had dominated.
The aggression from LaFleur is the problem, but the play sequencing certainly was.
This game, however, goes into Matt LaFleur’s mind shift. LaFleur wants to run the ball first and foremost. He knows he can’t. He’s leaning into Jordan Love and the passing game.
The only real coaching decision to question is why the Packers continue to roll with left guard Aaron Banks, who is either not healthy or not effective.
When you win by double digits on the road against the reigning AFC champions, those are what former defensive coordinator Joe Barry used to call champagne problems.
Meanwhile, even with a four-man rush that struggles to make an impact, Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon continually outfoxed Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels. Drake Maye was pressured on 18 of 38 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. When Gannon blitzed, Maye averaged only 4.2 yards per attempt.
There are almost no words to describe how Jordan Love played yesterday. I tried,…

title: Packers’ Jordan Love Makes Strongest Statement Imaginable About What’s Possible
full_text:
Jordan Love’s timing for his 100th career touchdown pass was exquisite.
Love reached 100 touchdown passes at a pace just behind future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers and just ahead of Hall of Famer Brett Favre.
Rodgers won four NFL MVP awards and one Super Bowl. Favre won three NFL MVPs and one Super Bowl.
With the way Love played in the Packers’ blowout victory over the Patriots – with legendary Tom Brady on the call for Fox – he perhaps for the first time in his career looked like a quarterback not just capable of winning a Super Bowl but perhaps destined to do so.
Love, in a word, was dominant. Facing one of the best pass defenses in the NFL – Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis are one of the top cornerback tandems in the league and the Patriots entered the week ranked fifth in sack percentage – Love was 23-of-29 passing for 372 yards and three touchdowns, good for a near-perfect passer rating of 153.2.
An absolute STATEMENT game from Jordan Love and the Packers pic.twitter.com/Tjb9CsmWDU
“You’re witnessing greatness,” running back Josh Jacobs said.
Under pressure, Love was 5-of-7 passing for 125 yards and one touchdown.
When blitzed, Love was 10-of-11 passing for 146 yards and one touchdown.
On passes thrown 20-plus yards downfield, Love was 6-of-8 passing 235 yards and one touchdown.
Some quarterbacks steer clear of premier cornerbacks. Gonzalez, a second-team All-Pro in 2024 and a Pro Bowler in 2025, is the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL. Love and his elite tandem of receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, tore him apart.
Christian Gonzalez allowed 7 receptions for 105 yards to Matthew Golden and 3 receptions for 82 yards to Christian Watson. Gonzalez is the only defender since at least 2018 to allow more than 80 receiving yards to two different players in the same game. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/2voC02QTd3
Golden caught all 10 targets for 164 yards and one touchdown. Watson caught 7-of-8 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown. Combined, that’s 17 catches out of 18 targets for 335 yards and two touchdowns.
Gonzalez allowed 187 yards in coverage, the third-most by any player this season, after he had allowed 196 yards in his first six games combined.
“I think that’s just the guys we got on the outside going out there making plays,” Love said. “You know, it really doesn’t matter who it is. We trust the game plan. We trust that guys are going to get open and make plays, and they did that tonight.
“I still got a lot of respect for him. He’s a great player, but it’s the NFL. We see great DBs every week, and I think our mindset is we got to keep attacking and we got good guys on the outside that are going to make plays.”
The Packers’ 45 points were the most in a regular-season game during coach Matt LaFleur’s tenure and the most points scored by a visiting team against the Patriots at Gillette Stadium.
Love almost certainly would have had his first 400-yard game had LaFleur not let him watch the final 9 minutes from the sideline. He set a career high for passer rating.
“He’s doing a great job, man,” LaFleur said. “I can’t say enough great things about him. What’s even better about him is just how he is on a daily basis. Just coming in, working with him, he is the same guy every day, whether it’s a great performance like he’s been doing consistently or … he’s just the same guy. He’s the same guy that we got when we drafted him, and I think it’s a big-time credit and I don’t want that to get overlooked.”
Golden set single-game career highs for receptions and yards. It was his fourth 100-yard game this season. He became the first receiver in the league this year with a 100 percent catch rate on a game of 10-plus targets.
“Phenomenal,” Golden said of Love. “Just being able to play with a guy like that is a blessing. Obviously, a lot of work had to get put in to get where we are now. It all goes back to OTAs and training camp, man. Just seeing the way he’s playing right now, it gets us going as receivers just being able to play with a guy like that, we kind of feed off that. Whenever he’s going, we all going.”
Watson set a single-game high for receiving yards, as well. It was the sixth-highest output by a player this season.
“Can’t ask for much more, can’t ask for much more,” Watson said. “At the beginning of the year when we were going through not being the team that we wanted to be, he was still doing everything that he could to play his best ball and doing everything he could. To see him continue to stay even keeled throughout this season, whether it was a positive or a negative, you can’t ask for a much better leader or much better quarterback or much better driver of this offense throughout the season.”
Love entered the game with the ninth-shortest MVP odds at FanDuel Sportsbook. Now, he’s fourth.
After a slow start, the Packers are 6-3. They can’t run the football, though their 129 rushing yards against the Patriots more than doubled their season average. They’ve dropped passes throughout the season, though they didn’t drop any on Sunday. Micah Parsons still hasn’t played in a game.
And yet, they’ve won five of their last six games. Love is playing at an MVP level. He’s playing like a Super Bowl-caliber quarterback.
Facing the defending AFC champions, who entered the game ranked ninth in points allowed and with an unblemished home record, Love was the dominant force. Everyone affiliated with the Patriots, whether it’s coach Mike Vrabel or Gonzalez, knew that the Packers’ only hope of winning was Love having a big game.
Love didn’t just have a big game. He had his biggest game. He looked like an elite quarterback, a player capable of hoisting the franchise on his back and carrying it anywhere – perhaps even SoFi Stadium for this year’s Super Bowl.
“We talk about the same thing every time, we got to take a mindset of one week at a time,” Love said. “I think you want to get rolling, we always talk about that, we want to stack wins. So, we got two wins, we got to be able to regroup.
“Obviously, we got Minnesota coming to our house next week, someone who we lost to earlier in the season. So, we got to be able to regroup, have a great week of prep and go on attack that week. I think the mindset’s just got to be all complete focus and preparation on Minnesota and you can’t let one game kind lull you to sleep. It was a great performance tonight, but it’s all about getting back to work and having a good game plan. But, yeah, that’s what we talk about: Stacking wins, get rolling as a unit, and that’s what we did.”

title: The First Thought After Packers Beat Patriots 45-27
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers can’t run the football, no matter who’s blocking or carrying the ball. They can’t rush the passer, unless it’s by Jonathan Gannon’s design.
Those two things should take any talk about the playoffs, let alone a championship, off the table.
Is it possible these Packers can defy conventional wisdom?
On Sunday, the Packers beat the New England Patriots 45-27. It was their fifth win in six games. This wasn’t edging the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield or blowing out the Bears without Caleb Williams.
This was beating the defending AFC champions. At their place. With their quarterback, 2025 MVP runner-up Drake Maye.
This was Jordan Love cooking.
This was Matt LaFleur stepping on the gas.
This was Gannon outfoxing Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels at every turn.
Yes, the Patriots played without their starting receivers. But the Packers were down to their third and fifth linebackers after backup-turned-starter Ty’Ron Hopper was injured early in the game. The Packers were down to their fourth and fifth running backs with Josh Jacobs injured and MarShawn Lloyd inactive and Chris Brooks on injured reserve. Micah Parsons is a couple weeks away from playing in a game.
What the Packers had was Love. In the first half, he was 11-of-16 passing for 219 yards. He had 372 yards and three touchdowns in the first three quarters.
“Man, it’s definitely up there,” he said when asked if this was his best game ever. “It felt great, you know. So, we’ll look at it, but it definitely felt like just a real fun game to be a part of. When everything’s flowing, we’re putting up points and everybody’s making plays, it’s definitely very fun to be a part of.”
What the Packers had was Matthew Golden running circles around Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez to the tune of seven catches for 150 yards and one touchdown in the first half.
What the Packers had was Christian Watson, broken rib and all, making plays down the field.
Through three quarters, they combined to catch 17-of-18 targets for 335 yards and two touchdowns. It was absurd, like an elite Madden player dicing up some rando. They are on pace to finish with more than 3,100 yards.
What the Packers had was Gannon calling the shots. And safeties Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams producing turnovers by the bushel.
A team that can’t run the football – though it did hit the 100-yard mark for the first time this season – and can’t really rush the passer without Gannon sending blitzers from here, there and everywhere, shouldn’t be able to go on the road and win games against good teams.
But, shoot, who knows. The Patriots are a good team. They’ve got a really good coach and a really good quarterback. They’ve got one of the best cornerback tandems in the NFL. They’ve got a good running back, good defensive tackles and a good overall roster.
And the Packers wiped the floor with them. They had four takeaways – a sixth consecutive game with at least two. McKinney had two interceptions, tying him for the league lead with five. They went 4-of-5 in the red zone. Embattled rookie They Smack made every kick.
The smackdown was so thorough that coach Matt LaFleur got to clear the bench for the final 9-plus minutes.
“I think against a really good team like this, you can’t take your foot off the gas,” he said. “In fact, I was a little hesitant to pull our guys as early as we did.”
This version of the Packers, who fell apart in Week 1 at Minnesota, barely won at the Jets in Week 2, got crushed at home by Atlanta in Week 3 and barely beat a backup quarterback at the Buccaneers in Week 4, might have beaten every team in the league with the way they played on Sunday.
The Packers are on the rise. They are a team with sizable flaws but are so good at what they’re good at that it didn’t matter against the defending AFC champions. They will host the Vikings on Sunday; Minnesota is 6-1 heading into Monday’s home game against Buffalo. Then comes the faux-bye week before their Thanksgiving Eve game at the Rams that could mark Parsons’ return to the lineup.
After a game at the Saints, the Packers will close the regular season with four home games in a span of five weeks.
The sky is the limit for the Packers. Love might not win MVP – though he surged to fourth on the board at FanDuel Sportsbook – but it’s impossible to argue that any one player is more valuable to his team than Love.
Love, who entered the game having accounted for a league-high 82.0 percent of the team’s yards, absolutely shredded the Patriots with a near-perfect 153.2 passer rating and an eighth game this season with multiple touchdowns.
“Flowing. That’s what it feels like,” Love said. “Feels like you’re just in that flow state. It’s a great feeling, and you just want to keep, you know, chasing every play and keep making big plays.”
He was 6-of-8 passing on throws 20-plus yards downfield for 235 yards.
“Those are low-percentage throws in theory, but he’s making them look high-percentage,” LaFleur said. “They’re right on the money, and our guys are doing a great job.”
The defense had four sacks and four takeaways with Parsons on the way back.
“I can’t say enough about JG, just dialing up stuff and getting pressure on the quarterback,” LaFleur said. “And then the guys up front, wreaking havoc and getting to the quarterback — that was a big thing going into this game and it allows our guys on the back end to make plays.”
The special teams fought to at least a draw against one of the best units in the league.
LaFleur knows that his team can’t rest. Now with the Vikings coming to town. Not in a week-to-week league.
But if this is the standard, watch out.
“It’s one game,” he said. “We’ve got a great team coming into our house, the team that’s leading the NFC North, and we’ve got to string together another great performance in order to get a win.”
