title: The Cases For—and Against—the Jaguars Trading for Moro Ojomo, Budda Baker and More
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The NFL Trade Deadline can sometimes be defined by the deals that aren't made much more so than the ones that do eventually get made.
With each deal that comes up in chatter around the deadline, teams must weigh the good and the bad, the pros and the cons, the risk and reward, and simply whether or not it makes them a better team.
So with plenty of eyes on the Jaguars and what potential move or moves they might make by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, it is worth weighing the two sides of the coin for each hypothetical blockbuster. So, what are the cases for and against the Jaguars making several deals?
The Case For: The Jaguars have a window to win a Super Bowl now, and adding some juice to their pass-rush could put them over the top. Arik Armstead has still been productive and Ruke Orhorhoro has given them some quality snaps as a backup, but Moro Ojomo would likely give the Jaguars a bigger punch inside, especially on third-downs. There is also the long-term outlook, with Ojomo a young and ascending player in his contract year. The Jaguars could either re-sign him and make him the foundation of their defensive line room moving forward with Armstead and Davon Hamilton set to be free agents.
The Case Against: Is it worth the cost? Ojomo will likely sign a deal that, at worst, could net the Eagles a fourth-round compensatory pick down the road if he leaves in March. The Eagles have seemed stubborn about moving him even with teams like the Jaguars reportedly interested. This is likely the Eagles posturing for a higher pick, which could be in the third-round and, perhaps, even steeper than that. Ojomo is a good player, but he is not yet an elite one. Is he worth a potential elite asking price?
The Case For: If there is one thing the Jaguars should have been doing during their mini-bye before they face the Titans next Sunday, it is looking at the safety room. The losses of Eric Murray for the season and Caleb Ransaw for an undisclosed time earlier this season have made the Jaguars thin at the position, even if they have been able to skate by in 2026. Budda Baker has the experience and traits to fill a big hole for the Jaguars before they play elite quarterbacks later down the stretch.
The Case Against: Do the Jaguars need to mess with a good thing? Yes, the Jaguars' safety depth chart has been hit hard. But we did see Rayuan Lane step up with game-changing plays against the Indianapolis Colts and Kaevon Merriweather has been a reliable backup. And eventually, the Jaguars will have to trust rookie safety Jalen Huskey . If it's not broken yet, do they need to attempt to fix it?
The Case For: The Falcons season is looking a bit more lost each week, and it certainly seems like they can't lean on their pass defense anyways after they just got lit up by Joe Burrow on Sunday morning. Convince the Falcons that their future is now and they do not need Jessie Bates on a shorter deal much longer. bates is one of the best ballhawks in football and would give the Jaguars the rangy option at safety they do not have with Ransaw injured.
The Case Against: Can the Jaguars make it worth more than a rental? Bates is in the last half-season of his contract and could opt to hit the free agency market and cash in for the second time in his career in March. It would likely take a semi-significant Day 3 pick to pry him from the Falcons, and it would have to be understood that you would lose him if you don't end up being the one to pay up. The Jaguars could make it worse cap-wise, but they have another safety on an expiring deal to think about.
The Case For: The Jaguars have one of the best defenses in the NFL thanks to the influence and guidance of Anthony Campanile. The only real way to make the unit better would be to add another interior pass-rusher, and that is exactly what Christian Barmore is. When Barmore has been at his best, he has been one of the NFL's more disruptive three-techniques against the pass when he has been at his best.
The Case Against: Can the Jaguars get Christian Barmore to be at his best? He has seemingly fallen out of favor in New England, and his snaps and production have each dipped as a result. Can he get back to his previous peaks as a pass-rusher, or are the Patriots simply trying to exit early on what they think is a career cliff on the way?
The Case For: After the season-ending injury to Davon Hamilton, the Jaguars need a difference-maker inside. There is no question the Jaguars have done their homework on potential interior defensive line targets, and the best overall talent whose name has come up in some fashion has been Carolina's Derrick Brown. The former top-10 pick commands attention against both the run and the pass and is the highest-ceiling player on this list. Adding him would be akin to adding Marcell Dareus for the 2017 playoff run.
The Case Against: Would the Panthers even be open to it? The fact that we have to ask suggests the answer is no, unless the price tag is met. And that price tag would likely be significant just based on Browns' talent. He is one of the best overall players on the Panthers roster, and most indications are that he would cost quite the pretty penny. Is he worth such a move? Maybe, but maybe not asclear as Jeffery Simmons would have been.

title: Jaguars Week 9 Rooting Guide: How AFC South, Trade Deadline Positions Can Both Be Improved
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have already had a good Week 9. It could get even better over the next 48 hours.
With the Jaguars having already improved to 6-2 after a dominant 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football, they can sit and watch the rest of the NFL's week play out on Sunday and Monday, and they can boost their position on several fronts as a result.
Jacksonville can get even closer to an eventual AFC South crown depending on some of Sunday's games, as well as improve their standing in what looks like a two-month-long race for top seeding in the AFC as a whole.
Then there is the trade deadline . The Jaguars have a few days head start to evaluate their trade deadline options after an early Week 9 game, and perhaps a few losses on Sunday could push teams toward selling for a potential buyer in the Jaguars.
So, what results should the Jaguars root for in Week 9? We break it all down below.
Rooting Interest: New York Jets
This one is clear. The Jaguars can not count their chickens before they hatch when it comes to the AFC South race, but it also seems like the Jaguars' lead in the division means their horizons can expand. One of those horizons is seeding in the AFC. Winning the AFC South would secure the Jaguars a top-four seed in the AFC, but the leaders of each divison are all still very much so in the race for the No. 1 seed.
The Chiefs have been at the top of the AFC's standings for much of the season, but they have hit some roadblocks lately. An upset loss to the New York Jets would be a surprise, but it would be a nice boost toward the Jaguars' pursuit of the No. 1 seed in the AFC -- or better. Having the Chiefs visit EverBank Stadium if the two sides meet in the playoffs seems better than playing on the road in Kansas City.
Rooting Interest: Los Angeles Chargers
This one is clear. It seems like the Los Angeles Chargers are so stubborn that even a 1-16 record might not force them to move off the idea that their season isn't over. If the Chargers aren't going to sell at all, then it doesn't really matter for the Jaguars if they pick up their eighth loss, even if they have at minimum three defenders who would make sense to be added to the Jaguars' defense at the deadline.
If the Chargers get their first win of the season, it would come at the expense of a Houston Texans team that really can't afford losing any more games down the stretch after a 2-5 start. Any more Texans losses would push the Jaguars real close to being locks to win the AFC South for the second year in a row, something the Jaguars have never done.
Rooting Interest: New York Giants
Will the Eagles actually trade defensive tackle Moro Ojomo? That, to me, is one of the biggest questions of the entire deadline period. Ojomo has arguably been the Eagles' best and most consistent defensive tackle this year despite sharing a room with Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, and there is a real chance he signs a $100 million deal this March somewhere. But could it take another big loss in the NFC East to make it happen?
The Eagles have never really been the type to start waving the white flag and selling off pieces of their roster mid-season. But they have some big bills coming due soon, their season is clearly over, and they have a ton of questions moving forward. A loss should tell them that the party is over for 2026 at least, if they do not already know it. And just maybe it could push them to deal the market's most interesting defensive tackle.
Rooting Interest: Minnesota Vikings
The Jaguars are Carson Wentz fans in Week 9, which is a weird spot to be in for anyone in 2026. It was weird in 2022. It is weirder now. But the Jaguars should root for the Bills to drop games for the next two months due to playoff seeding purposes. Yes, the Bills beat the Jaguars in the Wild Card last year in Jacksonville anyways, but that had more to do with Josh Allen going supernova. Avoiding a road game against Allen in the playoffs seems ideal, and the Bills do have a tough second-half schedule.
Rooting Interest: Seattle Seahawks
Could the Cardinals finally deal Budda Baker after years of losing with a final knockout blow against the Seattle Seahawks? That is the question any team with a safety need should be asking right now. The Jaguars are one of those teams after a season-ending injury to Eric Murray, and there are simply too many reasons why Baker would be the perfect fit for their secondary during a playoff push this winter.
This is one where, like, a tie would be best? The Jaguars should want the Panthers to lose to push them closer toward selling in the event that it comes down to a Derrick Brown possibility. But the Broncos losing would also be big for the Jaguars in the race for AFC seeding. This is one where you can probably feel OK about either result.

title: One Move the Jaguars Can't Afford to Get Wrong at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are one of the NFL's most fascinating teams ahead of next week's NFL Trade Deadline, but that doesn't mean there aren't still some lines that have to be toed.
Toeing the line of adding talent on paper against disrupting the Jaguars' set locker room and playing field chemistry is the ultimate line that general manager James Gladstone, head coach Liam Coen, and Executive Vice President of Football Operations Tony Boselli have to guard against.
That is why no matter what the Jaguars do this deadline, from Brian Thomas Jr. to adding new pieces on defense, adding a player who, for the lack of a better team, isn't intangibly rich is the one mistake the Jaguars can not afford to make at the deadline.
While we have not seen the Jaguars make many trade deadline decisions that have backfired in recent years (their most recent trades were for Jakobi Meyers and Ezra Cleveland, two multi-season starters), they can consider themselves the lucky ones. Each year we see a team with an open window, like the Jaguars are now. And each year we see a team flop, like the Indianapolis Colts a year ago.
That is not to say the Sauce Gardner trade has not worked because of Gardner's fit in the Colts' culture. Gardner lost a lot of games with the New York Jets so he is unlikely to be totally phased by the Colts' brand of football, and the real reason that trade hasn't worked out is because the Colts gave it no chance to with the price they paid.
But that is the lesson the Jaguars can learn from. It isn't about adding the right fit on or off the field, at least not completely. It is about reading the room and knowing which moves can, and which moves can't, take you over the top. The Gardner trade never seemed like it was going to make that difference for the Colts, and the Jaguars can't afford to make a similar mistake this trade deadline.
“Yeah, that's a lot of it when you're going through potential options, things like that. You start with, okay, does this player make us better or not? Yes or no? And then, is it going to fit what we're doing, how we operate, the locker room, all that stuff is very important with it and you can't just reach and grab," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week.
Everyone wants to add a pass-rushing defensive tackle, for example. But what about the fact the Jaguars' defense is hitting all cylenders with Arik Armstead and Ruke Orhorhoro as their prime pocket pushers. And while a veteran safety makes a lot of sense, is it worth disrupting the recent play of Rayuan Lane and his fit in Anthony Campanile's defense?
Those are the questions the Jaguars will have to ask themselves. They can not mortgage the future for a deal that will not put them over the top. And they also can't afford to take a big swing on a player who might not be the exact fit for what they are looking for in their culture.
"History shows, a lot of those situations. And then obviously last year, with Jakobi [Meyers], that was one of those that really just fit. You're always looking for that fit and it's so much about the person, the competitor, the football character, that is everything that you look at when making any of these types of decisions," Coen said.
"I'm sure a lot of teams are going through similar processes right now but it's very important, especially when you've got a good thing kind of going, that you're intentional with the background and making sure that the player is in the headspace to come in and fit what we're doing.”

title: Jaguars Stock Report: Parker Washington's Value Continues to Soar After Week 9
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars ... do not have much to worry about after nine weeks.
The Jaguars are of course dealing with a few season-ending injuries to key players like Davon Hamilton, Eric Murray, and Anton Harrison. They also have the looming NFL Trade Deadline, w hich could change both the ceiling and floor for the squad as they make a playoff push over the second-half of the season.
Jacksonville is also fresh off a 33-10 domination of the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football that forced the national football audience that they are for real at 6-2. So, a lot of things are pointing up, and the Jaguars could still look different within the next few days.
So, which Jaguars have their stocks on the rise after Week 9 , and who is trending the opposite way? We break it down below.
Parker Washington only had two catches on Thursday, and one of his failed targets (a drop on a screen) should have been a touchdown. With that said, he had the most important play of the game with his 50-yard catch-and-run against the blitz, proving that his connection with Trevor Lawrence is the one the Jaguars will hone in on when they need a play. But amongst all else, his volume has continued to prove that he is the offense's focal point, even if it doesn't happen every game.
Washington only had two targets in a run-heavy blowout of the Indianapolis Colts that ended at halftime in Week 8, but he did see seven targets come his way on Thursday. This comes after he had 20 combined targets in the two-game London span. Outside of a Cincinnati Bengals game that saw some missed chances and then the Colts game, Washington has been targeted like a WR1 more often than not. That is the value he has ahead of his eventual payday, which seems to be more and more of a sure thing as the season goes on.
The Jaguars have a serious need at the safety position entering the trade deadline. Part of the reason that is the case is because the Jaguars have not really cut it loose with rookie safety Jalen Huskey. The Jaguars had injury issues in Weeks 5 and 6 at the safety spot but still opted to not let Huskey see the field defensively. He has played 27 snaps on defense the last two weeks due to blowouts, but the Jaguars do not seem to be in a rush to see him in an expanded role apart from that.
If the Jaguars do end up adding a safety at the deadline, then it might be a question of whether Huskey will be active. He plays hard and can be a special teams piece, but right now it seems like he might be inching closer to a red shirt season despite the amount of injuries the Jaguars have faced at safety.
Jaguars cornerback Montaric Brown has made a big difference on the defense since he has gotten back from injury. Perhaps it is due to the level of quarterback the Jaguars have played in Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano, but the pass defense that allowed big plays in previous weeks has been much tighter since the bye week. The only big difference since the bye week though has been the return of Brown, who injured his hamstring in Week 3, missed Weeks 4 and 6 with it, and played just six snaps in Week 5 in the process.
Since coming back healthy from the bye week, Brown has had two good games in coverage. He allowed just 27 yards in 32 coverage snaps against the Indianapolis Colts, and he followed it up with a game against the Ravens where he allowed three catches for just 18 yards while also recording an interception. He has been limiting yards after the catch and explosive plays and the play of the secondary has elevated as a whole.
The Jaguars' staff has raved about the work of fourth-round rookie defensive end Wesley Williams in practice over the last few weeks, with both Liam Coen and Anthony Campanile deeming him as a riser. So, why is he tabbed with the stock down designation after the Ravens game? Simply because Williams has still yet to see the field during the regular-season as a rookie, earning his eighth-consecutive healthy scratch inactive in Week 9 against the Baltimore Ravens, which the Jaguars won 33-10.
Williams has been a healthy scratch each week in favor of undrafted defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr., and he was once again inactive on Thursday despite starting defensive end Travon Walker being listed as questionable. Walker ended up playing in the game after going through a pre-game workout, but it seems like the only chance Williams has of being up is if two defensive ends (including the still-injured B.J. Green) are inactive. After half a year, that has turned into a redshirt rookie season offcially.
Tanner Koziol did not have much of a role at all over the first month or so of the season outside some special teams snaps here and there. But the fifth-round rookie out of Houston has seen more and more snaps as the Jaguarshas picked up momentum during their productive three-game stretch, dating back to more snaps in a close and important game against the Houston Texans in Week 6 to prove it isn't just a case of recent blowouts.
The last three weeks have seen Koziol average 14 snaps a game after playing just 19 snaps during the first five games of the season. And after Koziol did not see a pass thrown his way through the first six games of the year, he suddenly has three catches for 23 yards over the last two weeks, including a two-catch, 15 yard performance against the Ravens. Far from eye-popping numbers, but he is playing in more and more three-tight end sets and should see his role continue to grow.

title: Latest Jaguars, Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Deadline Rumors: Separating Fact From Fiction
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The NFL Trade Deadline is nearly 72 hours away, and there isn't much more time to see what happens with Brian Thomas Jr.
The Jacksonville Jaguars' third-year receiver has been perhaps the most central name in all trade deadline discussions amongst NFL receivers. The Jaguars have held firm on keeping Thoma s dating back to last season, even with his production taking a massive dip in the first eight games of the 2026 season.
The Jaguars have not benched Thomas coming out of the bye week, but they haven't exactly made him a central piece of the offense either. They have played in two blowouts, and he caught a touchdown in one of them, but Week 9's battle with the Baltimore Ravens was the first game in his career in which he didn't register a target.
So, what do the latest rumors and reports say about Thomas entering the trade deadline weekend? And what seems like it is the cloest to being the true story? We break it all down below.
According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, there are a few teams at the top of the list looking for potential wide receiver help at the trade deadline: the Kansas City Chiefs, the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the San Francisco 49ers. This is not the first time the Chiefs and Steelers have been connected to a potential Thomas market, and it feels more and more like if there was a team in the running for Thomas just in terms of interest for Thomas, it would be Kansas City.
The Chiefs, Steelers and 49ers are among the teams calling around for WR help, and it’s a good bet multiple receivers will be traded by Tuesday’s deadline, with Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs and Calvin Ridley among names to watch. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/2WjDotsn76 pic.twitter.com/EXwFunbaum
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport noted the Jaguars, "also could wind up dealing wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., whom they have received multiple inquiries on in recent years while resisting all overtures. Thomas played only 19 snaps during Thursday night's victory in Baltimore and did not catch a pass. The Kansas City Chiefs have continued to be intrigued by Thomas."
This seems to all point to the Chiefs as a team badly wanting Thomas. Whether the Chiefs actually make sense is another question. The Chiefs have been a contending team in the AFC all season long and they look like they will be competing with the Jaguars for seeding at the top of the AFC's playoff picture later on in the season.
Would any NFC teams make sense? The 49ers have been noted as a top team in the receiver trade market, though trading a top talent to the 49ers would be just a bit removed from trading him to the Chiefs. The 49ers look like one of the top Super Bowl favorites in the NFC alongside the Chicago Bears, and what if the Jaguars were to make the Super Bowl and face Thomas in Kyle Shanahan's offense?
Outside of which teams might be interested in Thomas, there is also the question of whether the Jaguars would actually want to deal him, and what kind of price would make them feel comfortable doing so. The Jaguars pushed against all overtures for Thomas in the past, with general manager James Gladstone taking a vocal stance against reports that Thomas was involved in trade talks over the course of the offseason.
“No, we haven't, and there hasn't been a ton of dialogue around that front as teams check in simply because it seems like—I know the word reputable came up earlier—I don't think there's been any reputable statement. We don’t have any real action on any of those fronts," Gladstone said back in March.
Things have changed since then, of course. That quote was a month-plus before the Jaguars drafted players like left guard Emmanuel Pregnon, wide receiver Josh Cameron, and tight ends Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol to improve their running game and increase their rate of 12 and 13 personnel. Cameron has also established himself as an exciting developmental piece in the receiver room behind Thomas, which the Jaguars did not have in 2025 or in March of 2026.
The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reports that teams believe the Jaguars will ultimately move Thomas, who has seen his role decrease. Then there are reports like from NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe, who notes that the Jaguars are keeping a close eye on locker room chemistry when it comes to weighing moves. Wolfe went on to mention the Tyson Campbell trade a year ago, which saw a highly popular locker room veteran traded despite the Jaguars having a winning record at 4-1 at the time of the trade.
1 thing to note on Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. trade buzz: Travis Hunter & Thomas are close friends. BT liked in locker room. Speed still an asset w/o production. Jags wonder if Tyson Campbell trade last year had negative impact on immediate locker room energy. Learned from it.…
So, what is real and what isn't when it comes to the Thomas situation? Reports have been pretty consistent: teams like the Chiefs are interested. Teams believe due to his decreasing role he will be dealt. Teams also have had to deal with a Jaguars team that has not appeared to be in a rush to trade the former 1,000-yard receiver.
Those all appear to be the facts of the situation. When you consider the Jaguars' stance, it makes sense. They are pushing for an AFC South title and a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. Why would they lessen their depth and overall talent level for a pick that would not help them today? If the pick was high enough, or if it helped them add a defensive boost, perhaps then it would make sense. But only then.
If the Jaguars were going to trade Thomas, it feels like they would have done it by now. The fact that he is still on the roster after his Week 6 benching and is still well ahead of Cameron on the depth chart suggests they are more than comfortable moving forward with him on the roster. They should be, too, considering how wildly productive their current offensive set-up has been.
Would the Jaguars trade Thomas for the right price? That remains to be seen, but the fact that no trade has occured over the last year suggests nobody has been willing to meet a price the Jaguars would agree to. With the profile of Thomas and need for big-play receivers, it stands to reason that this can only be because the Jaguars' asking price is so high.
Most checks out on Thomas, but it feels like there is a better chance he is a Jaguar on Wednesday morning than otherwise.

title: Chiefs Receive Promising Injury News About Patrick Mahomes With Andy Reid’s Latest Update
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs were able to get back into the win column yesterday against the Jets, several key players went down with injuries. The most concerning was undoubtedly the one suffered by Patrick Mahomes .
On a dropback in the second quarter, Mahomes got tangled up awkwardly with Jets rookie David Bailey , resulting in a strip sack that NY recovered. After the play, the Chiefs' superstar signal-caller was in considerable pain, limping off the field as he favored his right arm.
Although Mahomes returned to the game without missing a single offensive snap, he spent much of the afternoon in game-manager mode with Kansas City winning comfortably. There were still questions about whether he'd miss any time once the adrenaline wore off. Head coach Andy Reid referred to the injury as one in the "elbow region" following the victory, though he was unable to provide a definitive diagnosis. Today, Chiefs fans received much more clarity regarding the situation during Reid's press conference.
"Patrick, he's really day-to-day right now. It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick," Reid told the media on Monday . "It looks like it's just a matter of some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We'll just see where it goes from there, but he's in good spirits today. I have seen him today, so he's in good spirits."
Patrick Mahomes comes off the field in pain with an apparent injury to his throwing arm following a turnover pic.twitter.com/5fsqKGPaFz
Mahomes underwent a subsequent MRI scan yesterday, which thankfully revealed no structural ligament damage. That aligns with Reid calling him "day-to-day" for the time being.
Even if the three-time Super Bowl champion feels lingering effects from the elbow ailment, it sounds like he plans to suit up next Sunday versus the Falcons regardless. He echoed that sentiment when he spoke to reporters after the victory. "If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes confirmed. "That's part of the game, that's part of playing. It scares you in moments where you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn't feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and then was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."
The Chiefs are obviously going to remain cautious with Mahomes considering he's less than a year removed from a major knee injury , but it appears they avoided the worst-case scenario with yesterday's brief scare. "We'll see where he's at [Wednesday]," Reid later added. "He feels pretty good today. He's sore, but I'm glad we're not practicing today."

title: Is the Chiefs' Pass Rush Fixed After Five-Sack Performance vs. Jets?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' pass rush has been a significant topic throughout the 2026 season, often due to disappointing zero-sack games littered throughout the first half of the year. On Sunday against the New York Jets , the defensive line came alive, sacking Geno Smith five times in a blowout victory. So, is the Chiefs' pass rush fully fixed? It's not quite that simple.
First and foremost, it was a great day at the office for Kansas City's pass rushers , particularly Chris Jones and George Karlaftis, who each recorded two sacks. That doubled Karlaftis' season total after entering the game with two sacks on the year, and Jones recorded his first full sacks of the season, bringing him to 2.5 in 2026. Add in one sack from Ashton Gillotte, and you've got the Chiefs' most productive day of quarterback-wrangling in quite some time.
The pressure also wasn't fluky or due to particularly horrendous quarterback play. According to TruMedia , Jones and Karlaftis each had six pressures, while Gillotte had five . Jones was the highest-graded Chief on either side of the ball by Pro Football Focus , and rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas got 28 snaps (44%), a small uptick from his lower-usage dips in Seattle and Denver (29% and 27%, respectively).
It's also worth noting that the Chiefs were without both of their first-round rookies, defensive tackle Peter Woods and cornerback Mansoor Delane . Woods could have helped add more pressure on Smith, while Delane's performance in the secondary theoretically would've bought the D-line even more time to get after the quarterback. I'm not going to adjust for hypothetical sacks, but it's nice to see that performance come at less than full-strength.
That's a lot of positive takeaways. Great day of work for the KC D-line. No notes on this performance. All good things. ...So, are we ready for the other side of the coin?
#Chiefs sacks by week this season 📊 Week 1 — 4 Week 2 — 0 Week 3 — 0 Week 4 — 0 Week 5 — BYE Week 6 — 4 Week 7 — 0 Week 8 — 1 Week 9 — 5 pic.twitter.com/cyYKuTpWYQ
The Chiefs now have 14 sacks in 2026, still the fourth-fewest in the league . Incredibly, 13 of those sacks have come in three games: Week 1 against the Denver Broncos (four), Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers (four), and Sunday against the Jets (five).
In the season-opener, Bo Nix was flummoxed. Against LA, Justin Herbert was playing behind a battered O-line and in an impossibly toothless offense. Against New York, Smith entered the game tied for the second-most sacks taken by any quarterback this season. I wrote about this exact possibility on Saturday.
"It would be a good sign to see them bring Smith down early and often on Sunday, but that's a matchup where the Chiefs should be able to pad their stats," I wrote. "Even if they do find their footing against Smith, they'll have to do it again against better offenses down the stretch."
As impressive as Sunday's performance was, I can't strike any of those comments from the record. That's all still true. Another zero-sack performance would have been disastrous. A mere one-or-two-sack day would have been uninspiring. Five is a stupendous effort, but it's also the second five-sack game the Jets have surrendered this year .
Where does that leave the Chiefs' pass rush? In a much better place than it was before this game, but not all the way to a place of non-concern. I'm hugely encouraged by Jones' performance, seemingly proving that there's still a game-wrecking version of Jones to be found in his age-32 season, and I'm continually impressed by Karalftis' growth as a well-rounded defensive end who is under contract with the Chiefs with a series of reasonable cap hits through the 2030 season .
Led by the stars of the defensive line, the Chiefs did everything you could want from a pressure perspective on Sunday against the Jets. Now, they just have to continue to find multi-sack performances against better lines, better quarterbacks, and better teams.

title: Where the Chiefs Stand Before the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs find themselves in a complex space with the 2026 NFL trade deadline on the horizon. While the club is 6-2 and looks like a team with a Super Bowl ceiling, the roster's talent and health at certain positions raise questions about that upside.
Add in a pair of recent losses to perceived contenders, and it becomes a tricky exercise when attempting to nail down what this year's Kansas City squad truly is. One way to help gain clarity, however, could be making a trade before it's too late.
Ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, let's dive into everything you need to know from a Chiefs perspective, ranging from available capital to ideal fits and much more.
The 2026 NFL trade deadline, in the blink of an eye, is almost here. Each trade-related transaction must be filed with the league office by 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. Make that 3 p.m. CT for those working from the offices up at Arrowhead Stadium.
Some moves may trickle in and be reported after the deadline has passed, which is commonplace in several other sports as well. Expect some potential chaos and perhaps a buzzer-beater or two, in addition to news of trades thats were close but never quite manifested.
One important note is that after the trade deadline and for the remainder of the season, all players become subject to the waiver claim system if released. That includes vested veterans, those with at least four accrued seasons, who would've otherwise gone straight into the free agent pool before the Tuesday cutoff.
Let's break this down into two buckets. One of them is a lot more positive than the other.
Getting the bad part out of the way, the Chiefs simply don't have the funds to make a splash for the type of player many are seeking right now. Estimates for their available salary cap space vary. The NFLPA's public salary cap report , for example, puts Veach at having $1.36M to work with. Spotrac is a bit kinder at rounding up to $1.4M, whereas Over the Cap swings the pendulum in the opposite direction ($1.08M).
There are certain in-season levers that can be pulled to create space, but wiggle room is tough to come by this time of year.
Picks are a totally different story. While it's hard to see Veach parting ways with a first- or second-rounder at this juncture, he's currently projected to possess two picks each in the third and fourth rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft. He also has some picks to swap late on Day 3 of the draft.
Add in a decent complement of 2028 NFL Draft selections, and being hung up on not having that kind of capital shouldn't be the case.
It's safe to say Kansas City has a pretty clear hierarchy of needs with the deadline closing in. Using a combination of current depth chart status, health, recent performances and more, here are the top three positions that make at least some sense to add a body for the final stretch of the campaign.
This is easily the most pressing need the Chiefs have with Tuesday's deadline approaching. The wide receiver room was already on thin ice in September, and that was before Rashee Rice failed to recapture his peak form, Tyquan Thornton sustained a significant ankle injury and Xavier Worthy also went down with a hamstring ailment .
With the free agent market not looking good whatsoever, improvement almost has to come by way of a trade unless a reunion with Tyreek Hill is in the cards. We've outlined some of the more realistic options for Veach and Co., although none of them is going to single-handedly save the season.
It may still be worth it to try, though. Many Chiefs fans want a star now, but that's more of an offseason route. The middle ground for 2026-27's purposes has always seemed to be Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts .
The Chiefs' offensive tackle situation is a tough one.
On one hand, undrafted rookie free agent Kahlil Benson started off the season faring better than just about anyone expected, and veteran Jaylon Moore has enjoyed spurts of productive play in the past. On the other hand, Benson seems to be getting exposed more over time. His peer on the right side of the line also isn't holding up and seems to be hobbled.
Jaylon Moore hobbled off the field & threw his helmet in frustration. He appears to have a lower body injury. Joshua Ezeudu is in at right tackle.
Joshua Ezeudu's usage is interesting at best. He was primarily a piece on the left side of the New York Giants' offensive line before coming over via trade , yet he's been filling in for Moore as needed at right tackle. Waiver pickup Diego Pounds isn't seeing the field barring a serious injury to Benson.
All of this said, it's difficult to envision the Chiefs sinking another real asset into the tackle spot prior to free agency or the 2027 NFL Draft. Of course, the simplest way to potentially see some improvement would be former 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons returning from the injured reserve list and finally making his season debut.
This is more of a luxury possibility. If there's a bad team out there that wants to deal a quality role player at the edge rusher spot or an unexpected high-level contributor comes available for an affordable price, the Chiefs would be wise to pick up the phone. The problem is the odds of either path presenting itself seem remarkably low.
The Kansas City pass rush showed a pulse against the New York Jets, getting to quarterback Geno Smith five times and making an impact on late downs. Star defensive tackle Chris Jones led the way with a pair of sacks , and players like George Karlaftis and Ashton Gillotte also held up their respective ends of the bargain.
It's clear that the latter two are useful players for the defensive end role. There's also the versatility that Jones provides along the defensive front, on top of the same possibilities with former first-rounder Felix Anudike-Uzomah. Should 2025 second-round tackle Omarr Norman-Lott come off the physically unable to perform list , coordinator Steve Spagnuolo would have even more avenues to go down.
That's without mentioning rookie R Mason Thomas , who's as twitched-up and intriguing as any player up front for the Chiefs. It isn't like the team doesn't have a need for more production in the sack department, but the cupboard also isn't bare.
An honorable mention goes to the prospect of landing a nice backup tight end who's a capable blocker. Noah Gray has flashed his pass-catching chops on occasion, but there isn't much depth at the position right now and KC isn't using fullback Ben VanSumeren like many had hoped.
If we're cheating and extending this list to five spots, I'd add linebacker.
According to head coach Andy Reid last week, he and Veach began the discussion process for potential trades "about a month ago." Although these aren't the days of Reid being the executive vice president of football operations like he experienced with the Philadelphia Eagles, he still gets considerable pull when it comes to transactions.
Reid trusts Veach to get the job done if there's a trade to be made.
"Brett does all of that," Reid said. "If he gets to a point where something is up and he feels comfortable about it, then he hits me up on it. He takes care of all of that. Those guys — you know how Brett is wired. He’s endlessly looking for people and trying to bring people on to make us better. That’s how he goes about it.”
Following Sunday's win over the Jets , quarterback Patrick Mahomes echoed a similar sentiment. He has faith in the decision-makers to do the right thing, but he's also confident in the club's internal options if no swaps occur by the deadline.
"I leave that all up to Veach and coach Reid," Mahomes said. "Whoever's in that building, I go out there and try to make the most of it and win football games. I think we've done a great job of that with a lot of different guys. I see the work these guys put in every single day, and they're ready. They're ready to go out there and make plays when their number is called. I leave that up to those guys."

title: The Winners and Losers of Week 9’s Chiefs win over the Jets
full_text:
It may have taken two quarters to put away the now 2-7 New York Jets, but once again, you never apologize for a win in the NFL. The Chiefs dominated the second half after taking a 14-12 lead into the break.
They led 28-12 by the end of the third after the defense allowed minus nine yards and the offense exploded even after a short-lived Mahomes health scare. A late fourth-quarter Emmett Johnson touchdown run sealed the 35-12 win. That score, especially, is one you don’t apologize for, no matter the opponent.
The game was a mixed bag of some hopeful signs of things to come and some frustrations boiling over from recent weeks. Let’s dive into the winners and losers of Week 9.
Defensive tackle Chris Jones 2026 season has officially begun. Week 9 came a little later than expected, but after coming into the game with .5 sacks through seven games, he took down quarterback Geno Smith twice in this game alone. And en route to it, he became the Chiefs' second all-time sack leader with 90 sacks, surpassing Tamba Hali
The first came late in the second quarter. On a third-and-six, Jones dominated a one-on-one situation, pushing the Jets back to a long 53-yard field goal. Jets kicker Jason Sanders was 4-for-4 up to that point, but this one was just far enough to force his first miss. With a make, New York would have gone into halftime up 15-14.
The second one also came on a third down, forcing a punt late in the fourth quarter, a stop that preceded Johnson putting the game away with his touchdown run. Two sacks on third downs are something the Kansas City could have used in their loss to Denver last week. For the Chiefs, hopefully it is a sign of things to come as the second half of the season arrives.
There was a real, heavy moment in this game when some inside Chiefs Kingdom felt the season was sabotaged. The Chiefs led 14-12 against a team they were heavy favorites to beat, and then the biggest scare of the afternoon happened.
Right tackle Jaylon Moore was beaten badly by 2026’s second-overall pick, defensive end David Bailey, and as Mahomes was letting it rip, Bailey violently strip-sacked his fellow Texas Tech alumnus. The mid-throw hit on his elbow put him in obvious pain as he walked off the field with his right arm limp after the Jets recovered the fumble.
As bad as it looked, he didn't miss a single offensive play, even completing a 12-yard pass to tight end Travis Kelce moments later. After the game, additional testing revealed no significant damage, and he was described as having an elbow strain/sprain.
Based on the three touchdown drives he led after the injury, he appears to be in good shape moving forward. Mahomes ended the day going 23-for-31, 242 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Chiefs Kingdom can take a sigh of relief.
After two subpar performances against the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos, star running back Kenneth Walker looked as he did in the first five games of the season. He took 18 carries for 102 yards and scored on a short-yardage touchdown run.
There was one distinct difference, however. This was not one of those games where Walker was a complete magician, forcing double-digit missed tackles. The offensive line was powerful and cohesive, creating massive holes for Walker to run through.
They struggled mightily in pass protection at times, especially the offensive tackles , though guards Trey Smith and Kingsley Suamataia made way with terrific blocks downfield on a 25-yard screen pass that Walker caught for a touchdown. Both Walker and Emmett Johnson averaged 5.7 yards per carry, and they forced only three missed tackles combined, which is a hopeful sign for the big boys up front.
Following Sunday’s game, kicker Harrison Butker is now 12-for-19 in field goal attempts for the season. So far, he's been perfect in only 2 of 8 games, and even then, he went 1-for-1 in both instances.
You have to go back to Week 4 to find a game where Butker didn't miss a kick. With Week 10 on the horizon, Butker’s display this week against New York may have been the most illustrative of how bad things have gotten.
With seconds left in the first half, Butker attempted a 56-yarder that clanked off the upright, but the Jets jumped offsides, giving him a shot from 51 yards. That attempt went completely wide right. He made all five of his extra points, but with how little confidence anyone has in Butker to make a kick, you have to wonder if they will activate Justin Tucker next week in Atlanta.
The Chiefs put 35 points on the board while missing a field goal and turning it over twice, which is fairly impressive. Kansas City came into the game top-five in the NFL in giving the ball away, but they struggled in that area in this Sunday noon game, putting the ball on the ground five times.
The first two fumbles came on the game’s opening drive. In the first return opportunity of his career, rookie receiver Cyrus Allen fumbled the Chiefs' opening kickoff, luckily with linebacker Jeffrey Bassa there to recover. The other was on the ensuing third-and-one when head coach Andy Reid called for a quarterback sneak featuring Justin Fields, and the snap never fully made it into his hands. This time, Kansas City was not so lucky, as linebacker Demario Davis recovered, giving the Jets a 6-0 lead moments later.
Speaking of poor center-to-quarterback exchanges, Creed Humphrey again put the ball out of shotgun for his seventh fumble this season. It was ultimately a drive-killer, leading to one of the Chiefs' three punts on the afternoon. Mahomes fumbled twice on the same drive, and Bailey forced it both times. Moore recovered the first one after giving up the sack. These are unlikely to become trends, but they do help explain the Chiefs' slow start to the ballgame.
The Chiefs faced plenty of questions last week when they marched down the field with less than two minutes to go, clear to the Denver Broncos' 4-yard line with a chance to win the game. The heat came when the Chiefs ran three plays from the 1-yard line.
On third-and-fourth-and-one, quarterback sneaks convert well over 80 percent of the time in the NFL, a much higher success rate than traditional runs or passes. On the two particular plays Kansas City had a shot at last week, it appeared that Mahomes could merely waltz into the end zone in between Humphrey and Smith. Instead, the Chiefs threw an incompletion and had Walker get stuffed, leaving room for criticism.
The Chiefs have not run a sneak with Mahomes taking the snap since 2019, when he injured his knee on the play. He didn't run it today either, but Reid called for it with Fields under center on the very first drive of the game, and to say it went poorly would be an understatement. Fields fumbled before he could even try to get a push. With it being such an easy button around the league, hopefully Reid and company will examine the play for next time, rather than abandon it altogether.

title: After Historic Sack Feat in Week 9, Chris Jones Credits More Than Himself
full_text:
One of the most glaring issues for the Kansas City Chiefs this season has been their lack of a pass rush. There's more context to it than that, but either way, Sunday's 35-12 throttling of the New York Jets provided a return to normalcy in many regards.
Leading the charge was star defensive tackle Chris Jones, who tallied a pair of sacks on the afternoon after producing just a half-sack in the seven games prior. It served as an in-season renaissance for someone who's long been regarded as a premier interior lineman, even if he hasn't played like it in 2026.
Jones' Week 9 performance meant more than that, though. His sacks were enough to surpass Tamba Hali, a longtime defensive stopper in KC and a career Chief, for the second most in franchise history.
Business is booming today for the CEO 💼 Congratulations, @StoneColdJones ! pic.twitter.com/0iFQtoWe90
The monumental achievement is just another example of Jones' greatness, but he isn't necessarily viewing it that way. Speaking to the media following Sunday's win, the seven-time Pro Bowler expressed gratitude to everyone who's supported him over the years.
"It's a testament to all my teammates," Jones said. "One person gets the credit, but it takes a village. It takes a lot of unselfish teammates for me to be successful. Especially to get 90 sacks, it's not an easy task, but it takes a lot of unselfish individuals. Super grateful for the teammates on this journey, 11-year journey that I've had, in order for me to even get close to that."
That includes Hali and other Chiefs of the 2010s who were still around when Jones entered the NFL as a second-round pick back in 2016.
"When I came here, I had Tamba, Justin (Houston), a lot of guys who had a lot of success on this team before me," Jones said. "I was able to sit on the bench and watch these guys. Watch how they prepare, watch what they eat, how they prepare throughout the week. I was able to learn a lot from those guys. I actually still talk to Tamba. My son plays on his seven-on-seven team. We're still very close, so to pass him with all the work and sacrifice he made for this organization, it means a lot."
It's been a slow-burning season in the sack department for Kansas City; Steve Spagnuolo's defense entered Sunday's play tied for the fewest in the league with nine. That's despite the club now sitting 10th in pressure rate, per TruMedia , and also batting down seemingly countless passes in recent weeks. The duality has also reflected in Jones' season production to this point.
According to NFL Pro , Jones' pressure total before Week 9 was just 14, accompanied by a 6.7% quarterback pressure clip and a career-worst 3.15-second average time to pressure. Versus New York, he managed to come away with six pressures on 29 attempts, as well as three "quick" pressures of fewer than 2.5 seconds. His average get-off was 0.85 seconds, 0.08 seconds quicker than his threshold in Weeks 1-8.
It isn't just outlet variance coming to Jones' aid, either. Pro Football Focus , for example, gave Jones five pressures and three hurries in its preliminary grading for Sunday's outings.
Following another quiet showing against the Denver Broncos in Week 8, Jones said "the sack part is kind of overrated" and urged folks to not get "too involved in the back-and-forth with the sacks and stats." It's a valid line of thinking, but coming close to finishing the job and still falling short gets old after a while. He, Spagnuolo and the rest of the defensive line know that.
Now that he's back in the sack column twice over and has climbed up the historical Chiefs ranks in the process, Jones is taking a different approach with a victory in the books.
"Listen, I know last week, I was like, 'Sacks don't matter,'" Jones said. "I lied. Sacks are everything."

title: Chiefs Fans Aren’t Thrilled About Andy Reid’s Sarcastic Response To Failed QB Sneak
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs boast a 6-2 record and are legitimate Super Bowl contenders at the midseason mark, fans are finding themselves in a weird place with the organization. KC has received widespread criticism over the controversial signing of Justin Tucker and a handful of questionable personnel decisions.
Andy Reid and Co. snapped their two-game losing streak with a blowout win over the Jets earlier today . After the victory, though, Reid ruffled some feathers with his postgame comments. Before the Chiefs began to pull away in the second half, the Jets dominated the time of possession battle and only gave Kansas City the ball for a little over a minute in the first quarter. During the offense's first drive, they faced a third-and-1 situation — an area the Chiefs have had difficulty converting all season — and dialed up a quarterback sneak with backup signal-caller Justin Fields. Needless to say, that play failed miserably.
The Chiefs FINALLY attempt a QB sneak, subbing in Justin Fields... - stopped short - ruled to have lost a fumble after Jets challenge😳 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/QvtjSWmjDz
When Reid was asked about the turnover during his press conference, he provided a snarky retort that Chiefs Kingdom wasn't particularly fond of. "I mean, you guys asked for it, so we gave it to you, and it didn't work. How'd you feel?" Reid sarcastically joked. "Listen, those are hard to practice live. A quarterback sneak is hard to practice unless you do it in a game. So, we just got to get those two on the same page."
Andy Reid on the failed QB sneak attempt with Justin Fields vs the Jets: “I mean, you guys asked for it, so we gave it to ya, and it didn't work. How'd you feel?” Adds: “Those are hard to practice live. A quarterback sneak is hard to practice unless you do it in a game.” pic.twitter.com/Ccf6sQqRVy
Throughout the course of the season, the Chiefs have struggled mightily with short-yardage conversions. Coming into today's contest, they were an NFL-worst 2-for-13 on goal-to-go carries, which sparked many media questions about why they hadn't followed suit with the rest of the NFL and embraced a quarterback sneak.
The decision to use Fields over Patrick Mahomes is understandable, as Reid is still haunted by a past incident involving the play. Mahomes suffered a dislocated right kneecap on a quarterback sneak back in 2019, which forced him to miss two games. Ever since then, he has been reluctant to call it. Even so, that hasn't prevented Kansas City fans from calling out the coaching staff. The dismissive, almost condescending , nature of Reid's response to the media has sparked outrage among the fanbase.
Let's take a look at what some of KC Sports Network's contributors had to say about the remarks:
That was a league worst version of a play that the whole league has used successfully. https://t.co/GT26f52EcY
As Swanson pointed out, many teams have successfully incorporated the quarterback sneak into short-yardage situations, most famously the Eagles and Jalen Hurts with the tush push. Certain offenses with less bulky quarterbacks even use tight ends for the push, such as AJ Barner of the Seahawks or Connor Heyward of the Steelers.
WOOF. This is some next level pettiness. https://t.co/JV2vviUlC1
The list of complaints goes on and on.
THIS DOESN'T MAKE IT ANY LESS OF A COACHING MALPRACTICE
Reid's comments made it seem as though the team will look to perfect the play moving forward. Many KC supporters are quite certain that they won't see it again anytime soon, though.
RIP Chiefs QB sneak Born Nov 8, 2026 Died Nov 8, 2026
Quarterback sneaks aren't the only possible solution to their short-yardage woes, either. As good as Kenneth Walker has been in his first year in the red and gold — and he's been pretty dang good — he's never been known as a bruising back. That's exactly what Kareem Hunt was used for the past two seasons, a role in which he amassed 15 touchdowns on the ground despite posting below-average rushing efficiency.
Regardless of how well a team is performing in the NFL, fans who pay their hard-earned money to go to games and dedicate their Sundays to the franchise are never going to take this kind of attitude lightly. It almost feels as though Reid was blaming the media and fans for his coaching staff's failure to execute a play that countless offenses in the league utilize every week.
With the Chiefs already facing criticism over their handling of the kicker situation, it's safe to say that many fans are on edge with Reid right now.

title: Chiefs Relieved but Not Out of the Woods After Patrick Mahomes' Injury Against Jets
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs made things look easy down the stretch of their Week 9 win over the New York Jets , but there were some tense minutes near the end of the first half. For a brief moment, every last bit of excitement was sapped from Arrowhead Stadium when quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered an injury.
Late in the second quarter of Sunday's game, the superstar signal-caller took a hard hit from Jets defensive end David Bailey as he wound up his throwing motion. The result was a sack-fumble on second-and-10, recovered by fellow edge rusher Will McDonald in Kansas City territory.
Mahomes briefly remained on the ground before grabbing at his right arm and being helped to the sideline. He ultimately returned for the ensuing Chiefs possession, but to say many folks' breath was held may not be an understatement.
Here is the video of Mahomes’ injury. pic.twitter.com/GePW0WYZET
Speaking to the media after the game, head coach Andy Reid described it as an injury to Mahomes' "elbow region." Mahomes himself said more testing is coming to determine the exact specifics of the ailment, including the precise location on the arm, but he wasn't going to stay on the sideline if he didn't have to despite the frightening sequence.
"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes said. "That's part of the game, that's part of playing. It scares you in moments where you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn't feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and then was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."
Mahomes played most of the second half before giving way to backup Justin Fields to effectively kneel the 35-12 game out in the waning moments of the fourth quarter. He revealed that he didn't feel he was throwing "the way" he wanted to coming out of the break, although that improved with reps. His focus is now squarely on getting good results from looming tests and preparing for Week 10.
"I feel good now," Mahomes said. "I mean, obviously, you get the win and the adrenaline's pumping. I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, but we'll get right to it. We'll get to work on it, we'll get ourselves ready to go. It was great to get the win. Now, it's about getting ourselves ready for next week."
7:40 p.m. CT UPDATE: Per a Sunday evening report from Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network , Mahomes' MRI didn't reveal a major injury. It's described as an "elbow strain/sprain."
#Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes underwent an MRI following today’s win and sources say the tests did not reveal a major injury. Mahomes’ elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling. But so far, so good. Mahomes did go back in the game. pic.twitter.com/uWPbBY3Gaa
In the aftermath of what was otherwise a low-stress game, Reid opened up about what was going through his mind when he saw his best player go down with what looked like an alarming injury.
"Get Justin ready," Reid said. "Quickly. That's kind of where you're at on the field. You let your medical people take care of that, and then you've got to kind of put everything back there and get the other guy going. But he's a tough kid. If there's any way he can come back from something, he's coming back. I didn't know until they were getting ready to start that series."
Over the years, Mahomes has fought through numerous injuries to stay on the field. In other instances, he's recovered quicker than expected to get back in the lineup. The biggest hurdle of his career to date, however, was an ACL tear suffered less than a year ago on the same field he got hurt on in Week 9. He admitted that it's always scary when something like an elbow or knee is banged up, but he's glad he seems to have avoided anything major.
Being able to fight through the pain and discomfort had a ripple effect on the rest of the team. In one of the most brutal sports known to man, Reid is grateful to have a quarterback like Mahomes on his side.
"When you have a quarterback that's tough, it affects everybody," Reid said. "That's that position, you're supposed to take everybody's game and help raise it. Part of that is sometimes, when you're banged up a little bit — you're in a vulnerable position back there, so you're going to get banged up a little bit — but if you get banged up, you're able to get back up and go. Nobody does it better than he does it."

title: Chiefs Get Important Xavier Worthy Injury Update After Win Over Jets
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs snapped their two-game losing streak today with an emphatic 35-12 blowout of the Jets . They still sit half a game behind the Denver Broncos for the AFC West division lead, but it was still a game that KC could not afford to lose.
Chiefs fans experienced a rollercoaster of emotions this afternoon , ranging from disbelief over Harrison Butker's back-to-back misses at the end of the first half and anxiety over Patrick Mahomes' apparent arm injury. However, another key player went down with an ailment of his own when the score had already gotten out of hand in the fourth quarter. Xavier Worthy came up lame with a non-contact injury in the closing minutes of the contest, and the Chiefs quickly ruled him out for the remainder of the day. After the win, head coach Andy Reid spoke to the media to provide an update on Worthy's status.
"Xavier tweaked his hamstring," Reid confirmed in his postgame press conference .
#XavierWorthy @Chiefs By video, apparent hamstring injury Unlikely to return Length of absence pending MRI pic.twitter.com/Dkc9c5ma7k
Worthy finished the day with one of his more productive outings of the campaign, catching six passes for 48 yards and coming close to finding the end zone on multiple occasions. However, Reid's latest update suggests that the speedy wideout could be held out a few games.
This is not the first time Worthy has dealt with a hamstring issue as a Chief. He missed his rookie minicamp with a similar injury, though he was able to return without missing any time. Without speculating too much, moderate hamstring strains typically take multiple weeks to fully recover from. Fellow wideout Rashee Rice strained his right hamstring during the Chiefs' win over the Raiders in Week 4, and he didn't return until last week when KC took on Denver.
Worthy had already endured his fair share of early-season struggles through the first half of the year, but Kansas City's thin wide receiver depth makes this a concerning situation. Tyquan Thornton will be out for most of the season while recovering from a dislocated ankle , and rookie Cyrus Allen may have lost any trust he had with the coaching staff after fumbling his first NFL kickoff return earlier today.
If there was any indication that the Chiefs were going to make a move for a wide receiver before Tuesday's trade deadline, Worthy's potential absence only amplifies it. That could come in the form of bringing in Colts standout Josh Downs , or Brett Veach may be willing to part ways with more premium assets given the current state of the receiver room. Without a trade, Kansas City would likely be staring at a potential wide receiving corps of Rice, Jalen Royals, and Allen going into next week's matchup with the Falcons.
More information about Worthy should emerge in the coming days, but hamstrings are always tricky to evaluate. Early signs suggest he could be in jeopardy of missing next Sunday's showdown.

title: 10 Instant Observations From Chiefs' Tremendous Rebound Win Over Jets
full_text:
Following brutal losses in consecutive weeks, the Kansas City Chiefs desperately needed a week in which plenty of things went right. Although everything was far from perfect in Week 9's game against the New York Jets, this was a massive step in the right direction.
Once the Kansas City offense got rolling, the outcome of Sunday's 35-12 win was never in doubt. Thanks to some efficient drives when called for and multiple high-intensity defensive downs, the home team breezed to a blowout triumph against an inferior opponent.
With the victory, the Chiefs snap their two-game skid and rise to 6-2 on the year. Let's jump into 10 instant observations and takeaways from Week 9.
Under defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, the Chiefs have typically been known to start a little slow and get going as the action unfolded more. Spagnuolo's in-game adjustments are second to few in the league, but that oftentimes comes with a growing pain or two on early possessions. Sunday was no different right out of the gate, although the end result was far from the worst-case scenario.
New York averaged 5.3 yards per play on a 14-play opening drive that took 8:13 off the clock. That also included a third-down conversion by the offense and some shoddy tackling from the Kansas City defense. With that said, the Chiefs' third-ranked red-zone defense lived up to its reputation and held the Jets to a field goal. Minimal harm, minimal foul.
Much has been made about how the Chiefs could've won last Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos had they simply lined up for a quarterback sneak at the end. The team has avoided letting quarterback Patrick Mahomes get under center for one like the plague, which stems from a knee injury in 2019.
Well, a third-and-1 sneak was tried on the first offensive possession of the afternoon, albeit in complete and utter failure. Backup signal-caller Justin Fields fumbled the ball after a weird snap exchange, leading to a successful New York challenge for a turnover.
Earlier this week, head coach Andy Reid said sneaking with tight end Noah Gray would likely be the club's "first call." He later added that an attempt with Fields was possible. Mahomes also spoke about his conversations with Reid regarding the play.
“I'll say that there have been quarterback sneaks in games that we've put in that we will alert and change at the line of scrimmage if they get in those tight fronts," Mahomes said. "Obviously, that wasn't the play in that situation of the game, but it's not like we're scared to call the quarterback sneak. It's just something that we haven't done. We've been able to execute with other things.
"So I don't think coach Reid's put that on me. But at the end of the day, if we can execute with the other things, I'm sure we'll have to make changes. That's something that Coach Reid's not afraid to do, is make changes whenever needed. So we'll see where that goes moving forward.”
It's become increasingly clear that Kansas City isn't going to operate the sneak in a normal way. Plan B doesn't seem to be working, either.
The Chiefs have generally done a respectable job taking care of the football on the year, coming into Week 9 ranked fourth in turnover differential (+5) and trailing just the Washington Commanders, Minnesota Vikings and Jacksonville Jaguars. Mahomes has only made a handful of mind-boggling decisions, and running back Kenneth Walker's been as reliable as anyone all year long.
It's the other members of the roster who haven't always held up their end of the bargain; Sunday was a prime example of that. In the opening two frames, specifically, a variety of fumbles took place. Sure, two of them were from Mahomes, but those can largely be chalked up to the aforementioned offensive line struggles.
Rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen is credited with another, taking place on the game's opening kickoff. Kansas City must tighten up the ball security, as these weren't the only instances of lackluster control. Better — and perhaps luckier — opponents will take advantage of self-inflicted mistakes.
Much has been made of the Chiefs' offensive tackle situation, and for good reason. On the left side of the line, the absence of Josh Simmons is lasting much longer than anyone anticipated, putting undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson in a precarious position. The first-year man looks worse with more tape out on him, along with better defenses being faced.
On the other side, veteran Jaylon Moore missed one week of play due to being in the concussion protocol but hasn't even been an average pass blocker at times when on the field. Concerns regarding both players culminated with an ugly opening half of play, including multiple strip-sacks of Mahomes and an injury to the two-time NFL MVP:
This is a close-up look at the injury to Patrick Mahomes: pic.twitter.com/suH7qpyLV9 https://t.co/BplvdRnJVG
According to Pro Football Focus ' live tracking for the first half, Benson and Moore surrendered three pressures each. Moore lost to rookie pass rusher David Bailey on a couple of occasions, and Benson owned a horrific 8.6 pass blocking grade.
Simmons can't be counted on to walk through the door, but internal improvement or consistency simply must be established for the long run.
It feels like beating a dead horse by now, but it must remain a talking point for as long as it's an issue. Once again, the Chiefs have a Harrison Butker problem on their hands, as the three-time Super Bowl champion continues to look like a shell of himself on field goal attempts.
Butker came into Sunday's game 12-for-18 on field goals, just two-thirds being made, and also had a missed extra point. He then had a 56-yard miss lead to a do-over after a penalty, only to miss the ensuing 51-yarder in the same fashion. This train doesn't seem to be reversing course anytime soon.
Speaking to the media this week, special teams coordinator Dave Toub backed Butker as the team's kicker when asked about the process of choosing between him and the recently-signed Justin Tucker .
“Because Butker’s our kicker," Toub said. "Butker, he's on our team, and we're paying Butker. And Butker has won a lot of football games for us. Butker is a champion, and he deserves the right to be exhausted on this thing, and we're going to exhaust every possibility with him.”
Most other teams would've moved on from Butker at this stage, even with all he's done for the organization. Legacy shouldn't prevent the right decisions from being made.
Father Time is undefeated, and defensive tackle Chris Jones is finding that out as much as anyone on the Kansas City roster. He entered the weekend with just half a sack on the season, which is far from what everyone's grown to expect from the proclaimed 'CEO of Sack Nation' over the years.
Reid didn't seem concerned about Jones' lack of statistical production when he spoke to the media this week, however.
"Going back to Chris, I mean, Chris is giving his all," Reid said. "He's doing everything he can do. He gets doubled from various angles. He's going to draw a lot of attention, and so that's [an] advantage to the other guys to have a chance to get themselves home. So as much emphasis is put on Chris, let's take advantage of that and get ourselves on the quarterback. Not just to the quarterback, but the quarterback.”
Regardless of whether Jones is back close to peak form, he flashed improved burst and closing ability in Week 9. Late in the first half, his third-and-6 sack of Jets quarterback Geno Smith ended the club's drive and helped keep the Chiefs' lead intact entering the break. He added another third-down sack in the fourth quarter for good measure.
KC has to be thrilled with that showing.
After an absolutely red-hot start to the season, Walker's return to Seattle saw him muster just 36 rushing yards on 14 carries. title: Live Game Thread & Updates for Kansas City Chiefs vs.  New York Jets in Week 9
full_text:

NY is alternating Breece Hall and Braelon Allen in the backfield. 6:47: An excellent drive by the Jets stalls on the goal-line. title: Time for Chargers to Have Uncomfortable Ladd McConkey Conversation After Latest Injury
full_text:
When it comes to the Los Angeles Chargers , it’s all eyes on whether they will be big sellers at the NFL trade deadline and the possible hot seats of Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel.
Don’t forget, unfortunately, the latest Justin Herbert injury that could cost the star quarterback time.
There are other issues, too, but there’s one to circle in red way down the list that deserves more attention than it’s getting right now: Ladd McConkey is hurt again .
The latest Ladd McConkey injury was one of the strangest yet.
McConkey wasn’t a major point of concern on the injury report all week, which in of itself is pretty rare now. But by the time the game kicked off, the Chargers had already ruled him "questionable" to return. Only reporting later attempted to clear the air: He was dealing with back spasms during pregame warmups.
So, the uncomfortable McConkey topic: He’s not reliable.
The Chargers are 0-8. When thinking about long-term building blocks, McConkey’s name should be right there next to guys like Herbert, Joe Alt, Omarion Hampton and Tuli Tuipulotu, to name a few.
McConkey is about to turn just 25 years old and is on a rookie contract. He should make that list. But frankly, he’s regressed statistically every single season since his rookie debut (82 catches, 1,149 yards, seven scores) and questions about his size (listed at 185 pounds, 6’0”) seem warranted after the injuries have piled up.
McConkey has a massive list of injuries, soft-tissue and otherwise, on the resume. In no special order, we’re talking about knee strains, calf strains, rib fractures, concussions, foot injuries and now this back issue.
Limited attendance here disrupts both McConkey and the Chargers’ offense. He played 73 percent of the snaps over 14 starts as a rookie. He played 78 percent over 12 starts last year. He’s started just three games in 2026 at 53 percent of the snaps.
There are obviously other major problems for the Chargers across the board. And there’s a conversation about the organization's training and approach to injury prevention worth having, too, because the injury rate in Los Angeles on an annual basis borders on preposterous.
But specifically with McConkey, it makes him unreliable. Quentin Johnston has drop issues and Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith haven’t fully emerged. McConkey should be the No. 1 and a critical piece.
Going into a draft where the Chargers might pick first and get Jeremiah Smith to pair with McConkey, that sounds good. But so did bringing McDaniel to Los Angeles to help Herbert.
Realistically, the Chargers have very few proper building blocks for three-plus years down the road right now. And things have hit a point with McConkey where it’s even worth questioning if he classifies as one of those.
