title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers Defense Breaks as Offense Watches Helplessly
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel tried a new approach against the Texans. McDaniel moved from on the field to the booth to call the game, the results were the same. The Chargers lost, again.
The Chargers' trainwreck of season continued in week nine against the Houston Texans. The final score of the game was 44-22; a final score that makes the game feel more competitive than it actually was. Los Angeles has now fallen to 0-8 on the season.
The Chargers offense continues to be unable to score and remains frustratingly inefficient. Despite being winless on the season, head coach Jim Harbaugh is not adjusting his coaching style, he maintains a conversative approach, opting for field goals instead of going for fourth-down attempts.
Los Angeles' defense has been the lone bright spot for the team this season. The defense has consistently put their best foot forward and gone to battle week in and week out despite the offense not holding up their end of the bargain. The defense was bound to have a bad day at the office and that day came this week against the Texans. Houston quarterback CJ Stroud appeared dialed in and carved up the Chargers defense. Even when the coverage was perfect, passes were still caught.
NICO COLLINS, ARE YOU KIDDING ME?!? 🤯 (via @HoustonTexans ) pic.twitter.com/zv7Zrgbuf0
There were several developments that happened before, during and after this beat down that are worth discussing for the Chargers. Let's dive into the biggest takeaways.
Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has dealt with every injury imaginable this season and his role in Mike McDaniel's offense has left him downrange for massive hits across the middle. He played only his second full game of 2026 in week eight afte coming off a bye. McConkey experienced back spasms in pregame warm ups in Week 9 and did not play a single snap against the Texans.
Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz brought in Cole Strange and gave him a low-level starters contract to be the Chargers new right guard after spending most of the season with Mike McDaniel and the Miami Dolphins in 2025. Everyone outside of the Chargers building suspected this may not go well.
It is not breaking news that the Cole Strange experiment has been awful. He has been the worst offensive lineman the Chargers have had on the field this season and the grades make that clear. Still, the Chargers rolled him out there every week but finally Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins took him behind the woodshed today, to the point where the broadcast was nearly laughing about how bad he was being beaten on a down to down basis.
The Chargers finally pulled him and rotated Branson Taylor and rookie Alex Harkey. Head coach Jim Harbaugh did say that Strange may have lost his starting job and they will look at it this week.
After 37 consecutive drives, the Chargers finally scored a touchdown as Quentin Johnston broke a tackle and broke free for a 57 yard catch and run. When asked about the streak ending, tight end Charlie Kolar had no idea it had been that many drives without a touchdown.
#Chargers TE Charlie Kolar had no idea the offensive did not score in 37 straight drives. 💀😅 “37!?” Kolar said. “I wish you never told me that.” @SportingTrib | #BoltUp pic.twitter.com/nlcpzub7TS
It appears breaking a bone now appears to be an annual tradition for Justin Herbert. Late in the third quarter Herbert stiffed armed away a would be sack and immediately looked down at his finger. In true Justin Herbert fashion, he did not come out of the game and actually finished the drive with the touchdown to Quentin Johnston.
Herbert went to the sideline and the blue medical tent and emerged with a glove with a massive temporary cast on his finger. The specific injury has not been announced but the broadcast did capture his finger pointing in an unnatural direction. Backup quarterback DJ Uiagalelei finished the game and threw his first career touchdown pass.
The Chargers are driving the NFL world mad with their apparent stance that they will not trade anyone. There is an argument that because the Chargers do not have high-value trade assets, the late Day 3 picks that they could get in return are not worth moving on from as they try to right the ship heading into 2027.
oh but remember, they don't want to make anyone feel discouraged!
It is worth noting that edge rusher Caleb Murphy who has mainly logged special teams snaps since he returned to the Chargers, did function as the fourth edge against the Texans despite Bud Dupree being active. Either Dupree has been demoted or Murphy may be getting a look in the event that Khalil Mack is moved before the trade deadline despite all the public statements that he will not be moved. Dupree has not logged snaps on defense since week five.
All eyes now shift to the Chargers front office ahead of the deadline. Will they still stand pat and move no one? Or will they move a player or two at the deadline?

title: Justin Herbert Injury: How Does Chargers QB’s Setback Impact NFL Trade Deadline?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have fallen to 0-8, already finding themselves in what we all thought was the worst possible situation for the franchise after their semi-successful 2024 and 2025 seasons. Unfortunately, in classic Chargers fashion, it got worse .
Justin Herbert suffered a finger injury , playing through the injury for a few plays, eventually moving to the blue medical tent once the offense was off the field. Once it was time for the offense to go back on the field, Herbert stayed back and found himself on the bench watching backup QB DJ Uiagalelei finish out the blowout loss at the hands of the Houston Texans.
While information has yet to be finalized on the exact injury Herbert has suffered, it seems that the consensus is a broken middle finger on his non-throwing hand. Herbert has played through broken fingers before, but it seems that the team may need time to consider if he should continue to play and risk more injury.
Now, with this hesitancy, this could very well change the Bolts' outlook on the NFL trade deadline, which is right around the corner, being marked as Nov. 10, 2026.
With the Bolts being 0-8, NFL teams were rightfully calling Los Angeles to ask about some of the team's players in hopes of hoping their own roster. The Chargers should be answering those calls and looking to build for their future, not for the 0-8 2026 Chargers.
Unfortunately, Joe Hortiz has seemingly been unwilling to move away from players, with reporters saying the Chargers "still have belief" prior to this Texans loss. Now, with another loss and their star QB injured, can they finally turn the other way and sell off assets?
Of course, only time will tell, but it was only logical when the team was 0-5; it is even more logical with the team being 0-8 and with an injured QB. To go full fire-sale mode, some names to look out for on the trade market:
Khalil Mack: The most spoken-about trade asset . He has mentioned he does not want to be traded, but it is worth mentioning that the veteran EDGE has plenty of value to other teams...if Mack were to change his mind.
Donte Jackson: Another veteran who could have some value for a team in need of a starting-caliber DB. Even with the Chargers having injuries piling up at the position, it could be smart to let young practice squad players play rather than letting Jackson play for no team-related upside.
Dalvin Tomlinson: One of the team's better run defenders could find his way on the market, as he is playing well, is healthy and is 32 years old. The Chargers have other options in Jamaree Caldwell and Nick Barrett who could take some snaps as the position.
Daiyan Henley: A young LB who had a 2024 season filled with promise. He had an interception against the Houston Texans, but he is obviously in need of a fresh start. He could possibly be valued highly around the league considering his age and history of strong play.

title: Where the Chargers Stand 48 Hours Before the  NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are officially at a crossroads. What was supposed to be a season of competing and building momentum has turned into something entirely different. At 0-8, the Chargers have reached a point where simply looking ahead to the next game isn’t enough.
Sunday’s game was another reminder of how much work remains for this team. Eight games into the season, the Bolts still cannot get into rhythm.
Now, general manager Joe Hortiz has to determine what makes the most sense for the organization moving forward. They don’t necessarily need to abandon everything they have been building, but continuing to approach the season as if a turnaround is right around the corner could be a mistake.
One of the biggest questions heading into Tuesday is whether they will seriously consider moving veteran players. I know they are firm on not dealing any of their guys whatsoever.
However, When a team is sitting at 0-8, the conversation surrounding potential trades naturally changes. Players who might have been considered untouchable earlier in the season could suddenly become part of a much larger discussion. With every loss more becomes possible.
Khalil Mack is an interesting name in that conversation. His experience and production make him valuable, especially to teams that believe they have a legitimate opportunity to compete this season.
There is also the question of what the Bolts could realistically receive in return. A trade only makes sense if the compensation matches the value of what the organization is giving up. Accumulating draft picks is important, but those selections eventually have to translate into players who can help change the direction of the franchise.
The same approach should apply to any other veteran who could generate interest around the league. Hortiz needs to evaluate the roster honestly rather than make decisions based solely on the disappointment of the current record.
Perhaps the most important part of this situation is what happens once Tuesday passes. The Chargers still have the remainder of the season to evaluate their roster, develop younger players and determine which areas require the most attention heading into the offseason.
There is no reason to make unnecessary moves simply because the season has gone poorly. However, there is also little reason to ignore opportunities that could improve the team beyond this year. The Chargers have reached a point where the remainder of the season should be about finding answers. Tuesday’s deadline gives the organization its first major opportunity to act on that reality.
Honestly, there's no salvaging the season. The question is whether the decisions made over the next 48 hours can help prevent another season like this one.
The Chargers are reportedly not trading players ahead of the deadline. Per ESPN, they do not want to send the message that they are quitting on the season. title: Chargers' Justin Herbert Suffers Injury During Blowout Loss
full_text:

title: NFL Trade Deadline Speculation Wonders About Justin Herbert to Vikings
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has suddenly been connected to speculation involving the Minnesota Vikings, creating an interesting conversation about what a potential blockbuster trade between the two organizations could look like.
NFL reporter Albert Breer wrote that the Vikings should at least inquire about Herbert, as it wouldn't hurt anything at all. Breer noted that “I wouldn't mind the Vikings taking a swing on this.” With the Bolts being winless halfway through the season and Kyler Murray not living up to expectations, this wouldn't be a stretch by either side.
However, Joe Horitz and Jim Harbaugh have made it crystal clear that Herbert is not available and they are sticking with their franchise quarterback.
Obviously moving on from a quarterback like Herbert would be an enormous decision for the organization. His arm strength, ability to make difficult throws, and overall physical tools have made him a major part of the Chargers future. Players with that kind of ability simply do not become available very often.
That is exactly why this situation is so interesting.
For the Vikings, the idea of bringing in Herbert would be a massive opportunity. The Vikings have been looking for long-term stability at the quarterback position, and acquiring someone with Herbert’s experience and ability would immediately change the conversation surrounding the franchise.
A quarterback of Herbert’s caliber would not come cheap. Any team attempting to acquire him would likely have to put together a significant package involving valuable draft capital and potentially additional pieces. We're talking about multiple first-round picks.
Meanwhile, the Chargers would have an equally difficult decision. Moving a player like Herbert would signal a major change in direction, especially considering how important he has been to the organization. It would also raise questions about what the Bolts believe their future should look like and whether the team would be willing to start over at the most important position in football.
At this point, there is a difference between discussing a possible trade and suggesting that something is actually close to happening. Herbert remains a Charger, and speculation involving the Vikings should be treated accordingly. Still, the fact that his name is being connected to a potential move like this is enough to get people talking. If a deal of this magnitude ever became realistic, it would easily become one of the biggest quarterback stories in the NFL. The Vikings would potentially get their franchise quarterback, while the Chargers could find themselves entering an entirely different era.
It is a fascinating possibility, even if it remains just that for now.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: Easiest Matchup for the Bolts Since Week 2
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have reached a point in their season where every opportunity matters.
After a frustrating start, the Bolts return to SoFi Stadium on Sunday to face the Houston Texans in a matchup that could provide a much-needed opportunity to turn things around.
For starters, the Texans have not exactly been the consistent team many expected them to be entering the season. This is particularly important for a team desperately searching for something positive to build on.
The biggest question however, revolves around the Chargers offense and whether it can finally put together a complete performance.
Justin Herbert remains the centerpiece of everything the Bolts want to accomplish offensively.
His ability to extend plays, make difficult throws and create opportunities downfield gives the Chargers an advantage against practically any defense. Unfortunately individual talent has not translated into enough production this season.
The Texans have an aggressive pass rush capable of disrupting an offense, but there are opportunities for them to attack elsewhere. Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter are particularly dangerous, meaning Herbert cannot afford to hold onto the football for extended periods. That makes the offensive line’s performance especially important. The Chargers need to establish some consistency in protection while finding ways to get the football out quickly.
Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and the rest of the receiving group could play significant roles in helping Herbert find an early rhythm.
Another area worth watching is the running game. Omarion Hampton gives them another way to take pressure off its quarterback. Of course, Vidal and Mitchell deserve mentions as well.  If the Chargers can establish a legitimate rushing threat, opponents will have fewer opportunities to send extra pressure and make Herbert panic. The Chargers have shown that their defense can compete, but putting together four consistent quarters remains essential. Allowing Houston to build momentum early would make an already challenging situation considerably more difficult.
There is also an important psychological component to Sunday’s game. The Bolts need something to change, and a victory could provide the confidence this team has been missing. Playing at home gives the Chargers another opportunity to establish momentum, but the responsibility falls on the players to deliver. The Texans have enough talent to make this competitive, particularly with its defensive front. Still, this is a matchup where the Bolts have a realistic opportunity to get back on track.
The Chargers do not need a perfect performance. They need a disciplined one, simple as that.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Reveal Stance on Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey Offers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers will risk falling to 0-8 before the NFL trade deadline this week.
Despite this, so far, the only big change for the Chargers is a little Mike McDaniel news .
As for that NFL trade deadline, the Chargers won’t be sellers . That’s what head coach Jim Harbaugh and everyone else continues to say in public. It’s also what every little bit of reporting says, right up until kickoff on Sunday afternoon.
What’s interesting now, though, is a fresh bit of reporting that says the Chargers indeed have calls on two superstar players, but that the organization is also intent on sending a pretty specific message at the deadline.
Not that this will come as a great shock, but we now have reporting that says the Chargers are indeed getting calls on stars like Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey.
The report, courtesy of ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , says the Chargers are shooting down any questions about those two players.
“The Chargers also don't like the message of giving up on the season,” the report noted. “Calls from rival general managers on Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey and others have received hard nos.”
Schefter and Rapoport also noted that the Chargers are not acting winless in their trade talks and that Khalil Mack’s status as a “pillar of the organization” has them denying any trade calls about the veteran pass-rusher, too.
Other teams wouldn’t be operating properly if they didn’t at least ask the hapless Chargers about names like Herbert and McConkey.
Trading either doesn't really make any sense for the Chargers though. Herbert has a no-trade clause and a staggering number of dead money on his $262.5 million contract extension if they move him. McConkey, despite his injury woes, has proven to be maybe the only viable long-term asset in the passing game.
What the Chargers ultimately do with Harbaugh and McDaniel next offseason is a question mark. But Herbert and McConkey are two guys who will undoubtedly be on the team and serve as foundational building blocks, provided they don’t demand trades or something dramatic.
Any chatter about the Chargers trying to send proper messages and stuff, though, is just cutesy window-dressing on a miserable season. The record and refusal to change outweighs any reported behavior while navigating the trade deadline.

title: The Unseen Strategy Behind the Chargers’ Trade Deadline Stance
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers, despite being 0-7, have bewildered everyone around the NFL with their stance to date of being unwilling to engage in trade talks . The trade deadline is days away and the Chargers front office has made their stance clear heading to the final hours.
As the November 10th trade deadline rapidly approaches, the Chargers have maintained their intention to stand pat and not trade anyone away. The initial belief was the Chargers were going to try to emerge from their week seven bye refocused and with limited reinforcements returning to the field and make an attempt to turn their season around. Along with that belief was that the Chargers would eventually face reality if they lost to the Rams and change their tune heading into week nine winless.
The Chargers lost to the Rams and apparently, still appear unwilling to move on from any players before the trade deadline according to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport in a shared deadline notebook. One of the more confounding quotes mentioned in the notebook is that "The Chargers also don't like the message of giving up on the season."
Whether the decision on messaging is the stance of the front office or the Chargers ownership is unclear. It does appear that the franchise is currently in an odd state of denial about how the 2026 season has gone. The season is over. The Chargers have to operate with that understanding.
Schefter and Rapoport reiterate that the Chargers will not be moving veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack at the deadline. Mack himself has publicly stated that he does not want to be moved. It is possible that Mack has voiced that desire in private as well and the Chargers are simply granting Mack's request. Head coach Jim Harbaugh values Mack's leadership and if the Chargers are going to get some momentum heading into the offseason, Mack's leadership can play a valuable role.
If the goal is to not be giving up on the season, the focus should be to build for the future and get the ship heading in the right direction or at least have a more clear path forward into 2027. With the goal being focused on getting the ship heading in the right direction heading to 2027, why is more draft capital in 2027 not the priority?
General manager Joe Hortiz has already demonstrated the ability to move around the draft board and acquire more capital during the draft. The only value the Chargers would be getting from any of their trade assets would be late day three picks. They do not have a Jeffery Simmons or Jonathan Taylor on the roster to trade and are not looking at a full rebuild.
The mentality for the Chargers is that the short term value to the team is greater than the value of late Day 3 picks in next year's draft class. One of the factors that is currently under-discussed in the deadline narratives is the value of day three picks in the NIL era.
The college football landscape had dramatically shifted since players are now able to make money off of their name, image and likeness. The system overall may be flawed, but it has dramatically changed the landscape of NFL draft prospects. The general consensus is that due to players returning to school for NIL deals, as opposed to forgoing their final seasons of eligibility to enter the draft, the depth of quality prospects has gone down.
Because there are less players to choose from with draftable grades overall, players with lower grades are going earlier in the draft. The downstream effect of this shift has devalued later Day 3 picks. Wide receiver Brenden Rice is the only Chargers seventh-round to pick make the 53-man roster during Joe Hortiz's tenure and he was only active for three games his rookie season.
In this context, the hargers have to weigh the value of current players helping the team for the remainder of 2026 against the value of what they could get in return. Khalil Mack has the highest potential value of any of their trade assets and would likely only bring back a fifth-round pick at best.
Hortiz made multiple trades in this past draft and gathered more capital going that route than the Chargers could gain in trading players away. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler echoes this thought in response to Schefter and Rapoport's deadline notebook.
Good intel here. Chargers still not in seller mode at 0-7. L.A.’s stance seems to be: Can get Day 3 picks any time, so why trade good players for them? https://t.co/pBSaFUrXP3
The current messaging coming from the Chargers could use some cleaning up if they do have a plan. Standing pat at the trade deadline could make sense if they are essentially looking at a two-year plan. Although they have no business being buyers, they could even talk themselves into a minor move or two to aid in that plan.
Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs. He graduated from UC Riverside with a degree in Political Science and The University of Redlands with an MBA.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams’ Win Over Commanders: Myles Garrett Dominates, But Concerns at Wide Receiver Remain
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won their third straight game on Sunday, beating the Washington Commanders 20-13. While it wasn’t pretty, the Rams are above .500 for the first time this season, with Myles Garrett impressing in his return . Let’s get into this week’s 10 takeaways.
Over the last two weeks, the Rams have gotten off to a slow start, but it’s been an issue for much of the season. They have yet to score a touchdown on the opening drive of a game. The Rams rank 24th in first quarter points per game and 17th in first quarter offensive EPA per play. Following the Rams’ opening drive that ended in a field goal, they had back-to-back three-and-outs. Sunday’s game was a 10 a.m. PT start on the road, but the Rams need to find a way to start quicker.
Over the last two months, the Rams have been awaiting Myles Garrett’s return to the field. After he returned to practice last week, Garrett made his return on Sunday in a limited role and made his presence felt. Garrett finished with three sacks, which was more than Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey had all season. He also created a turnover with a forced fumble in the first half that resulted in points for the offense. Late in the fourth quarter, Garrett had a sack that helped stop a late surge by the Commanders. If Sunday was only a glimpse of what is to come, it’s hard not to be excited.
Nacua is carrying way too much of the Rams’ passing game. He finished with 14 catches on 19 targets. It was the fifth time in six games that Nacua had 10 or more targets. It’s also the second time he’s had 15 or more targets in a game. On drives in which Nacua had two or more catches on Sunday, the Rams scored all 20 of their points. When he didn’t, they punted four times and had an interception. It’s simply not sustainable and increases the risk of Nacua getting hurt.
The Rams did not convert a third down until the fourth quarter against the Commanders. Heading into the week, the Commanders ranked 26th in third down defense. The Rams are 6-for-25 on third downs over the last two weeks. Had the Rams not gone 3-for-3 on fourth down, it could have been a long day on offense. The third down operation hasn’t been good enough in recent weeks.
Throughout Aaron Donald’s career, players have experienced an “Aaron Donald effect”. Essentially, Donald was so good and garnered so much attention that other players benefitted. Donald got to experience the other side of that on Sunday. He had his best game of the season, recording nine impact plays according to Sumer Sports. His four pressures were also a season high. Donald came out of retirement to play alongside Garrett, and after the game, it was obvious how much he enjoyed it.
When the offense has struggled over the last two weeks, the defense has stepped up and done its part. After the Rams went 3-and-out on back-to-back drives following the Commanders’ touchdown, the defense forced two quick punts as well. Following the Rams’ two turnovers, the defense responded by forcing a turnover on the next play after one and holding the Commanders to a field goal after the other. The Rams asked their defense to win the game for them late in the fourth quarter and got two crucial stops.
Over the last three weeks, the Rams have found a good balance with their running back rotation. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum have had 10 or more carries in each of the last three games. Williams led the way with 15 carries, while Corum had 11 against the Commanders. Corum had 58 yards on his 11 carries with a long of 15 and also scored a touchdown. Matthew Stafford did throw the ball 43 times, but the Rams were able to lean on the run game when they needed to and the offense had balance.
After Trent McDuffie injured his back at the end of the game against the Chargers, he entered Sunday’s matchup listed as questionable. The Rams were also without Jaylen Watson, who was ruled out for the season with a shoulder injury. With McDuffie and Watson out, the Rams were relying on their depth corners in Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace. Both played well with Forbes having a tackle for loss and two key pass breakups. Wallace remained as steady as he’s been all season. The Rams have asked a lot of their depth cornerbacks this season with injuries and they stepped up again on Sunday.
Dare I say that the Rams’ special teams unit was actually good against the Commanders? Three of Joshua Karty’s four kickoffs hit the landing zone before going through the end zone for a touchback, putting the Commanders at the 20-yard line. Jordan Whittington had a nice kickoff return and Ethan Evans averaged over 50 yards per punt. It was by far the best performance from the special teams unit this season and it will be interesting to see if they can build on it.
When it comes to other teams in the NFC, the Rams likely aren’t in that top tier right now. They are likely a step below teams like the Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers. The Rams remain an imperfect team with clear flaws, but they seem to be finding their stride. After losing to the Cardinals, the Rams have won three straight games. Early in the season, the Rams found ways to lose. Now, they are finding ways to win. Getting to the bye week at 6-4 would be huge, but for the first time, the Rams are above .500, and that’s a step in the right direction.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Finally Get the Myles Garrett They've Been Waiting For
full_text:
Sitting in the press box at the Melbourne Cricket Ground back in September, it was almost depressing watching the Los Angeles Rams trot a limited version of Myles Garrett onto the field . Garrett was very clearly not 100 percent in that game and voiced that afterwards. After not recording a single pressure, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and NFL sack leader walked into the media room and said, “This was the worst version of myself.”
Days later, the Rams placed Garrett on injured reserve, where he remained until Sunday.
The Rams traded away Jared Verse for Garrett in what was their biggest move of the offseason. In a similar thought process to when they traded Jared Goff for Matthew Stafford, the Rams hoped that trading for Garrett would match their current timeline better than Verse. Essentially, they could accelerate that development process.
Garrett was supposed to be the missing piece of the defense and the player who helped them close out games in the fourth quarter. What if the Rams had Garrett available in their losses to the Denver Broncos and Arizona Cardinals? Those were two games the Rams led late in the fourth quarter and the defense was unable to get a stop.
Instead, Garrett watched from the sideline in those games as he managed a knee injury that he’d dealt with since training camp. There was a lot of angst heading into Garrett’s return. Some weren’t even sure if he’d be back before the bye week. Garrett was originally given a six-week timeline before eventually missing seven games. Would he be the same dominant player the Rams had traded for in June?
The answer to that question was yes.
On Sunday, Garrett finished with three sacks, two of which were in the fourth quarter. His first came with him chasing Jayden Daniels from the backside before halftime, forcing a fumble and creating a turnover. That was one play after Puka Nacua and the offense had fumbled and the Commanders were looking to take control of the game.
Garrett’s second sack came on a 2nd-and-9 on Washington’s first drive of the fourth quarter to set up a 3rd-and-14. While the Commanders ended up converting, Garrett’s final sack may have been his most impactful and showed why the Rams traded for him. The Commanders faced 3rd-and-5 from the Rams’ 38-yard line after Garrett jumped offside. He immediately made up for it.
On the very next play, Daniels dropped back and Garrett cleanly beat the center to burst through the middle of the offensive line. Garrett wrapped up Daniels and sacked him to set up a 4th-and-17. When Emmanuel Forbes broke up the pass from Daniels to force a turnover on downs, the game was basically over in large part due to Garrett’s sack that resulted in a 12-yard loss.
Back in September, Garrett called that the worst version of himself. If Sunday was just a glimpse of what he can provide, it’s hard not to be excited for what’s to come. On Sunday, Garrett showed exactly why the Rams made the investment they did. It was only one game, but if this is the version that the Rams are getting for the second half of the season, the outlook for this team changes significantly.
It should be considered malpractice if the Rams don’t trade for a wide receiver this week . Puka Nacua has 41 targets in the last three weeks. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington have combined for 16 targets in that same span. Nacua had 19 targets against the Commanders alone and finished with 150 receiving yards. The next closest Rams wide receiver had 20. It’s just not sustainable.
Without trying to jinx anything, the Rams’ special teams unit played well yesterday. Josh Karty had three kickoffs bounce through the end zone to set up the Commanders at the 20-yard line. It seems crazy to keep two kickers, but it has worked. Ethan Evans averaged 52.8 yards per punt and had two land inside the 20. Jordan Whittington had a nice return as well. The bar is very low, but that was a promising performance.
The Rams were without their two starting cornerbacks on Sunday, yet they held Jayden Daniels to -0.19 EPA per pass, which ranked 19th for the week.. Emmanuel Forbes finished with two crucial pass breakups and had a tackle for loss. Josh Wallace remained solid as well. Defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake deserves a lot of credit for how well he’s coached up the cornerback depth.
How do you not give the game ball to Myles Garrett in this one ? Garrett had three sacks and a forced fumble. He was dominant in his return to the field in limited snaps. The Rams and Garrett had been waiting for that type of game, and with a lot of patience, they finally got it.
While the Rams may have been an abysmal 3-for-14 on third down, they were 3-for-3 on fourth down. The Rams converted a 4th-and-1 on their opening drive to set up a shorter field goal. They went for it again on 4th-and-3 during their final drive of the first half, which eventually resulted in another field goal. Those are six points the Rams added by going for it, and those points proved to matter in what was a seven-point win.
Since losing to the Cardinals, the Rams have gone on to win three straight. They’ll play the Cardinals again on Sunday and hope to take a four-game winning streak into the bye. Sunday could prove to be difficult if the Rams are without Puka Nacua after he got injured late against the Commanders. The Rams are still searching for their first division win of the year, and the Cardinals will be a good opportunity to get that.

title: Rams Winners & Losers: Myles Garrett Dominates in Return as Rams Win Third Straight
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Washington Commanders 20-13 in Week 9 to win their third straight game and improve to 5-4 on the season. Sunday also marked Myles Garrett’s return to the field after spending the last two months on injured reserve. Garrett was one of the biggest winners of the day, recording three sacks and a forced fumble. Let’s get into this week’s winners and losers.
For the last two months, the Rams have been awaiting Myles Garrett’s return . Garrett showed up in a big way on Sunday. He had three sacks, the first of which forced a fumble and the last one helped put a stop to a late surge by the Commanders. Garrett opened up opportunities for Aaron Donald and others while making a significant impact despite a limited snap count. If Sunday was only Garrett scratching the surface, the Rams can be very excited for what’s to come.
Back in 2023, the Commanders took Forbes in the first round of the draft. Forbes was cut in the middle of the 2024 season and has been with the Rams ever since. While he’s been a rotational player this year and still hasn’t lived up to his first-round draft status, Forbes filled in for Jaylen Watson on Sunday and had a bit of a revenge game. Forbes played physical and had two crucial pass breakups in the second half, including one on 4th-and-17.
Every week, it seems we’re talking about the Rams’ lack of wide receiver depth , and this week is no different. The Rams did get Atwell more involved as he had a season-high five targets. However, he had a crucial drop on a 3rd-and-2 in which he was wide open over the middle and Matthew Stafford hit him in the hands. A big narrative over the last month is how the Rams need to get Atwell involved. That might be true, but Atwell needs to take advantage of his chances when he gets them.
One of the biggest winners of Myles Garrett being back in the lineup against the Commanders was Aaron Donald. A big reason why Donald came out of retirement was to play alongside Garrett. While he didn’t end up with a sack on Sunday, he was credited with nine impact plays via Sumer Sports. Garrett opened up 1-on-1 opportunities for Donald and it seems like only a matter of time before he gets his first sack.
Since falling to 2-4, the Rams have won three straight. According to The Athletic, the Rams have a 40 percent chance to make the playoffs. A win against another NFC team will help with tiebreakers. The Rams still need to focus on getting their first division win of the season and should have a good chance to do that this week against the Arizona Cardinals.
It’s clear that the Rams need Terrance Ferguson back in the lineup. Tyler Higbee simply can’t be consistently relied on in the passing game. He had some moments, but couldn’t come down with a perfectly placed ball from Stafford in the second half. Later in the game, he completely stopped on a route, leading to an incompletion. Higbee has his role in the offense, but it’s unrealistic to ask him to be the second receiving option.
Like Emmanuel Forbes, Kam Curl had an opportunity for revenge against his former team on Sunday. While Curl showed up as questionable on the injury report going into the game, there was no question he was going to do his best to play this one. Curl led the Rams’ defense with eight tackles and played a big role in the secondary with McDuffie and Watson out. He’s been one of the most important players on the Rams’ defense over the last two seasons and showed why against his former team.
Sunday’s game against the Commanders might be the first time all season that we haven’t had to talk negatively about the Rams’ special teams. Kyren Williams didn’t offer much as a returner, but the special teams unit played well. Joshua Karty had multiple dirty kickoffs go through the end zone, resulting in the Commanders starting at their own 20. Brandon McManus made both of his field goals and extra points. Ethan Evans averaged 52.8 yards per punt and had two punts land inside the 20. Dare I say, the Rams’ special teams unit played well?

title: Myles Garrett Was Worth the Wait as Rams Beat Commanders For Third Straight Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams overcame another slow start on Sunday against the Washington Commanders, winning 20-13. For two months, the Rams w aited for Myles Garrett to make his return , and Sunday showed that the wait was worth it. Garrett made his presence felt, finishing with three sacks and a forced fumble as the offense went through Puka Nacua in the win.
After trading for Garrett this offseason, the Rams had been without the 2025 sack leader and NFL Defensive Player of the Year since Week 1. Garrett had been on injured reserve for much of the last two months with a knee injury, but finally returned on Sunday.
It was Garrett’s forced fumble at the end of the first half that gave the offense momentum going into halftime and then his third sack of the day late in the fourth quarter that propelled the Rams to victory.
Without Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson at cornerback, the Rams relied on their cornerback depth. Facing his former team, Emmanuel Forbes had a pair of pass breakups in the second half.
Still, it took the Rams’ defense some time to find its rhythm. The Commanders scored on their first two drives as Jayden Daniels hit former Rams wide receiver Van Jefferson in the end zone to put the Commanders up 10-3.
For a second straight week, the offense had a slow start. Outside of Puka Nacua, they couldn’t find answers in the passing game. However, even Nacua took time to get going. With the Rams trailing, Nacua fumbled and the Commanders recovered at midfield.
That’s when Garrett and the defense took over. On the first play of the next drive, Daniels scrambled to his right and Garrett came in behind him and knocked the ball loose. Omar Speights recovered, giving the offense another chance to get points before the half. While the offense didn’t get in the end zone, Brandon McManus’ second field goal of the day made it 10-6.
Following the Commanders' opening touchdown, the Rams' defense went six straight drives without allowing a first down. That gave the offense the time it needed to get going. On the opening drive of the second half, Stafford hit Nacua on back-to-back plays and then it was Blake Corum who finished off the drive in the end zone to give the Rams their first lead of the day.
After Stafford threw an interception that led to the Commanders tying the game at 13, the Rams went right back to Nacua on the next drive. Stafford hit Nacua on 3rd-and-11 to convert one of their only third downs of the afternoon. Nacua’s 14th catch of the day made it 20-13 for the Rams as Stafford threw a perfect ball to the corner of the end zone.
Sunday’s game once again confirmed that the Rams have a need at wide receiver . Nacua finished with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. Outside of Nacua, the Rams got little production from their other receivers. Tutu Atwell had a drop, while he and Konata Mumpfield combined for four catches for 36 yards.
The defense remained stout for the Rams, closing out the game in the fourth quarter. Garrett sacked Daniels as the Commanders looked to answer the Rams. After Garrett jumped offside on 3rd-and-10, he sacked Daniels on the next play to make it 4th-and-17. Forbes then knocked away a pass intended for Jefferson to force a turnover on downs.
With the game on the line, the Commanders made it interesting, progressing to the Rams’ 31-yard line. On the final play, Byron Young recovered a loose ball as the Commanders attempted a series of laterals in a last-ditch effort to tie the game.
It was another imperfect win for the Rams. However, it’s their third straight as they improve to above .500 for the first time this season. The Rams leaned on their stars to win the game, and both Nacua and Garrett stepped up when needed.
This is a Rams team that has yet to truly reach its ceiling, but with Garrett back, it appears to be getting closer.. With a win against the Arizona Cardinals next week, the Rams would be 6-4 at their bye week and in a good spot heading into the second half of the season.

title: Rams Injury Report: Trent McDuffie's Status Adds to Secondary Concerns Despite Key Returns
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be without their two starting cornerbacks on Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Earlier this week, the Rams announced that Jaylen Watson’s season was over with a shoulder injury . After missing all week of practice with a back injury, the Rams could also be without Trent McDuffie as he is officially listed as questionable.
"He's really done a great job in practice," said McVay on Friday about Garrett. "He has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan. It's been great having him out there."
If the Rams are without McDuffie and Watson, they will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes as their top two cornerbacks. While Wallace has filled in for McDuffie and Watson throughout the season, Forbes has remained in a rotational role. Without both McDuffie and Watson, Forbes would be thrown into a full-time role for the first time this season against his former team.
While the big news for the Rams on Friday was the team announcing that Myles Garrett would make his return against the Commanders, he won’t be the only player returning from injury.
The Rams were initially set to get tight end Terrance Ferguson back, he injured his hamstring during Friday's practice. Ferguson had been out since Week 3 with a medial ankle spring and would have been a welcomed addition back to the offense. Ferguson was expected back as the Rams activated his practice window this week. However, the team sent out an updated injury report on Friday with Ferguson's status updated to out on Sunday against the Commanders
With Ferguson out, the Rams could be shorthanded at tight end for a second straight week. Colby Parkinson was listed as questionable, but was a limited participant on Friday. If the Rams are without both, they would likely need to lean on rookie Max Klare.
The Rams are also likely to be without long snapper Joe Cardona as he manages an ankle injury, leaving Jake McQuaide in that spot. Wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and safety Kam Curl (foot) were all listed as questionable as well. Curl was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, but his status is still up in the air. However, Curl will have motivation to play against his former team if he is able.
While Steve Avila and Matthew Stafford were listed on the injury report earlier this week, neither was given an injury designation on Friday. Stafford was a full participant all week with an elbow injury while Avila was a full participant the last two days as he manages a hamstring. Both should be good to go.
On the Commanders’ side, they will be without wide receivers Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown. Defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton was listed as questionable.
If the Rams are without Watson and McDuffie on Sunday, it will be a significant blow to the secondary, especially if Curl is also unable to play. The return of Garrett should help take some pressure off the defensive backs, but the Rams will be relying heavily on their depth to get through Sunday against the Commanders.

title: Myles Garrett Set to Make Return vs. Commanders, But What Should Rams Expect?
full_text:
Ever since he was placed on injured reserve after Week 1, the Los Angeles Rams have been awaiting the return of edge rusher Myles Garrett. What was initially given a six-week timeline turned into seven. When the Rams a ctivated Garrett’s practice window this week , there was some positive momentum that he could be ready for Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders. On Friday, head coach Sean McVay confirmed that Garrett will play.
Rams DE Myles Garrett is expected to play vs. Commanders, Sean McVay says
The Rams traded for Garrett in what was their biggest acquisition of the offseason . However, shortly into training camp, Garrett began missing practices with what was described as knee soreness and then was placed on injured reserve that week as he underwent arthroscopic surgery.
"There were just things I was dealing with mechanically that only continued to worsen as I played more throughout that game," said Garrett on Friday. "It was rough and I was trying to avoid it, but you learn and you grow. Now it's just a lesson that I had to learn from and I took the necessary steps to come back.”
With Jaylen Watson heading on injured reserve earlier this week, the Rams won’t get a look at what their defense could have been with Garrett, Watson, Trent McDuffie, and Aaron Donald. However, the Rams will get a look at what their defense can do with Donald and Garrett on the field together for the first time.
Trading for Garrett played a large role in Donald coming out of retirement. The Rams’ season certainly hasn’t gone as Donald may have expected, but nine weeks into the season, he’ll finally get to play alongside one of the biggest reasons he came back.
“It's good to have the pieces back to the puzzle. It was good to see him out there yesterday and today. He’s looking good, looking fast,” said Donald on Thursday. “Getting to work with him in full pads and playing off each other. It looked pretty good today, so I'm excited about having him here, having him back, and seeing what we do Sunday.”
As Garrett gets set to make his return , the question now becomes how much he’ll play on Sunday against the Commanders. The Rams have played it safe with Garrett since the summer and paid the consequences for not doing that in Week 1. While the Rams opened Garrett’s practice window and will activate him for Sunday’s game, it remains unlikely that he’ll play 100 percent of the defensive snaps.
The Rams have a strong rotation with Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey, who have both filled in nicely while Garrett has been out. Additionally, Garrett coming back remains a step-by-step process. The Rams activated his practice window, slowly got him back into rhythm by having him take half the practice reps, and will now see how he reacts to a game.
“As far as what that snap count looks like if he is able to play, it's really truly like, 'Let's just see how today goes, and then let's see how tomorrow goes and [then] the following day,’” McVay said.
Back in Week 2 against the New York Giants when Donald played his first game of the season after slowly ramping up, he played 56.9 percent of the defensive snaps. In Week 1, Garrett played 61.5 percent of the defensive snaps while not being 100 percent.
It seems likely for Garrett's snap count to end up somewhere in that same range. He may play half or slightly more than half of the defensive snaps against the Commanders. The Rams will slowly ramp him up over the next few weeks, depending on how his body reacts. Overall, the goal will be to get Garrett to 100 percent for the second half of the season after the bye week.

title: Rams’ Most Likely Trade Deadline Move at Wide Receiver Is Far From Guaranteed
full_text:
Things remain quiet on the trade deadline front for the Los Angeles Rams. While they may inquire about players to see if there is a deal worth making, a trade remains unlikely right now given how competitive the wide receiver and defensive line markets have been.
With that said, if the Rams were to make a move, wide receiver seems to be the most likely position they would target. While the need for better wide receiver depth has been emphasized with Davante Adams being out, it's still something the Rams could use when he returns. The Rams simply don’t have a wide receiver they can trust behind Adams and Puka Nacua.
Konata Mumpfield has a 38.1 percent targeted success rate and has averaged -0.32 EPA per target. Despite running a route at the 25th-highest rate in the NFL, his 0.13 targets per route run ranks 86th out of 103 qualifying wide receivers.
Over the past few weeks, the Rams have been adamant that they trust their wide receiver depth. “I do think there are some guys on the roster that are capable of being able to step up if their number is called,” said McVay before referring to Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell.
“We definitely feel good about those guys being able to catch the football, but with a 60, 70-play game, there's going to be a lot that we require them to do,” added offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase on Thursday. “We feel like those guys can step up and do all those things.”
The Rams have consistently said that they trust their wide receiver depth, but their actions suggest otherwise. Mumpfield and Atwell have combined for just three receptions over the last two weeks without Adams. Comparatively, Nacua has 19.
Wide receiver is the most pressing need on the roster, and it’s an obvious one. Things will certainly improve to an extent when Adams gets back and Terrance Ferguson returns to action. However, at some point, the Rams will have to be able to throw the ball with three wide receivers on the field.
Last season, with the game on the line in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams had to rely on Mumpfield and Ferguson, who were both rookies. The Rams need a player they can trust in crucial situations to get open outside of Nacua.
The Rams don’t necessarily have the draft capital to compete with other teams in the wide receiver market. Josh Downs remains a top option for the Rams, but he also has other suitors such as the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers. According to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, Downs would probably cost a fourth-round pick.
Brian Thomas Jr. has been mentioned as a potential Rams target, but Breer reported that the Jaguars have been less inclined to trade him. Said Breer, “Thomas brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.”
That leaves the Rams looking at secondary options, and at that point, is it worth making a move simply for the sake of it?
Treylon Burks and Calvin Ridley could be among the options. However, Burks has never had more than 450 yards in a season and hasn’t proven to be reliable. Breer reported that Ridley may only cost a sixth-round pick. While Ridley would only cost around $2.8 million this season, his cap hit jumps to $29 million next season, with $7.5 million in dead money if he's cut.
Which receivers are winning most of their routes? Data: @FantasyPtsData , min. 120 routes (% of routes with a positive separation score) pic.twitter.com/IMy3n6ZNOP
For as much as the Rams need a wide receiver, they may be waiting for an opportunity during the season if a veteran player is cut, similar to Odell Beckham Jr. in 2021. Brandon Aiyuk could be among those options .
The Rams certainly have a need at wide receiver. It’s been a need since the spring and the Rams have ignored it at every turn. Given their lack of draft capital and a hot wide receiver market, it seems unlikely the Rams will make a move at this point.
This is a team in a championship window, and for as much as the coaching staff has said they trust their wide receiver depth, that very clearly has not been the case. If the Rams make a trade, the most likely move at the trade deadline would be for a wide receiver.

title: Grading Each Raiders' Position Group Following Week 9 Against 49ers
full_text:
Week 9 was another Sunday when the Las Vegas Raiders started slowly and hinged their hopes on mounting a second-half comeback. The only problem is that Las Vegas turned the ball over three times in the second half. One of those turnovers was an interception returned for a touchdown.
As expected, Las Vegas was set to face a rested San Francisco 49ers team that was coming off its bye week. Things got out of hand early for the Raiders, much like they did against the New England Patriots earlier this season. The Raiders' struggles started early and often on Sunday.
Kirk Cousins continues to rank near the top of the league in several statistical categories.
Las Vegas has a solid player in Connor Heyward, but fullbacks are only impactful on offenses that are productive.
The Raiders only rushed the ball for 24 yards. Brock Bowers had two of those yards. However, Ashton Jeanty averaged over four yards per carry. Las Vegas likely would have been able to run the ball more had they not had an interception returned for a touchdown in the third quarter.
Teams cannot run the ball when they are down by nearly three touchdowns early in the second half. Until Las Vegas starts games faster and fixes its issues along the offensive line, its ground game will continue to struggle, as it did in each of the past three seasons.
Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer kept the Raiders' offense afloat for another week. Together, they accounted for 148 of the team's 216 receiving yards. However, both players also fumbled the ball on Sunday, which essentially ended Las Vegas' chances of mounting another comeback.
Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, and Jalen Nailor did not have much of an impact on Sunday's game, as the Raiders again leaned heavily on their tight ends.
The Raiders need help at offensive guard. Any progress they've made by starting Trey Zuhn appears marginal, at best. After holding an offensive guard competition during the offseason, the position will be the offense's downfall for the remainder of the year.
After entering Week 9 having allowed among the fewest sacks in the league, the unit did not allow any sacks on Sunday.
The Raiders once again struggled to stop the run in the first half, allowing the 49ers to rush for 125 yards. However, the unit also held the 49ers to only 65 rushing yards in the second half.  They did so even though the 49ers ran the ball nearly 20 times in the second half.
Las Vegas needs help along its interior defensive line, just like it needs help along the interior of its offensive line. Games, especially against the league's best, are won and lost in the trenches. Deep in the trenches, which is exactly where the Raiders need the most help.
The Raiders will keep falling short against the league's best until they fix the interior of both of their lines. This offseason, Las Vegas must make a major addition to the interior of its defensive line.
The Raiders' linebackers will continue to struggle if the defensive line cannot get off blocks and the defensive backfield cannot contain receivers.
Sunday was another rough outing for the group. However, this is what the development of young players at critical positions looks like, especially against the league's elite. The best thing the Raiders can do now is keep developing the young group.
The best development is what they are getting on Sundays. The unit's struggles are not unique to them. Several former young cornerbacks the Raiders have tried struggled early in their careers but may have succeeded under a better coaching staff and roster.
Cornerback is one of the most challenging positions on the field.
Rookie safety Treydan Stukes' second-half interception set the Raiders' offense up to score. Stukes continues to improve week to week, while also showing areas that need improvement. Overall, Stukes is a valuable part of the defense.
Dylan Laube continues to make an impact for the Raiders weekly. After registering the league's first kickoff return for a touchdown last week, Laube added another solid return in Week 9.
Kicker Matt Gay made a 50-yard field goal, giving the Raiders a puncher's chance in the second quarter.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: What We Learned About Raiders in Week 9 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' return to the win column was brief, as they fell to the San Francisco 49ers 38-17 on Sunday.
With that in mind, here are several things we learned about the Raiders in their blowout loss in Week 9.
Kirk Cousins has been a revelation this season after looking like his career was over after two dreadful seasons in Atlanta. However, the 38-year-old quarterback struggled mightily on Sunday, completing 22-of-32 passes for 216 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions.
It's not that Cousins was inept, but this is Las Vegas' fourth loss in five games, and Cousins' three turnovers were costly. He threw a pick-six on the first play of the second half, and one of his other two interceptions occurred in the red zone.
With the trade deadline on Tuesday, the Raiders could turn to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. On the other hand, the Raiders face the Seattle Seahawks next week, not the best matchup for a rookie quarterback to walk into.
Entering Week 9, Las Vegas desperately needed to revive its rushing attack, which has been dormant for most of the season. It didn't show any signs of life, as Jeanty led the backfield with six carries for 25 yards. Meanwhile, Mike Washington Jr. took six carries for -3 yards.
If the Raiders want to contend for a playoff spot, their rushing attack has to be better moving forward. The interior offensive line has to develop lanes for Jeanty and Washington Jr. The two running backs have been hit behind the line of scrimmage too often.
This is why Las Vegas moving multiple veterans for future draft capital could be the best route for this team. The Raiders certainly have shown plenty of promise throughout the season, even on Sunday. However, all five of Las Vegas' losses are against teams above .500. That is a telltale sign that this team is a season away from being legitimate playoff contenders.
The Raiders' future is incredibly bright, with Klint Kubiak as head coach, Mendoza as the future franchise quarterback, and several foundational pieces on both sides of the ball.
It's not all doom and gloom for the Raiders, but Sunday was another reality check for this ownership and front office that the team still has plenty of room for growth. The playoffs are still within reach for the Raiders, as they are half a game out of the wild card. If they want to improve their chances of competing for a playoff spot, trading for a wide receiver and/or offensive lineman is necessary.

title: 3 Overreactions to Raiders Bay Area Loss vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders fell to the San Francisco 49ers in their return to the Bay Area, 38-17, in a game that wasn't particularly close to begin with.
The 49ers dominated this game from the start, and it was clear early on that the Raiders were overmatched, overpowered, and overwhelmed— you name it. It was not a pretty sight, and it won't get any better in the coming weeks against more quality opponents, but a 4-5 record at this juncture, compared to preseason expectations, is something to celebrate from an optimistic point of view.
After watching this game, I have some immediate overreactions to share. There may be some emotion in these takes, but there is some substance to the changes that could be on the way.
Kirk Cousins had arguably his worst performance of the season against the 49ers, throwing three interceptions in a game that showed his physical decline as an aging veteran. As the season progresses and losses against quality teams mount, it's time that we have serious discussions about playing Fernando Mendoza, regardless of how Cousins plays.
We're getting to the point where we know who the Raiders are. They aren't going to match up well with teams that have great rosters and coaching across the board, and they don't have the talent to go wire-to-wire with teams like Los Angeles, San Francisco, and New England.
Mendoza needs the experience, and he needs to see the field sooner rather than later. I'm eager to see No. 15 on the field with this offense and one of the league's best weapons, Brock Bowers. It could come this week against Seattle or after the bye week, but it must happen soon.
It's as simple as that. The Raiders will beat the bad teams, maybe upset a good one at some point, and then lose to almost all of the good teams. You could argue the Raiders are on their way to a 7-10 record, and that would be considered a big success for Year 1 of this rebuild.
After starting 3-0, it's frustrating to see these kinds of losses; I've experienced them plenty in the Carolinas over the last eight years, and this is no exception. Las Vegas has a bright future with Mendoza, Bowers, a young secondary, and quality linebackers. They want to be fairly disciplined in their approach to rebuilding this franchise.
The losses stink, but this is the way, no matter how you frame it. The Raiders are who they are, and no one is coming to save them.
Once a promising prospect from Oregon, the former second-round pick is in his third season and is riding the bench after losing his starting job to Caleb Rogers, then Trey Zuhn III. With the NFL trade deadline set for Tuesday at 4 pm Eastern (1 pm Pacific), I think we may have seen Powers-Johnson play his final down for the Raiders.
Powers-Johnson will be coveted by teams searching for depth, and he is one of the few offensive linemen on a rookie deal with one year left and a ceiling that has yet to be scratched in some instances. It wasn't working here, and he wasn't a John Spytek selection. It's better to get some Day 3 value out of Powers-Johnson and allow him to hit the reset button elsewhere.

title: Winners & Losers: Self-Inflicted Wounds Cost Raiders vs. 49ers
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, CA.—The Las Vegas Raiders fell to 4-5 on the season yesterday in a 38-17 drubbing by the San Francisco 40ers (7-1) at Levi's Stadium.
Once again, the story wasn't that the rebuilding Raiders lost; it was that an overmatched Raiders team competed and ultimately lost because of poor play by veterans.
The day after every game, I give you my complete list of winners and losers, not my report card that breaks down every facet of the game, but one from a bird’s-eye view before reviewing all of the film.
I asked Klint Kubiak why his team couldn't stop the run. I have told you for months that the Raiders are thin on the defensive line and young at defensive back, but is it schematic or personnel? He wanted none of that.
“We all share the blame. There's no finger-pointing, it's thumb-pointing. So, we'll figure it out together.”
Well, in five of the last six weeks, the Raiders have given up 150-plus yards in rushing, so how does he fix it? “It's got to take something different.”
It is the sixth week in a row that the Silver and Black defense has given up 30-plus points, so when do they have to discuss doing something different?
“We'll look at the film and we'll make our decisions when we have cooler heads.”
Superstar DE Maxx Crosby always performs at a high level, and this season is no different. That said, he was asked point-blank whether the issues are schematic or personnel, and while his answer may sound political to the untrained ear, it wasn’t. It was truthful.
“There are multiple things. There are a lot of things up front. You have to be tied together at the back end and linebackers do as well. It's communication, it's leveraging the formation, several things that tie into stopping the run. It's not just one player. It has to be all 11, all hands on deck. It's something we're going to have to continue improving on, and I think we will.”
The Raiders D made critical adjustments at halftime yesterday, but Crosby talked about why his side of the ball struggles to start big contests.
Brock Purdy launches it deep to Jordan Watkins to extend the 49ers lead 🚀 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DgGxhzVHmb
“Going into every game, it's different. You have to give credit to them. They had some answers to the things we're doing. And we got to make more plays defensively. We have to take the ball away. We can’t wait until late in the game to start taking the ball away. There are a lot of things that go into it, but you have to give them their credit. The Niners play really well.”
He wasn’t done: “They're a really good team. They've been in great adversity often, and have been in multiple Super Bowls, and they know what it looks like. So, you can't give them layups and things like that, or it's going to be really difficult. We believe in each other, I know this locker room does. Some of the turnovers, I know guys had zero intention of having that happen, but it’s how you respond. I'll go to war with these guys every single day of the week. That's what we're going to keep doing.”
CB Hezekiah Masses (3) and S Treydan Stukes (2) are the only rookie teammates with multiple interceptions in the #NFL this season. They're the the first pair of #Raiders rookies with multiple interceptions in a season since 1975: Charlie Phillips (6), Neal Colzie (4). https://t.co/3TBwjXMPD9
CB Hezekiah Masses and S Treydan Stukes are the only rookie defensive back combo in the NFL this year with multiple interceptions, and I asked Kubiak about Stukes’ tremendous play on Sunday.
“Yeah, absolutely. He's been a bright spot throughout the season. Very instinctive playmaker, hard worker. Proud that we have him on our roster.”
Don’t tell Stukes he was a bright spot; he passed the credit on and took the blame. The young man is a burgeoning star, and this was just another example.
Treydan Stukes in the right place at the right time 👏 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ybBp5MdnTi
“It was good communication all around. I got some pre-snap communication with the other players and that's what helped me be able to be in front of the play and have a chance on that one. We have to find a way to do that more often, get our offense more chances so we can win these games.”
Credit the Raiders; in the midst of this aforementioned rebuild, they are beating the teams they should, and that is a sign of how things have changed. In their five losses, three have been blowouts, albeit against superior teams. Kubiak wasn’t shy about what it takes to get over the top and win one of these.
“You got to start the game a lot faster. You got to go toe-to-toe in the first half so that the second half isn't a throwing fest.”
The NFL trade deadline is scheduled for Tuesday at 1 PM PT, and the Raiders are under the proverbial microscope. They need to make some tough decisions. Kubiak was asked about them.
“We're always talking about that with Spy [Las Vegas Raiders GM John Spytek] and looking at everything.”
He was asked whether yesterday's loss could affect what he and GM John Spytek do on Tuesday. “Every day the calculus changes. You get new information about your team, and that goes into the decision-making moving forward.”
QB Kirk Cousins is having an amazing year despite a bad day on Sunday, and his name keeps coming up as a trade target. Especially with the 2026 NFL Draft No. 1 overall pick, and the young man NFL executives ranked the best QB prospect of the last four years, Fernando Mendoza, waiting in the wings.
Cousins was asked about it: “It feels a little bit out of my hands. So, I'll just let decision makers make decisions and react accordingly, but love it here. Love the guys here and feel good about what we have here.”
The reality is that sitting at 4-5 is an overachievement given how the season predictions were aligned, but no one sane thought this was a Super Bowl team. They are still in the hunt, but not for a Super Bowl, and Kubiak addressed his roster.
“At this time of year, we're focused on winning games. I really like our team. I don't like losing games like this. We’ve got to have a lot more resilience when you're playing a really good team like we played today. When you start that slow, you don't put yourself in a good position, but I'm proud to coach the guys that we're coaching.”
One thing about this season is that these guys, from coaches to players, are on the same page. Crosby said it will stay that way; there won’t be any issues, and these guys are in this together.
“We've got a bunch of hard workers on this team. We've got gritty football players and veterans. We love to play football. We love to come to work and play football. So, we're just going to get back to work and keep practicing. I'm obviously going to focus on the ball security details. We've got a bunch of people on this team who love football and love to win, so that's not going to be a problem for this team.”
That's 3️⃣ interceptions for the 49ers defense! LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dd1BGmWmu7
As mentioned, the Raiders lost because of the veterans' self-inflicted wounds. Crosby wasn’t looking for an excuse for how it made him feel.
“I think anytime you lose a game like that, regardless of turnovers or not, there are things to clean up schematically and with ball security. So, I'm sure we've got to clean up a lot of things.”
Cousins addressed those self-inflicted wounds head-on: “I think it's just a little more painful, certainly when you come away and you feel like maybe you could have been in that game had you played to the standard you expect of yourself or of your group, and I think that's the hard part.”
TE Michael Mayer has really matured as a player and a leader, and he was guilty of some of those self-inflicted wounds, and the young man didn’t dodge it, or even try.
