title: Is Steelers Success Hurting Mike Tomlin’s Legacy?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have settled in under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy after some rough moments during the first few weeks of the season and have rode a four-game win streak into their Week 9 bye, leading to a 6-2 record and sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Upon hiring McCarthy after Mike Tomlin stepped down following a 19-year stint at the helm with the Steelers, the general consensus was that the organization downgraded.
Pittsburgh looks like a rejuvenated football team, however, and its ceiling in 2026 appears to be higher than it has been in at least half a decade.
While Tomlin is no stranger to regular season success in the slightest, as evidenced by never turning in a losing campaign with the Steelers , the McCarthy era is off to a better start than anticipated.
While McCarthy and his staff still have to prove their momentum can translate to the postseason, has Pittsburgh's hot start to the year already diminished the legacy Tomlin left behind?
Lauded as one of the NFL's top defensive minds, Tomlin's units fell short of expectations on that side of the ball in recent years despite having loads of talent.
For example, in 2025, the Steelers' defense allowed the seventh-most yards (356.9) and 16th-most points (22.8) per game. Under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham this season, however, the group has given up the sixth-fewest yards (305.6) and third-fewest points (18.0).
If the year were to end today, that would mark the least amount of yards allowed per game for a Pittsburgh defense since 2019 and the fewest points given up per game since 2011.
Considering the core of the defense largely remains the same in 2026 as it was in 2025, outside of cornerback, where the Steelers have arguably gotten worse due to their trade of Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys, that's quite an indictment of Tomlin and how his philosophy resonated amongst the group as compared to where it now stands with Graham calling the shots.
It was pretty clear, even for multiple years, that a parting of ways between Tomlin and the Steelers would be beneficial for both sides.
Sometimes a change and a fresh perspective, or voice, is necessary to help spark a team and an organization. That was certainly the case for Pittsburgh, who lost seven-straight playoff games under Tomlin and felt like it was stuck in the mind to a certain extent.
McCarthy has come in and introduced a slew of changes alongside his staff that appear to be paying off early in his tenure. What the rest of the season and the long-term future for the regime holds remains to be seen, but the hire feels like a success thus far.
At the same time, even if Tomlin stepping down and bringing in McCarthy has worked out for the Steelers up to this point, that should have zero bearing on how the former's legacy with the franchise is viewed.
He's still a future Hall of Famer who brought a Super Bowl title back to Pittsburgh in 2008 and had the team in playoff contention on an annual basis for nearly two decades.
Tomlin consistently elevated both the floor and ceiling of the Steelers, and it sure feels like he's generally underappreciated for his body of work with the black and gold.
No matter what McCarthy accomplishes in Pittsburgh, whether it be winning the team a Lombardi Trophy and/or developing its next franchise quarterback, it should not taint Tomlin's legacy in the slightest or take away from his long list of accomplishments.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Steelers' Second Half
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — After an earned bye week, the Pittsburgh Steelers begin the second half of their season with an AFC North showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Entering with a 6-2 record, the Steelers can capture a fifth consecutive victory and a commanding lead in the division if they take down the Bengals. That contest will be a measuring stick for the Steelers as they kick off the back half of the schedule, as the team eyes a deep run in the postseason.
To get there, the Steelers have to keep improving. Hopefully, a trade or two comes through before this year’s NFL Trade Deadline that upgrades the roster accordingly, but even if that doesn’t happen, this team still has many problems to solve.
They also need a few of these bold predictions to become reality as they progress through the remaining portion of their regular season schedule.
After signing a deserved contract extension that made him one of the highest-paid kickers in the NFL, the 2026 campaign has been forgettable for Chris Boswell. He’s made 18 field goals on 23 attempts, but what stands out is his struggles beyond 40 yards. He’s been perfect from all attempts up to 39 yards, but he’s converted on just eight of 13 attempts of 40 yards or greater. His 78.5% success rate is woefully below his career average of 87.1%.
That’s what makes this bold prediction just that. Boswell’s longest field goal on the season is a 58-yard bomb and his career-long is a 60-yard field goal he booted last season.
This year, he breaks that and then some. The longest field goal kicked in NFL history came last season off the foot of Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little. He put a 69-yard attempt through the uprights, and Boswell will beat that feat by season’s end. It will be quite the redemptive act that makes up for a less-than-stellar year from the best kicker in Steelers history.
Tight end Pat Freiermuth’s career-high for touchdown catches is seven, a feat he’s accomplished twice. So far in 2026, ‘Muth has hauled in four touchdown receptions in eight games to lead all Steelers receivers.
With nine games to play, expect Freiermuth to continue to be a fixture in this offense . Tight ends are a major piece of their game plan, with he and Darnell Washington combining for seven of Aaron Rodgers’s 13 touchdown passes.
Rodgers will continue to lean on his top tight end, and Freiermuth will topple his previous career-best mark. Not only that, Freiermuth will hit double digits for the first time in his NFL career.
Pittsburgh football is synonymous with smashmouth defense. Once again, the 2026 version is living up to that reputation and defying expectations.
The defense is flawed, but what remains elite is their front seven and ability to pass rush. The Steelers lead the NFL with 26.0 sacks entering Week 9 contests, highlighted by T.J. Watt’s 7.5 sacks.
That puts them right on pace to set a new franchise record for sacks in a season. The current team record is 56.0 sacks as a team, accomplished in both 2020 and 2017. The 2021, 2001 and 1994 teams each posted 55.0 sacks, according to data from StatMuse .
If this year’s squad keeps this pace up, they will surpass 50.0 sacks with ease by the end of the year. But this group is different. Watt is playing at an MVP level. Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig are both poised for huge second-half production, and the rest of the defense continues to chip in as they get after the quarterback.
It’s a dangerous pass rush in Pittsburgh, and I believe it will be franchise-record-setting by the end of this season.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Game-By-Game Predictions After Bye Week
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers had about as good of a first half as they could've hoped for.
At 6-2 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North during their Week 9 bye while riding a four-game win streak, the Steelers feel like they could put themselves in position for a deep playoff run depending on how they approach the trade deadline and finish out the season.
With that, here are our week-by-week predictions for the remainder of the 2026 campaign .
The Steelers got the better of the Bengals in their prior matchup this season, winning by a score of 27-24 in a tightly-contested bout that was clinched after Derrick Harmon recorded a strip-sack of Joe Burrow that Sebastian Joseph-Day recovered.
Separated by half-a-game currently in the AFC North, Cincinnati feels like it poses the biggest threat to Pittsburgh's hold on first place.
The Bengals' defense has taken a few steps forward this season, with their offseason trade for Dexter Lawrence II doing a lot of the heavy lifting, though it's still a rather mediocre unit overall.
While Cincinnati has yet to get much of anything going on the ground this season, its trio of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins makes its passing offense incredibly tough to stop, even for an elite defense like the Steelers have.
Pittsburgh is 12-4 on the road vs. the Bengals since 2010, and if it wants to really put itself in the AFC North driver's seat for good, it has to win once again at Paycor Stadium. That's far easier said than done, however.
Prediction: Bengals win 24-21
The Steelers have not won on the road in Philadelphia since 1965. This Eagles team is contending with a ton of issues, though, and Pittsburgh really should have the clear edge.
Philadelphia named Joe Milton III as its starting quarterback for its Week 9 matchup with the New York Giants, sending Tanner McKee to the bench as a result.
With Jalen Hurts out for the remainder of the year due to blood clots in his lungs while the Eagles are dealing with a slew of other injuries and the possibility of selling to an extent at this year's trade deadline, the Steelers are simply the better team at this moment. The only way they should run into any issues is if Milton proves to be the real deal.
Prediction: Steelers win 27-16
The Broncos are currently 6-2 and on a four-game win streak, much like the Steelers in both respects.
Denver's offense is one of the worst in the league, though, as it is averaging the third-fewest yards per game with 273.0 amidst Bo Nix's struggles while also consistently falling short in the run game.
The Broncos' defense is still a good unit, but the unit is not nearly as stout as it was in 2025 when they ranked at or near the top of just about every major statistical category.
Denver is also 15-14 on the road since Sean Payton took over as head coach in 2023, while being 23-7 at home over that span.
Given that this game is at Acrisure Stadium and the fact that these two teams feel rather comparable, Pittsburgh should have the advantage.
Prediction: Steelers win 20-16
The last time the Steelers hosted the Texans for a primetime bout, they lost 30-6 during the Wild Card round of the playoffs last season in what was Mike Tomlin's final contest as the franchise's head coach.
C.J. Stroud and Houston's passing offense (253.4 yards per game, seventh-most in the NFL) have really turned things around this year, but its run game is essentially non-existent.
Despite having the same defensive core that helped them to a 12-5 record in 2025, the Texans have largely ranked in the middle of the pack at best on that side of the ball this season.
While it is 2-5, Houston still has a ton of talent and should pose a real threat to Pittsburgh. Regardless, there are the types of games the Steelers have to win if they want to be considered a top contender in the AFC.
Prediction: Steelers win 21-20
Right up there with the Buffalo Bills as the best teams in the AFC over the first half of the season or so, defeating Jacksonville on the road might be the toughest ask remaining on Pittsburgh's schedule.
The Jaguars are averaging the fifth-most points per game (28.0) while allowing the second-fewest points per game (15.9), making them arguably the most complete team in the league at 5-2.
The Steelers could very well run into Jacksonville during the postseason as well, and while it's not unbeatable, it does the upper hand in this matchup.
Prediction: Jaguars win 28-17
With Lamar Jackson potentially done for the season with a thumb injury while Tyler Huntley will be sidelined for the rest of 2026 due to a turf toe injury, the 4-4 Ravens are attempting to breathe new life into their campaign by acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals.
Brissett was solid at times over his 20 starts for Arizona, but without Jackson behind center, it doesn't feel like Baltimore will make much noise this season.
Pittsburgh is 5-1 against the Ravens at Acrisure Stadium since 2020, and that trend should continue.
Prediction: Steelers win 26-17
This feels like a potential trap game for the Steelers.
Not that the Panthers are completely uncompetitive, as they still have a relatively good shot to win the NFC South while currently being 3-4, but they're not really a high-profile opponent who feels like much of a threat at first glance.
Carolina's offense, led by Bryce Young, has proven to be potent at times though, as proven by averaging the ninth-most yards (363.7) and points (25.4) per game.
The Panthers' defense, on the other hand, has dealt with injuries to key players such as Nic Scourton, Jaycee Horn and Jaelan Phillips, among others, and the team fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero following their Week 8 loss to the Green Bay Packers due to the unit's shortcomings.
This is a contest Pittsburgh should win, but the Panthers could easily steal a victory here too.
Prediction: Panthers win 27-24
This will be the Titans' final game at the old Nissan Stadium, where they've played since 1999, before moving to the new Nissan Stadium next season.
Perhaps emotions will be high as a result, though it really shouldn't matter. While Cam Ward and Tennessee have shown some signs of improvement over the past few weeks, it is 1-7 for a reason.
If the Steelers don't win this game by a comfortable margin, that wouldn't bode well for their chances of embarking on a playoff run.
Prediction: Steelers win 27-13
It's at least feasible that Baltimore will still be alive in the race for a Wild Card spot during the final week of the regular season, though it's more likely that it will have nothing to play for in this one.
The stakes should be much higher for Pittsburgh from a seeding perspective, and perhaps the Bengals will remain in the running for the AFC North title alongside it by the time Week 8 rolls around as well.
Winning at M&T Bank Stadium is never easy, particularly in this case where the Steelers could be under a fair amount of pressure, but they should ultimately get the job done.
Prediction: Steelers win 24-20 and finish 12-5
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Trade Candidates to Watch in Week 9
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers aren't in action during Week 9, but a future member of their franchise might be.
With the 2027 NFL Trade Deadline just days away, the Steelers are trying their best to upgrade this team. Jumping out to a 6-2 record to begin the year, they've earned the right to go all-in for the remainder of 2026, and that includes adding talent on both sides of the ball.
Whether or not that happens remains to be seen, but the Steelers have their eyes on several players ahead of the deadline. These players stand out as the top trade targets in action during the Week 9 slate of contests.
The wide receiver most consistently tied to the Steelers during this Trade Deadline rumor cycle is Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher Josh Downs. The 25-year-old is in the final year of his rookie contract and desperately wants out of Indianapolis.
A strong performance in Week 9 will only help the Colts get more for the speedy receiver, however. They take on a fledgling Dallas Cowboys squad, and are reportedly seeking a third- or fourth-round draft pick in a potential trade.
But over the last five contests, Downs has been featured less and less. His single-game high during that stretch is 47 yards against the Steelers in their earlier matchup. If he posts another middling day in Week 9, it might help the Steelers land him for even less.
A former first-round pick of the Baltimore Ravens, Hollywood Brown is a lower-tier name who could wind up in Pittsburgh. An ankle injury kept him out of four games this season, and he's also been made inactive on game days, but he's managed four receptions for 47 yards in two games since returning.
Brown is far from the top player on the market, but he would give the Steelers a bit of depth without giving up too much. He's posted four seasons with at least 500 receiving yards across three different franchises in his career, and if healthy, he still has the athleticism and agility to help the Steelers.
The Steelers seem to be focused on acquiring a wide receiver, but the secondary could use reinforcements. Riq Woolen is an easy solution, coming with a championship pedigree, and he's owed just a few million dollars on the one-year deal he signed in the offseason.
For a sixth or seventh-round draft pick, the Steelers can solve their depth issues in the secondary.
The pipe dream for the Steelers is that the youngster Ladd McConkey could be pried out of the Los Angeles Chargers, but a more likely trade option is Quentin Johnston. McConkey is a do-it-all receiver who fills almost every need the Steelers have on offense.
Johnston is not, however. He's speedy, but has a problem getting in the lineup and catching the ball. As a last resort, it's better than nothing. At the same time, is it?
The Steelers could also look to the Chargers for defensive help , and two options stand out. One is former Steelers cornerback Donte Jackson, who excels in zone coverage schemes and brings steady production to the CB2 position.
A bit bigger of a goal is Cam Hart. A long and rangy outside cornerback with upside, the Steelers could get a player still on his rookie deal with the potential to be a starter for multiple seasons.
The Athletic's Mike DeFabo listed Amani Hooker as a potential player the Steelers could look at for secondary improvements, and what a tantalizing option he would be. A versatile safety with an NFL-leading five interceptions this season, Hooker is a big-play defensive back who potentially gives this defense its missing piece.
The Tennessee Titans battle their thoughts and failures in Week 9 before returning to action in Week 10. By then, Hooker might be on another NFL franchise, and maybe even in Pittsburgh.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Are Going to Do It Again, Aren't They?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need a wide receiver. They're one of three teams that appear to be really looking at the NFL trade deadline . But once again, they're being linked to the least exciting option available.
Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. were the big names to watch over the last several days, as the trade deadline approached. The Indianapolis Colts and Jacksonville Jaguars, respectively, aren't sold on dealing either of them, but teams like the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers and the Steelers are trying to make a push for one of the top options available.
Then, as the weekend approached and the deadline continued to near, Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley's name entered the mix. Ridley became the third-biggest name to watch, but a much different option than Downs or Thomas.
And, of course, everyone is going to guess that'll be who the Steelers land.
I’d rather the Steelers make no move than trade anything for Ridley. They tried the end of career receiver trade last year. https://t.co/vThkETr12U
CALVIN RIDLEY THE PITTSBURGH STEELERS LOVE YOU 😭 pic.twitter.com/l6EB0fYsij
Unlike 25-year-old Downs and 24-year-old Thomas, Ridley is 32 years old. Downs is on an expiring contract and Thomas has another year left on a rookie deal. Ridley is in the second-to-last year of a four-year, $92 million contract. Next season, he'd make $29.75 million unless he's moved. His dead cap if released is $7.5 million.
Ridley also has less receiving yards than Downs and Thomas on the season.
For Steelers fans, this may feel like deja vu. Pittsburgh is chasing a wide receiver at the deadline, clearly in need of help to make a push in the second half of the season and improve their offense, and instead of competing with other teams adding help, they'd be choosing the least favorable of those available.
Now, Ridley is a much better option than names like Adam Thielen, Mike Williams and Marquez Valdes-Scantling have been in years past, but in this year's field of options, he's very clearly No. 3.
The Steelers have a chance to chase a player in Downs who may step onto the field as their WR2 before the end of the season. The speedy inside receiver has reliable hands, great separation ability and upside he still has yet to reach.
Thomas may have fallen off with Jacksonville, but this is a 1,200-yard, 10-touchdown rookie just two years ago. With another year left on his rookie contract and first-round potential, any team that wants to take a swing should be willing to take one on the Jaguars' wideout.
Both are more expensive, though.
Ridley will likely be a late-round NFL Draft pick, while Downs could go as high as a third-rounder , and Thomas is expected to be worth even more.
So, here we go again. The Steelers know exactly what they need at the NFL trade deadline. Will they finally break the streak of disappointing additions, or is this year different?
It feels like, while it may still be better than years past, the excitement about the next addition in Pittsburgh is starting to die down, and the worry of repeating history is starting to creep in.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: Seahawks Were on the Right Side of Two of NFL's Worst Deadline Trades
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks general manager John Schneider is one of the longest-tenured GMs in the league. He's been in charge in Seattle since 2010 and has led them to plenty of success throughout his career, including building two championship teams.
Part of what makes Schneider so good is his ability to pull of big trades that benefit his team . He's hopeful that his recent move for guard Quenton Nelson could be the missing piece on their offense. If so, it could go down as a major win for the Seahawks, but it won't necessarily be his greatest pre-deadline deals.
That's because Schneider has fleeced teams in the past. That includes being on the right side of two trades that Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski named among the 10 worst deadline moves over the past decade .
After being unable to come to terms with Duane Brown on an extension, the Houston Texans sent Brown, along with a 2018 fifth-round pick, to Seattle inexchange for a 2018 third-round pick and a 2019 second-round pick. As Sobleski says, the Texans thought they were getting excellent value for a player set to decline, but instead, they gave Seattle a stud who made two Pro Bowls in four seasons.
"The Houston Texans thought they were getting a premium return for a declining veteran. They were wrong," Sobleski wrote. "Duane Brown was 32 years old when the Texans shipped him to the Seattle Seahawks. Brown would go on to play seven more seasons, including four and a half in Seattle."
Following his stint in Seattle, Brown signed a two-year deal with the New York Jets. He retired following the 2023 season, playing until he was 38.
Brown isn't the only veteran who was sent to Seattle only to surpass expectations. Schneider landed Leonard Williams during the 2023 season in exchange for a 2024 second-round pick and a fifth-rounder in 2025. Considering he was on an expiring contract, plus the fact that the Giants were rebuilding, it made sense to move Williams. That said, the return wasn't enough, according to Sobleski, considering what Williams has done in Seattle.
"In retrospect, the Giants didn't get enough in return for Williams, who has been dominant with the Seahawks. Granted, landing second- and fifth-round picks for an expiring contract is usually viewed as an excellent return. In this case, it wasn't.Williams has since been named to two Pro Bowls and a second-team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl in 2025 as Seattle's best defensive player," Sobleski wrote.
Williams admitted that he was considering ending his career, but fell in love with the game again in Seattle. The culture, and of course, the winning has him focused like never before and he's been one of the more prominent leaders of the Dark Side Defense.

title: Seahawks Get Drew Lock Injury Update After Cardinals Game
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock is recovering from an oblique injury that he suffered in Week 9 against the Arizona Cardinals.
There was a question mark surrounding whether Lock's injury was serious or not. However, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed on Seattle Sports 710 AM that Lock's injury isn't considered serious and that he could still start in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald told @BrockHuard and @TheMikeSalk on Seattle Sports 710 ESPN that he is ruling out Sam Darnold for this week’s game vs the Raiders. But tests on Drew Lock’s oblique injury were “good”, and they believe he can start vs. the Raiders. pic.twitter.com/mba3rSJrZt
Getting Lock back for Week 10 is important, especially because Sam Darnold's status is also up in the air as he is dealing with quad and rib injuries. During Lock's start against the Cardinals in Week 9, he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown.
Bucks are 2-0 at the start of this season, and the team really appreciates what he is able to do in a backup role when he is called upon in case of an injury.
"He's a beast. He just threw it around. Just went after it," Macdonald said via the team's website .
"I think our medical people deserve a shout-out too for putting a great plan together and treating Drew, and Jalen Milroe too, operating our offense when he took the snaps that he took and being ready to play in case Drew couldn't go or couldn't finish. Really a great team effort, but Drew, I don't know how you can get any tougher. Both guys, just tough as nails."
The Seahawks will monitor Lock's entry throughout the week, but if he is unable to go, they will try to see if Darnold can make a return. There is reason to believe, however, that Darnold will miss this upcoming game as well.
The Seahawks' bye is in Week 11, so giving Darnold extended rest to fully heal from his quad and rib injuries is important. This means the team will likely look to Milroe to make his first career start. The 2025 third-round pick has been planted behind Darnold and Lock on the depth chart, but the team may have to turn to him if both Darnold and Lock are injured.
The kickoff between the Seahawks and Raiders is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 pm PT inside Allegiant Stadium in Sin City. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: 3 Reasons Why Seahawks Should Trade Sam Darnold
full_text:
Hear me out on this one. I know it’s a little nutty, and if there’s one thing this world doesn’t need more of, it’s nutty NFL trade propositions.
But after the Seattle Seahawks' Week 9 game against the Arizona Cardinals , where an injured Drew Lock was able to play the sound, fundamental, functional game that Sam Darnold hasn’t been able to recently, I just feel like we’ve got to play with it for a few minutes.
Maybe this is a little harsh. But I think it’s accurate. The Seahawks have eight games plus the postseason remaining, and Darnold is currently sidelined with multiple injuries . His play to this point has been bad, and if/when Darnold returns he will still be working with the flailing Brian Fleury as offensive coordinator. So righting the ship this season is highly unlikely.
So then you’re in the offseason. Darnold will be on the last year of his deal, which has a cap hit of $41.9 million. Extending him, even with his poor play, will put a heavy weight on the cap for the foreseeable future. As Baker Mayfield can attest , you often get paid based on your best work, not your most recent work, as an NFL quarterback.
And John Schneider has already shown that he’s very hesitant to give out the quarterback mega-deal, so the odds of him playing along are low. So, with all apologies to Sam, who will always be remembered fondly in this fanbase, it’s very difficult for me to imagine any other way for this to go. One way or another, he’s not around next season.
The Vikings, who play a big game tonight, are one piece away from a clear super bowl contender. Unfortunately, that one piece is a quarterback. It’s a team that is swimming with talented players and brilliant coaches, but is stuck choosing between Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz to line up and take snaps every week. They have to do better.
Normally, they couldn’t do better. Acquiring a new quarterback midseason is almost impossible. On top of finding one available for trade, there’s the issue of learning a new offense with new teammates after the trade. It takes months to really fit into an NFL offense, especially as a quarterback. But guess who already knows the Minnesota offense?
I don’t mean that in a general sense. Darnold was literally the starting quarterback for the Vikings two years ago, under Kevin O’Connell and many of the still-present assistant coaches. He even knows quite a few of his potential teammates. This might just be the one exact circumstance where a quarterback could slot right in on a new team.
During that 2024 season, O’Connell was able to get a full season of quality play out of Darnold, with the meltdown hitting at the very end. Despite the evidence that Darnold isn’t a great quarterback , it’s entirely possible that he could look like one in the Minnesota offense. And that’s a lot more than you can say for Murray or Wentz so far this season.
It all comes together, doesn’t it? Assuming that the Vikings don’t get good quarterback play tonight, and are staring down the possibility of wasting this remarkable team, you call them up for a trade. Maybe you can get Minnesota’s second round pick? Could you get their first if you offered to send back a third? It should be a seller’s market here.
I will offer up the one obvious counter, which is that the Seahawks shouldn’t be helping an NFC rival get better when they themselves are still in the fight. That has to be weighed here. It’s just hard for me to worry about that when I envision in my mind what Brian Fleury’s offense would look like against Brian Flores, regardless of who their quarterback is that day.
If we end up getting bounced from the playoffs by Darnold in a Vikings uniform, people will certainly have their laughs. I just don’t think that possibility is enough of a deterrent when compared to the definite value of extra draft capital you could get. And if it helps the Vikings beat the 49ers or Rams in January…well, that’s something too, isn’t it?

title: The Truth About Seahawks QB Sam Darnold’s Recent Struggles
full_text:
There’s a civil war over the quarterback position in the Seattle Seahawks fanbase right now. As someone who has been covering this team in some capacity for the last decade-plus, I’ve become intimately familiar with quarterback civil wars.
We’ve seen it with Russell Wilson, we’ve seen it with Geno Smith, and now, we’re going through it with Sam Darnold.
Obviously, Sam Darnold has been playing poorly so far this season for the Seahawks . That’s apparent to anyone who’s been watching the games, including those who continue to stand in his corner. However, there’s an obvious scapegoat to pin Sam’s struggles on, in the form of Brian Fleury. He wasn’t here last year, he’s here now, therefore, it’s his fault.
Don’t take any of what I’m about to say as a defense of Brian Fleury, who I do believe has been very poor to this point as offensive coordinator and playcaller. Now, even if we ignore the fact that Drew Lock has looked better in Fleury’s offense than Darnold so far, this argument hinges on Sam’s struggles starting this season. Let’s make sure they actually have.
In 2025, Sam Darnold quarterbacked a top ten offense and won the super bowl. So obviously, he must have played pretty well. During the first nine games of the season, he played exceptionally well . His line over that stretch of football was 2,262 passing yards, 71.1% completion, 17 touchdowns, and 6 interceptions, for a rating of 116.5.
And then, the Rams defense turned him upside down in Los Angeles, and he wasn’t the same. Over the last eight regular season games, Darnold posted 1,786 passing yards, 64.7% completion, 8 touchdowns, and 8 interceptions, for a rating of 83.2. Even if you remove the outlier game in LA, it’s a massive dropoff in performance.
Advanced numbers tell an even more compelling story. Over that nine game stretch to start the year, Darnold was #1 in the entire NFL in EPA/play (0.337), Success Rate (55.9%), and Completion Percentage Over Expected (11.1%), all while being second in air yards (9.6). Genuinely , he was an MVP candidate. But what about after the Rams game?
Sam’s EPA/play dipped to -0.004 (26th), his Success Rate fell to 50.9% (6th), and his CPOE actually went negative to -0.3 (19th). All the while, his air yards shriveled to 6.8 (23rd). Over that stretch, you might not even be able to call him average. It was easy to ignore since the team kept winning, and Sam came up big in the most important game, but it’s there.
Things got better in the postseason, but even that was accomplished almost entirely on the back of an incredible performance against the Rams (0.408 EPA). He was highly efficient against the 49ers (0.362 EPA), but was asked to do so little in that game it barely registered. His super bowl performance (-0.009 EPA) was back to below average .
The point I’m trying to make here is that the narrative about Sam playing great until Fleury showed up doesn’t match up with reality. He’s worse now (-0.014 EPA), but the problem started under Klint Kubiak. Even under the instruction of a great offensive coordinator, Darnold could only maintain a high level of play for half a season.
So, when discussing Darnold in Seattle, there needs to be a bit of a reality check. It was easy to ignore in the moment, and even shortly after, since the team kept winning, but it’s there. So if your solution to Darnold’s poor play is to reunite him with a quality coordinator, just know that it’s no guarantee of getting Sam back to his MVP-candidate self.
This organization and fanbase will always have love and appreciation for Darnold. He helped them win a Super Bowl, in a season where most assumed the team would be battling just to make the playoffs. But that doesn’t change the fact that, with about a season’s worth of evidence to back it up, he looks like a pretty average player right now .

title: Hanich Panic Meter: Seahawks' Defense Showed They Had to Improve
full_text:
Nearly halfway through the 2026 NFL Season, there was clearly something wrong with the Seattle Seahawks, both physically and mentally. This was evident in the Seahawks’ 34-17 home loss on Monday Night Football to the Chicago Bears. The Seahawks needed to make some changes to save their season amid the long list of growing injuries.
​Week 9 versus the Arizona Cardinals is the Seahawks' "get right" game on both sides of the ball as they come out with a 17-3 win . While there are some glaring issues on offense that the Seahawks need to address, there are some areas that the Dark Side Defense needed to fix. Seattle ranks at the top in major defensive categories; there were two huge concerns that head coach Mike Macdonald needed to fix against the Cardinals.
​The Dark Side Defense was one of the toughest defenses to play against, but there were certain aspects that made them vulnerable. The Seahawks were sixth in the league in points allowed per game (19.9) entering Sunday, but they were last in allowing fourth-down conversions (90.9%) and last in red zone defense (83.2%). One of the biggest reasons is that if the Seahawks don't get the quick stop and their backs are against the wall, they crack under pressure.
​Macdonald and veteran edge rusher DeMarcus Lawrence knew this was an issue coming out of Week 8 and knew this had to change. They both mentioned that the days leading up to the Cardinals were going to be crucial. It would be the team's best chances to fix their biggest mistakes against competition before they played more efficient teams.
​The Dark Side Defense had one of their best performances on Sunday against the Cardinals. The Seahawks allowed 198 total yards from the Cardinals with only 50 yards coming from the running game. The Cardinals only converted 4-of-13 on third downs in the game.
​The biggest moments were Seattle's clutch play, which was on fourth-down plays and in the red zone. Arizona only converted one of its two fourth-down attempts and was 0-of-2 in the red zone.
​This was against a Cardinals offense that had some traction towards a more productive unit. Arizona entered Sunday with the 20th-ranked scoring offense (21.9) and the 11th most efficient offense in converting on fourth downs (61.5%). The Seahawks held their own against a young offense that has shown signs of becoming a dangerous team in the future.
​The Seahawks were without some of their stars in defensive tackle Leonard Williams and edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu. They were also without some reliable depth players like defensive tackle Brandon Pili.
​Seattle (5-4) now has this momentum and can prepare for the second half of the season, which starts with a road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (4-5). Like the Cardinals, the Raiders also possess a solid slate of young players that have been improving.
The Raiders have a head coach in Klint Kubiak and offensive coordinator in Andrew Janocko, who were the Seahawks’ offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach last season , respectively. They know how to beat the Seahawks’ elite defense regularly.

title: 3 Takeaways From Seahawks Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back in the win column after a 17-3 victory against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 at Lumen Field.
The defense flexed its muscles and proved exactly why they are the best unit in the league, bouncing back from their struggles against the Chicago Bears in their previous game . Here's a look at three takeaways from the contest:
Drew Lock did his job as the Seahawks' backup quarterback. He kept the ball in Seattle's possession and managed the game properly. It was revealed following the game that Lock suffered an oblique injury during the contest but did not have to leave.
This puts his status up in the air for the team's Week 10 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, which could be a trap game given that former offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is on the other sideline.
Lock could have performed better, but it's possible that his struggles were linked to his oblique injury, so it's unfair to truly evaluate this performance fully. The hope is that Lock will be healthy for the game. Otherwise, we might be seeing Jalen Milroe make his first NFL start.
After struggling in his first game back from injury against the Bears, veteran running back Zach Charbonnet looked like the leading rusher the team needs against the Cardinals. He ran the ball 16 times for 77 yards, averaging nearly 5 yards per carry in the win. Charbonnet was able to move the Seahawks downfield throughout the game, which is something the team has not had consistently enough this season.
Charbonnet was always viewed as the team's top running back when he returned, and now that he is back, the Seahawks can breathe a sigh of relief knowing they have someone who can lead the charge on the ground.
After letting 34 points stick on the board against the Bears, the Seahawks responded with another strong outing against the Cardinals. It's the second time in three weeks they've allowed a mere field goal, which was given up on the opening drive.
The Darkside defense has been the top unit in the league over the last two seasons, and it's clear after this game that the defense can still go out and win the Seahawks a football game. They will face tougher opponents down the stretch and in a potential playoff situation, but if they can find a way to remain dominant against these teams, it could carry them all the way to another deep playoff run.

title: Seahawks QB Drew Lock's Status For Week 10 'Up in the Air' After Injury
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks got through an injury-stricken Week 9 with a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals , but it’s not looking like it’s going to get any better next week.
Quarterback Sam Darnold missed his second full game of the season, thrusting Drew Lock back into the starting role. Lock, though he was able to play the entire game, came in with an elbow injury to his throwing arm and suffered an oblique injury in the third quarter.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame that he isn’t sure who will be under center in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
“I think we’ll probably re-evaluate [Darnold’s situation] earlier in the week, but I’m assuming we’re probably going to have to make a decision on who we’re going to get ready and how we’re going to do that,” Macdonald said. “Drew’s situation, we’ll have to evaluate that as well. Unfortunately, it seems like it’s kind of up in the air right now.”
Macdonald was asked to clarify his answer, particularly on Lock’s situation. If both Darnold and Lock are out, former third-round pick Jalen Milroe would be in line to make his first NFL start.
“[Lock] made it out [of the game], but I’ve sat here before and told you a guy would be ready and then he wasn’t,” Macdonald said, grinning. “So, [leaving] my options open.”
Lock was more optimistic after the game, stating he would get his oblique looked at on Sunday night and it was “not too bad.” He also said his elbow felt good during the game.
“I wouldn’t say it did,” Lock said when asked if the injury affected his play. “I went into the tent, had it looked at, came back out, [was like] ‘Let me see how it feels throwing the ball’ … I mean, you feel it, but it’s nothing that was going to keep me on the sideline.”
It was a weird week for Lock, especially since the Seahawks were coming off a Monday night loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 9. On a short week, Lock only had one full day of practice, even though he was slated to start. Milroe received a lot of the reps during the week.
“The only balls that I threw were on Thursday,” Lock said. “We did a little bit of a split there, but I would say I took a majority of the reps Thursday, and that was it.”
Milroe, the 92nd pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, has not thrown a pass in a regular-season NFL game. He was used in a limited, run-first capacity as a rookie, totaling three carries for four yards and a fumble.
Seattle’s practice reports during the week will be telling regarding who is trending toward starting against the Raiders.

title: 4 Winners, 1 Loser in Seahawks' Week 9 Win vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are celebrating after a dominant 17-3 win against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 inside Lumen Field.
The Seahawks surrendered a field goal to Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland on the opening drive, but were able to keep them off the scoreboard for the remainder of the game. Meanwhile, the Seahawks tacked on a pair of touchdowns in the second quarter, both from tight end AJ Barner.
Here's a look at the winners and losers from the matchup:
Unsurprisingly, Barner is the big winner of the game, scoring both touchdowns for the Seahawks in their win. He ran the ball in from a yard out to give the Seahawks a lead, and he also caught a pass from seven yards out later in the quarter. It's Barner's second and third touchdowns of the season, and he is slowly working his way up the ranks on the offense.
Rookie running back Jadarian Price played in his second game back from injured reserve. While he did not lead the team in rushing, he was able to make a big impact on the receiving end. Price was the team's leading receiver with four catches for 54 yards in the win.
Being able to contribute both on the ground and through the air is a massive part of the offense. It's a promising sign that the Seahawks are getting something from their rookie after not getting a whole lot in the first half of the season.
Drew Lock is 2-0 as the team's starting quarterback. While his statistics didn't pop off the page, he was able to stay upright and keep the football in Seattle's possession, which has been their biggest struggle throughout the season.
Lock is possibly going to be needed to start next week when the team faces off against their former offensive coordinator, Klint Kubiak, and the Las Vegas Raiders.
It's hard to pinpoint one specific winner on the defensive side of the ball, but the entire dark side defense has held the team to just a field goal for the second time this season. Julian Love led the way with eight tackles, while Byron Murphy, Demarcus Lawrence, and Dante Fowler Jr. each recorded a sack. The team put a lot of pressure on the Cardinals all afternoon long and made quite the impression after giving up 34 points on Monday Night Football last week against the Chicago Bears.
The Seahawks were incredibly dominant today, and it's hard to pick a loser from anyone on that sideline. Therefore, we're giving today's loser status to the referees for making some pretty questionable calls throughout the game.
Some of these calls could have compromised the Seahawks' defensive efforts, but ultimately the unit was too strong to have anybody stopping them, including the referees.
Pass interference on the seahawks, this is a terrible call pic.twitter.com/LkQg7JVL3G
The #NFL refs called unnecessary roughness instead of taunting which is why #Seahawks Devon Witherspoon reacted this way: The refs suck today. Video credit: @kairo7news https://t.co/JKOUEH0rrg pic.twitter.com/rF5LDXQIQf
These are just a couple of the many odd calls throughout the game, but the Seahawks can now focus on facing off against the Raiders in Week 10, in hopes of going into the bye with some momentum.

title: Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba Hits Major Milestone in First Half vs. Cardinals
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has done it again. The superstar pass-catcher reached 1,000 receiving yards in the first half of the team's Week 9 game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.
It's Smith-Njigba's third straight season with at least 1,000 receiving yards, and he did it in just nine games for the second straight year. Smith-Njigba joins Tyler Lockett (2019-22) and Steve Largent (1978-81, 1983-86) as the only Seahawks wide receiver to reach that mark in three straight seasons or more.
Smith-Njigba entered Sunday's game against the Cardinals with 89 catches for 985 yards and nine touchdowns. He had exactly three catches for 15 yards to hit the golden number in the first quarter.
Even if he didn't catch another pass the rest of the game, Smith-Njigba would still be on pace for 173 catches, 1,888 yards and 17 touchdowns in 2026 — all numbers that would surpass his record-breaking 2025 season that ended with him winning Offensive Player of the Year.
This year, however, Smith-Njigba could break league history.
The likelihood, however, of Smith-Njigba going quiet for three quarters is slim. He has had at least 102 yards receiving in seven of eight games this season and has surpassed 150 yards twice. The former first-round pick is accounting for 51.5% of the Seahawks' receiving yards, as one of the only things offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has schemed effectively is getting the ball to Seattle's best player.
If he reaches 100 yards receiving once again, Smith-Njigba would keep his season-long pace to potentially break Calvin Johnson's all-time record of 1,964 yards in 2012. This has been yet another instance of Smith-Njigba posting one of the most dominant pass-catching seasons in NFL history, and it hasn't started slowing down.
Ever since a mediocre rookie season in 2023, Smith-Njigba has been on a meteoric rise to stardom. He logged 1,130 yards and six touchdowns in his second season, also tying Lockett's then-franchise-record 100 catches in a single campaign. He broke that record, along with many others, in 2025.
The Seahawks currently lead the Cardinals 7-3 in the second quarter with Drew Lock quarterbacking the offense in the absence of Sam Darnold, who is out with rib and glute injuries.

title: 7 Seahawks Ruled Inactive vs. Cardinals: What It Means for Week 9
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are putting together their final bits of preparation as they warm up to face off against NFC West rival Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 at Lumen Field.
The Seahawks are watching their injury report grow as the season goes along, and several key players are inactive for the game against the Cardinals as a result. Here's a look at the full list of inactives for both teams and what it means going into the game.
The offensive line is a bit banged up on the left side, as Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson are both out for the team with their respective injuries. Cross is dealing with a high ankle sprain, while Nelson has a knee injury. Both are expected to be out for multiple weeks.
Leading into the Week 11 bye, with those two out for today's game, look for Anthony Bradford and Josh Jones to step up in their place.
The team is also without quarterback Sam Darnold, who is dealing with quad and rib injuries . That will put Drew Lock in the starting lineup, even though he's been dealing with a right elbow injury for the past couple of weeks and was limited in practice over the last couple of days.
The team is also dealing with a loss, as Leonard Williams is out with a stinger. This will put a lot of pressure on Byron Murphy II to be the leader on the defensive line.
The most notable inactive for the Cardinals is running back Bam Knight, who has taken advantage of his teammate Jeremiyah Love being injured throughout the season. Knight ran the ball 15 times for 80 yards in Week 6 against the Los Angeles Rams, but his absence today opens the door for Tyler Allgeier to be the lead back for the Cardinals.
Kickoff between the Cardinals and Seahawks is scheduled for 1:25 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

title: 4 Winners, 2 Losers From 49ers' Win Over Raiders: Jordan Watkins Flashes
full_text:
For most of the game, the San Francisco 49ers had an easy go of it against the Las Vegas Raiders.
It went as expected, with the 49ers winning 38-17 to get back on track after the Bye. So, who were the winners and losers from the 49ers' expected win? We break it all down below.
Have a day, Jordan Watkins. The second-year receiver made a nice impact in this game, tallying four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. Three of his four catches went for first downs.
He also ran a team-high 26 routes. Watkins got his opportunities in this game and delivered. That is certainly going to go a long way with Kyle Shanahan.
Watkins came close to having a breakout game in Week 7 against the Falcons, but couldn't secure a couple of big-time catches. This time, he made sure to seize his opportunities. His stock is up.
This was one of Fred Warner's best performances of the season. As usual, he forced a fumble, his fifth of the year and a career-high for him in a season.
No one executes the "peanut punch" as perfectly as Warner does. But his most impressive play came in the fourth quarter, when he stone-walled Kirk Cousins on a goal-line quarterback sneak.
Warner continues to prove why he's a cut above the rest. He's trekking towards earning the Defensive Player of the Year award. If there were midseason awards, he'd win it right now.
The yips may have disappeared for Eddy Pineiro , as he nailed every single one of his extra-point (5) and field-goal attempts (1) in this game. That will go a long way for him.
It proves that he's greatly benefiting from the Bye Week. The only way he would shake off the yips was by getting away and clearing his mind. After one game back, it looks like he's succeeded.
One question entering this game was how the 49ers would integrate Marques Sigle. He's been out for the last three games with an ankle sprain, but he was playing well before his injury.
The 49ers couldn't deny him snaps, which means one safety had to cede playing time. Sure enough, the 49ers had Sigle take some snaps from Ji'Ayir Brown, which was the right call.
Sigle saw 28 snaps, while Brown saw 32. This is a great sign for Sigle that he still has the coaching staff's trust and that there's a world where he can supplant Brown.
One reason the 49ers couldn't enjoy the win against the Raiders was that rookie Gracen Halton suffered a season-ending broken ankle. Halton got rolled up by teammate Keion White.
You have to feel for Halton. He was killing it this season and was arguably the 49ers' best rookie. Now, his promising season comes to a halt, and the 49ers lose an impactful defensive lineman.
Kirk Cousins was fairly comfortable whenever he had to drop back to pass. That's because the 49ers' pass rush only pressured him nine times on his 32 dropbacks, with zero sacks.
It was a pitiful display considering they got Nick Bosa back and reunited with DeForest Buckner. The 49ers' pass rush didn't look any different than it did against the Falcons.
This should be cause for concern. Maybe it pushes the 49ers to make a trade for another defensive lineman, especially after Halton's injury.

title: 5 Notable Lineup Changes the 49ers Made in Week 9
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers came out of the bye week and had a few notable lineup decisions to make. What were some noteworthy differences coming out of the bye week?
Demarcus Robinson returned to the lineup, and was second amongst the wide receivers in snaps. Brandin Cooks went from a starter to the 49ers' number three. Jacob Cowing went from an increasing role to fading out of the picture. Perhaps more notable is that Jordan Watkins still led the team in snaps and receiving production. When Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans come back, there is a chance that Watkins joins them as the top three , and Robinson is a fourth man.
The team added DeForest Buckner, and he stepped into a normal starter's workload of snaps. That meant that rookie Gracen Halton was going to play less. He went from getting the bulk of the snaps on the defensive front to being the third man and playing less than 20 snaps. He was already going to play a career-low in snaps, but an injury made that official. Halton left the game on a cart with an air cast on his leg.
The team was not going to lean on him as much, but now they might not have him for the foreseeable future. James Thompson and Sebastian Valdez went from rotational contributors to being out of the mix.
The team got Nick Bosa back. He led the way for the group. Then, the team mostly had Mykel Williams and Romell Height rotate based on down, distance, and personnel. Keion White mixed in for Bosa and also got a few snaps, mixing in with Williams and Height. Bosa finished with 30 snaps; the other three were all under 20.
Marques Sigle returned after missing two weeks. However, Malik Mustapha might have been the 49ers' best safety when he was gone. So, the team decided to rotate all three safeties. Mustapha played with Sigle. Mustapha played with Brown. Then, Brown played with Sigle. They rotated all three throughout the game. The 49ers should eventually settle on a pairing, but it's smart to use this time to see what works best.
The 49ers saw Renardo Green leave with what could be a serious injury. Rookie Ephesians Prysock stepped in for him now that they had released Jack Jones .

title: How the 49ers' Trade Deadline Plans have Shifted After Their Week 9 Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 to move to 7-1 just two days before the NFL trade deadline. Returning from the bye week, the game has changed the team's trade deadline needs.
The talk of the 49ers adding to the offensive line or a skill player like a receiver seems to be gone. Connor Colby has been up and down and appears to be matchup-dependent. Still, he has shown that he is a capable enough starter, even if they could improve the spot.
At receiver, the 49ers got Demarcus Robinson back healthy. Jordan Watkins has strung three solid games together. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel will be back soon, as will De’Zhaun Stribling.
All of a sudden, it does not look like the team needs a wide receiver as much as they have in recent weeks.
Nick Bosa returned from injury but looked a bit slow as he is still working himself back from a calf injury. Former first-round pick Mykel Williams had the bye week to reset and came out flat. Rookie Romello Height has not seen enough consistent growth, and Keion White is a rotational runner.
With DeForest Buckner added to the interior, it is starting to look like the biggest need right now is an edge rusher. Khalil Mack has been speculated to the 49ers for weeks. Sitting at 0-8, the Los Angeles Chargers might finally be ready to make a trade.
If the 49ers cannot add to the front seven, they need to find a way to add to the secondary. Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir might be back soon, but both suffered injuries in Week 9. With Jack Jones cut and Nate Hobbs inactive, the team was quite thin at cornerback.
Hobbs might be getting a helmet soon, and Ephesians Prysock is being eased in. Still, another cornerback would not hurt.
The team could also add a safety. They rotated three safeties and mixed and matched who played with each other. Malik Mustapha was benched to start the year. Marques Sigle was benched last year. Ji’Ayir Brown has been benched throughout his career.
The team has three options at safety, and at the same time, they do not have a long-term option at safety. It is an underrated need.

title: 49ers Grades After 38-17 Win Over the Raiders: Kyle Shanahan Makes Key Adjustment
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy played well, but hasn't played like an MVP candidate since Mike Evans went down. Today, he scrambled extremely well, but that's partly because he didn't trust his receivers, with the exception of Jordan Watkins (more on him in a minute). Purdy usually lets it rip before receivers have made their breaks. Now, he's holding the ball longer than ever and using his legs more than he probably would like to. Because when he does let it rip, and Evans isn't on the field, Purdy often gets intercepted. Either Evans needs to come back soon, or the 49ers need to trade for another wide receiver. Otherwise, Purdy will struggle against decent defenses. Fortunately for him, the Raiders' defense is laughable.
Christian McCaffrey averaged just 3.8 yards per carry against a horrendous run defense, but he also scored two touchdowns -- one on the ground and one through the air. And he wasn't even the 49ers' leading rusher. That was Kaelon Black, who averaged a whopping 6.4 yards per carry. The more the 49ers give him the ball, the better their offense performs, because the 49ers are a run-first offense, and they can't control the game with their rushing attack if they use just one running back. Today, they ran the ball 43 times. They couldn't have done that without Black.
Jordan Watkins committed two penalties and still was the only good wide receiver in the game for the 49ers. He caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown, and looked like a quality complementary receiver, but not a go-to guy. Not someone who could catch 10 passes in a game. Against better defenses, the 49ers will need Mike Evans or some other wide receiver they could add via trade in the next day or two (George Pickens? Brian Thomas Jr.?). Demarcus Robinson certainly doesn't count. Neither does Deebo Samuel.
George Kittle had four catches for 58 yards. Luke Farrell had zero catches yet again. Hard to believe the 49ers gave him a three-year deal just to make no impact. Thank goodness they still have Kittle.
They gave up just one sack and helped pave the way for the offense to gain 190 yards on the ground. Still, they got stopped on a quarterback sneak because Jake Brendel and Dominick Puni generated no movement at the point of attack against a junior varsity defensive line.
The 49ers' defensive linemen recorded four tackles for loss and helped shut down the Raiders' anemic run game, but they never sacked Kirk Cousins, who is extremely sackable. Fortunately for the D-linemen, Cousins threw three bonehead interceptions. Still, the 49ers probably were expecting Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner to superchange their pass rush, but they didn't. Neither made a big impact, and the 49ers now haven't recorded a sack in their past two games. In addition, they lost rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton to a season-ending leg injury with fewer than four minutes left in the game while leading by 18 points. That hurts. The 49ers might need to trade for another pass rusher before Tuesday's deadline.
Fred Warner might be the best player in the NFL. Today, he recorded just 5 tackles, but he forced a fumble, recovered a fumble, and jumped over the pile at the goal line to stop a quarterback sneak for a two-yard loss. That final play was one I've never seen a linebacker make. I didn't know it was physically possible to stop a quarterback for a two-yard loss on a sneak. Warner invents new ways to be great every week. And he isn't the only good linebacker on the team. Dre Greenlaw had three tackles for loss, and rookie Jaden Dugger had a pick-six.
Renardo Green and Malik Mustapha each intercepted Cousins once, which is impressive considering Cousins wasn't under much pressure. Still, Cousins gift-wrapped those interceptions. Collectively, this group gave up 7 catches for 111 yards and a touchdown to Brock Bowers, the only legitimate weapon on the Raiders. You'd like to think a Super Bowl-caliber defense could shut down one player, even if he's great. In addition, the 49ers gave up 3 catches for 37 yards to backup tight end Michael Mayer, who fumbled at the goal line and was flagged for a ticky-tack offensive pass interference penalty in the end zone that negated a touchdown catch. The 49ers seem to have issues covering quality tight ends. Something to monitor the rest of the season.
Eddy Pineiro made all of his field-goal attempts and extra points, but the kickoff coverage team gave up a 54-yard return. Unacceptable.
Raheem Morris' defense forced five turnovers, but most of them were gifts from the Raiders, who stink. It's alarming that Morris' defense generated minimal pressure on Cousins and struggled to cover the Raiders' two tight ends, even when they lacked a viable threat at wide receiver and running back. The 49ers should consider trading for a safety before the deadline because Ji'Ayir Brown is a liability.
On offense, Kyle Shanahan won the game because he committed to the run game and finally trusted his young weapons, unlike two weeks ago when the 49ers lost to the Falcons, who are worse than the Raiders. In that game, Shanahan refused to feature Watkins and Black, and so the 49ers lost. Today, Watkins was the leading receiver, and Black was the leading rusher. And as a result, the 49ers offense scored 31 points. Good to see Shanahan honestly size up his performance during the bye week so he could improve. Now, he needs to make another trade.

title: Promising 49ers Rookie Suffers Season-Ending Injury
full_text:
Injuries continue to pile up for the San Francisco 49ers .
This time, it is rookie Gracen Halton. He broke his ankle in the 49ers' Week 9 38-17 win against the Las Vegas Raiders. He's expected to miss the remainder of the season.
Brutal. Just brutal for Halton. His season-ending injury has made it tough for the 49ers to enjoy their win. Halton was having a strong, promising season. He established himself as a key player on the defensive line in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
Halton broke out massively in that game with a sack and a forced fumble that he recovered for a touchdown. He was elite in that game, but has been solid in every other game.
The 49ers drafted Halton for his pass-rushing skills, and he's lived up to the bill. However, he's been a surprising help defending the run, too. Halton's been an impactful player through and through.
His loss will sting the 49ers and his development. This makes acquiring DeForest Buckner look even better. They reunited with Buckner to give them a premier interior presence.
But it was also to strengthen their defensive line depth. Now, their depth takes a hit with Halton ruled out for the rest of the season.
Second-year defensive tackle C.J. West will be back soon, which will help their depth a bit. But West isn't good. Not even a little bit.
He will fill Halton's spot in name and nothing more. Mykel Williams will need to be the player that steps up and finally prove the 49ers right for drafting him No. 11 overall.
Williams was quiet in the win against the Raiders. He made zero impact in the game. That needs to be the last time he tursn into a ghost with Halton out.
Sebastian Valdez will need to step up as well. If not, the 49ers can always consider a trade. The deadline is in a couple of days.
Another defensive tackle or an edge rusher would go a long way for the 49ers. They have an amazing defense. It would be a shame if they didn't maximize it by trying to make their pass rush come alive.
Surprisingly, they've performed better against the run than rushing the passer. The 49ers will have much to think about over the next 48 hours.

title: 6 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 9 Win Against Raiders
full_text:
As expected, the San Francisco 49ers took care of business at home against the Las Vegas Raiders , winning 38-17.
It did get a little messy for the 49ers in the third quarter, but they were never in any real danger of losing. Let's unpack the six biggest takeaways from the 49ers' Week 9 win against the Raiders.
I think so, and it isn't particularly close. Fred Warner has been on a tear this season. His performance against the Raiders perfectly illustrates how he's played all season long.
Look no further than his typical "peanut punch" on his fifth forced fumble of the season. That's his career high in a season, and he's only played in eight games. His previous high was four.
How about his goal-line stand early in the fourth quarter to deny Kirk Cousins a touchdown on the quarterback sneak? That was by far his most impressive play of the game.
No other defensive player is playing as well and is helping his team more than Warner. Warner is bound to win the Defensive Player of the Year award at this rate.
He came close to having a breakout game in Week 7, but Jordan Watkins made up for it today against the Raiders. Watkins tallied four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. Most of his catches were chunk plays.
His 37-yard touchdown play was his highlight of the game. Brock Purdy threw him a sweet throw with the defensive back draped all over him. Watkins can use this game as a stepping stone for future performances.
Even though Watkins had a breakout game, it wasn't enough to feel good about the 49ers' passing game. They need Mike Evans back to thrive, especially for Brock Purdy.
He played well today, but he'll never be at his best without Evans, the 49ers' real MVP. The 49ers can skate by through the air against weak teams like today. But against strong defenses, it will be bleak without Evans .
By far, the 49ers' biggest concern today was their ineffective pass rush. Kirk Cousins wasn't sacked at all, and he didn't face a ton of pressure either.
With DeForest Buckner reunited with the 49ers and Nick Bosa back , this should've been a big day for their pass rush. Instead, it was more of the same before either player returned. It's very concerning.
It should be clear as day to the 49ers that they need to make a trade for both a wide receiver and an edge rusher. Any wide receiver help will do. They don't need a premier receiver, even though that would be perfect.
The 49ers need to get Josh Downs- someone, anyone. They just can't remain content with their group anymore. As for an edge rusher, it's slim pickings on the market. The Chargers won't move Khalil Mack, and he doesn't wanna leave.
But the 49ers can't stand pat at the trade deadline. This performance against the Raiders proved that a move at receiver and edge rusher is needed. If not, they'll have their fingers crossed that everyone steps up.
Arguably, no other player benefited from the Bye Week more than Eddy Pineiro. He made all five of his extra-point attempts, along with a 35-yard field goal. Pineiro might've shaken the yips.
The Bye Week seems to have helped him reset his mind by getting away. Of course, it's just one game, but given how often he was missing kicks before the Bye, it was encouraging to see him get back on track.

title: 49ers Could Target Former 2nd-Round Pick Wide Receiver in Trade
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been tied to a lot of wide receivers prior to the NFL trade deadline. However, a potential name that has not been floated around enough but could be a good fit is former second-round wide receiver Adonai Mitchell. Mitchell is the wide receiver that the 49ers should target, according to Seth Walder of ESPN.
Walder notes that the 49ers need a receiver, combined with the Jets having a young surplus of pass-catching options.
“It's no secret that the 49ers are down bad at wide receiver,” wrote Walder. “Mitchell has long flashed more promise than results, though we saw that promise Sunday when he recorded seven receptions for 142 yards and a touchdown. The Jets might be reluctant to part with Mitchell. But because they have Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr., and Kenyon Sadiq, it's worth making a call.”
The 49ers have been tied to Wilson in trade rumors already. However, the combination of the Jets' asking price and their lack of interest in moving on from him has made that seem unlikely. However, if the Jets are not going to trade Wilson, they would be likely to listen to offers on Mitchell.
Mitchell was a draft pick by the Colts, but was essentially viewed as a throw-in for the Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade, because he had gotten off to a slow start.
Still, Mitchell had 464 yards with the Colts in 25 games. He has 566 yards with the Jets in 12 games. So, it is clear that he can be productive in the NFL. The question is how much the Jets need him now.
With Wilson ascending and two rookie pass catchers added into the mix, he is starting to fade down the pecking order. Still, this is a talent with a bit of production, and he is still on his rookie contract. San Francisco can trade for him and get him for this year, and then they can decide what to do with the final year of his deal next offseason.
Mitchell can learn behind Evans, and then eventually the 49ers could have Mitchell and De’Zhaun Stribling as their future core at wide receiver. So, he not only solves a need right now; he has potential to help down the line.
Mitchell is much less talked about, but could be a great fit.  The deadline is November 10.

title: 49ers Receive Sobering Injury Update on Mike Evans
full_text:
Don't expect to see Mike Evans on the field any time soon.
He hasn't played since he hobbled off the field at Levi's Stadium with an Achilles injury on Oct. 19. He won't play today when the 49ers face the Las Vegas Raiders at home. And he's "questionable at best" to play next week when the 49ers face the Dallas Cowboys on the road, according to Mike Garafolo.
"He's dealing with some tendinitis," Garafolo said . "We know how painful that can be...He is improving. He is working his way back. But Christian McCaffrey dealt with this a couple years ago, so the 49ers know how painful and debilitating it can be."
It's interesting that Garafolo compared Mike Evans' injury to the tendinitis McCaffrey suffered two seasons ago. Granted, McCaffrey had bilateral Achilles tendinitis, meaning he had it in both legs. Evans has it in just one.
Still, Evans is 33. McCaffrey was 28 in 2024, and he missed the first eight games of the season, then he had a Week 9 bye week to help him get ready for his Week 10 season debut. That's how long it took him to get ready to play. He even had to fly to Germany to receive treatment that isn't available in the United States. And when he came back, he lasted only four games before he suffered a season-ending injury in his knee, which might have been a compensation injury that was related to his Achilles.
If the 49ers learned their lesson with McCaffrey, they should let Evans take as long as he needs to recover completely before letting him play again. If that means sitting him until Week 14 or 15 or later, so be it.
Because if he returns too soon and goes down again, the 49ers won't win the Super Bowl. But if he's 100 percent healthy when the playoffs start, they absolutely could win it all. He's that important.
Which means the next couple weeks or couple months could depend on Kyle Shanahan's ability to trust his young players on offense. We know he prefers playing guys in their 30s. We know he has no patience for young players when they make the smallest mistakes.
He has to find some patience. He has two terrific young weapons in Jordan Watkins and Kaelon Black. Use them. If Shanahan had trusted them and used them more two weeks ago, they would have beaten the Falcons. Instead, Shanahan overused McCaffrey on the first drive and he got injured. Then Shanahan kept calling plays for Christian Kirk and Brandon Cooks, both of whom are washed.
Now, the 49ers are coming off a bye week. Shanahan has had plenty of time to figure out how to move the ball and score points without Evans.
Let's see what Shanahan cooked up.

title: What 49ers DE Nick Bosa Needs to Show When He Returns on Sunday
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa will have plenty of eyes on him upon his return.
And understandably so. After signing a then-record-breaking contract in 2023, hearing that Bosa has featured in just 19 of a possible 41 games since 2024 would naturally raise questions about the value of that investment.
He played all of 2023 (17 games) on the back of his 2022 Defensive Player of the Year campaign. He made 10.5 sacks, 53 combined tackles and 16 tackles for loss.
From 2024 onwards, across two and a half seasons, he's played 19 games, recorded 11 sacks and 76 combined tackles.
That's a staggering drop-off in availability.
It has to be said, but there must already be conversations from the 49ers' front office about his future in San Francisco.
When he's healthy, Bosa is a capable producer and though he has declined since his 2021 and 2022 seasons, where he recorded 15.5 and 18.5 sacks, respectively, his availability is the biggest concern.
Bosa has now played just five games since the start of the 2025 season, and his long-term future in San Francisco should be under threat.
At some point, the 49ers must consider whether to trade him or move on before his contract expires after the 2028 season. His talent is undeniable, but availability is becoming a significant concern, particularly given the financial investment involved.
If not, when he's back from the left calf injury he suffered before Week 3, at least he still has the opportunity to prove he can return to the level that made him one of the NFL's best pass rushers.
There are obstacles standing in his way. Staying healthy is one, while rediscovering the form that made him one of the league's best pass rushers is another. However, once he returns, the remainder of the season presents several games where he can overcome both challenges.
With his practice window now open , Bosa has at least taken the first step towards returning to action. However, there is a scenario in which the 49ers move forward without him in the coming years.
If there is no reduction in salary in a theoretical new deal, the salary-cap space freed up by his eventual departure, particularly if they move on when his contract expires, could provide significant flexibility to invest elsewhere.
With all eyes on him for the rest of the season, this is his time to shine.
